title: Shemonah Kevatzim
text:
The Spiritual Images That Exist in the Aspirations of the Nation’s Soul
Each of us lives in concert with the spiritual images that exist in the aspiration of our nation’s soul.

These images are sparks of light. We are connected—with the connection of the soul of life, the connection of all of our being—to every place where these images are hidden: whether that is a literal place (a site on earth), or whether that “place” consists of people’s actions at whose core these images are hidden, or whether that “place” consists of people’s thoughts and ideas, of whatever sort they may be.

We Must Sustain the Richness of Our Lives
A person who comes to slash the branches of these images, to diminish their power, their honor, and their importance to us diminishes the richness of our lives, and we must rise against him with all our might.

The Power of Our Lives
In the totality of the written and oral Torah and the interweaving of all of its particulars is hidden the most elevated and originary spiritual image of the desire of our nation from the aspect of the goal of its highest life-force. That image glows due to the totality of its comprehension and breadth, its thoughts, the ways that it expresses itself, and the outcomes of its perspectives on existence, Godliness, the world, humanity, the individual, society, good and evil, life and death.

The more that Torah understanding and awareness manifest themselves in our nation, the more is our nation’s soul well-founded, and then the more that soul’s power of life rises and grows splendidly strong.

The Harmony Within Practical Judaism
And our actions are the physical basis, the tangible element, in which this grand theory, this glowing image, places its treasures. And the more the value of our theoretical understanding grows, the more the light hidden in all of our actions shines in the midst of the entire nation.
And then the power of the trait of beautiful harmony within practical Judaism for the sake of God is revealed.

We Will Not Abandon the Banner
Sometimes people’s lives stumble in their courses and lack the strength to proceed bolstered by spiritual images, since their spirits are too weary to crystallize these images into deed.
Confusion is engendered, and people’s viewpoints are torn asunder.

Those of us who have a hardy spirit say: Life is susceptible to illness, but it is also susceptible to a return to complete health, and “whatever is joined to life is secure” (Ecclesiastes 9:4). Therefore, we will not abandon the banner, the precious ideals that are hidden within deeds. Those ideals will necessarily come to light precisely when they will be crystallized into deed. Those deeds are not yet completed, they have not yet reached their goal, a time when it will be possible to say that they have completed their work. They must yet illuminate all the darkness of life, a darkness that is still great and extremely vast.

But we will not abandon the banner. We will carry and bear it. With actual deeds, we will give form to the great thought of the spirit of Israel—as our nation has begun doing since it has begun to see its life as that of a collective whole.
Even though the burden is heavier now than it was before, bearing the yoke for the sake of this goal is worthwhile.

We have left the circle of other nations, children with capricious minds who tire of taking serious actions that do not bring immediate gratification. We have matured with knowledge and a fullness of personal feeling, so that we know how to live and how to bear the yoke of life with a calm heart and mighty will for the sake of a worthy goal. Although that goal is still hidden, it will ultimately be revealed.

Our Aspiration and Our Action
We aspire to attain the supernal goal and, at the same time, hold onto the practical foundation. But if we lack the strength, if the nation stumbles so that over the course of time the burden of the practical—which is waiting to receive its full power when the ideal light will be revealed in it and through it—grows too heavy, then we will seek proper solutions in keeping with the spirit of the nation’s soul and in keeping with the way of the Torah in its entirety, in order to ease the weight so that this necessary alleviation will not even for a moment cause any lack of the spiritual form of the actions that express the nation’s aspiration.

When We Do Injury to Concepts
When we do injury to our concepts, when—as a result of our immersion in the smallness of routine life—we grow distant from the height of supernal thoughts that generate great deeds, thoughts in which powerful Godliness is hidden, then we do injury to our deeds.
Their level sinks and their glory dims until they manifest themselves in an irate form that leads to rupture and desolation instead of the might and glory that are their natural garment.

And when our deeds are injured, our concepts grow distant, becoming a sort of weak thought that arouses the disdain of every man of action, because that thought is so far from life and has so little ability to affect life.

Our Return to the Soaring Idea
To find a remedy for this terrible situation, for such a disease that consumes life’s “both extremities, with the insides charred” (cf. Ezekiel 15:4), we must strive as much as possible to guard our deeds, to cherish them and reinforce them to the extent that we can.
But we must not be satisfied with that. We will not gain anything in our efforts if we do not link the elevation of our deeds to our return to the soaring concepts stored and hidden in them.

If actions remain “the commandment of men learned by rote” (Isaiah 29:13), not only are they unhelpful, but they will diminish the concepts even more, and in the end, the diminishment of the concepts will conclude with the person abjuring his deeds with disgust.

We Will Not at All Be Disconcerted
We will not at all be disconcerted by those who intimidate us against flights of thought, by those who say that we are brazen to rise to the heights of heaven without a ladder.

That is not so. We have a ladder “set on the ground, whose top reaches heaven” (Genesis 28:12): the light in our souls, in the soul of all the people and the soul of the individual, that will be awakened thoroughly by the light of the secrets of the Torah.

They Are Really Saying the Same Thing
Regarding matters of concepts and beliefs, which are matters founded on spiritual, abstract matters, it is a more common occurrence than in any other dispute that two disputants who, viewed externally, are very far from each other, are both really saying the same thing. And the entire essence of the dispute, which sometimes appears to flame up to the heart of heaven, is only a dispute of language, because neither person understands the other’s language.

The Self-Same Idea
Regarding the basis of beliefs, everything depends on the quality of the blending of a person’s thought: how its parts depend on each other. In this, there is a great difference between one person and another—and, even more, between one generation and another.

Sometimes, as a result of some thought based on a concept, one person is the recipient of a complete structure of ethics and holy feelings, and it doesn’t at all touch his spiritual structure in which his soul lives.
And sometimes, the self-same idea causes one person to sink and descend, and another person to rise and ascend.

Improving One’s Concepts
The wise person improves his concepts so that they will be properly organized.

Regarding spiritual concepts that fill a person’s spirit, to the degree that his thoughts are illuminated, their general form is correct and close to the truth and to the attribute that elevates the spirit.

Faith with Intellect
Maimonides was happy when, in his teachings, the form of God’s providence took on the character of a construct in which it correlates to a person’s sapience.

And it is fitting to be happy about this, because as long as this faith, which provides the basis for life in the world, exists without an intellectual framework, it does not blend with all of the waves of life of the spirit of wisdom, which yearns to comprehend.

But after faith receives its intellectual form, it is rooted in the depths of the soul in all of its chambers and depths, and a person finds himself content, as his spiritual form coalesces into a single unit.

Obliterating Forms of Ordinary Artlessness and Piety
From the hidden depths of the soul, let us take the light that will revive the entire nation and set it on its feet.
The power of life grows stronger, it blazes its pathways. But we must study the content of its spirit.

The yearning for a supernal, holy spirit—a holy spirit that emulates the spirit of the men of might girded with the power of God, whom we had in earlier days when the nation knew itself—is increasing.
As that yearning shines forth, it breaches fences, it obliterates forms of ordinary simplicity and piety. Apparently the situation is terrible, bare on all sides.

But all of that is merely a transition. We must immediately approach the supernal brilliance of the light of life that pours forth from its elevated source, exalted from the beginning, which will make an imprint with its power of a new and sturdy form, better and more filled with the holy might than anything that a middling simplicity and a stumbling piety can provide.

Healthy Souls
The ideals at Israel’s source are being increasingly revealed. With the essence of their thundering power, they give life to the spirit prepared to receive them. And they demand the attainment of their role: which is that vessels will be prepared for them, many vessels—these being healthy souls of a fresh generation that lives upon its land and is girded with the might of the salvation of God’s right hand.

What Our Soul Demands of Us
The Sanctuary, prophecy, and sovereignty, with all of their methods, send their beam to us, their light that is sown (cf. Psalms 97:11) in the land of life.
Rays come from them to us (cf. Habakkuk 3:4). Waves of their lights beat upon our eyelids, which have been closed throughout the entire course of time of the exile, which dissolves everything.
We are summoned to prepare ourselves for the light, to know ourselves and our purpose, to know what our soul, with all of its sturdiness, demands of us.

On Our Historic Soil
The great and elevated spirit that yearns for the very greatest things—it, and it alone, comprehends life and humanity in its splendor and its might.

The only thing that parallels the might of a complete life—one that fills bodies that are pervaded with healthy blood and tremendous power, enormous energy and an immense joy of life—is the might of the spirit in its supernal vigor, shining and rising over humanity with the power of the strength of Israel, a strength that grows ever more apparent in our lives as they are now bursting forth in a current that bends toward the revival of the nation on its historic soil.

For the Sake of a Meaningful Life
Without a purpose to a person’s power of life, his spirit melts away. Its strength diminishes and collapses, it is worn away and strides toward disintegration, which lies directly before it on a downward incline.

But the power of life that is crowned by the entire people, by the community of the nation, appears with its proper goal directly before it in our lives—in the care of our lives. And for the sake of that we live, exist, battle, and prevail.

Spiritual Immaturity and Illusions
Illusion comes as the result of a person’s propensity to engage in exalted inquiry when that propensity bursts forth before its time, before it has been properly prepared—that is to say, before it has sufficiently learned specific practical teachings, which must always precede exploration into the supernal and the elevated.

This person’s propensity has not provided the basis of its full moral stance that will suffice for the presence of an exalted spirituality capable of aligning itself with an inquiry filled with light and spiritual strength—such as inquiry into the Divine in its sublime form.

That is why we always find that, following a person’s tendency to being inspired to seek the exalted, illusion comes: an illusory faith or an illusory heresy. And that is all due to students who have not served their full apprenticeship, who have risen to the heights of exploration without having first prepared themselves.

Closeness to God
It is a great spiritual endeavor for a person to develop himself so much that in his inner being he will recognize God’s closeness to him.
When this all-inclusive propensity will be thoroughly awakened, all of the affairs in his life will straighten out.

For a person to attain this, it makes no difference how these feelings of closeness to God come to him—whether through his intellect and rational awareness or in the way of inner feeling—as long as he recognizes within himself the might and truth of that closeness.
All of the Torah’s commandments and prayers are the best preparations to broaden a person’s propensity toward closeness to God and to broaden its steps in the depths of his spirit.

Therefore, the value of every prayer recited with intent, every blessing and praise of God, every mitzvah and every good custom is very great and exalted, because they are the means via which a person lays a solid foundation for feeling close to God in his heart.
How wretched are those people who do not know Hashem, who do not pray and who do not perform the commandments together with the entire congregation, the community of Israel.

The soul’s aptitude for demanding closeness to God seeks to fulfill its function in those people as well. But since they do not fulfill their obligation to themselves, they remain wretched, dry of all dew of purity. Even if they bring the moisture of good deeds to fulfill the natural moral thirst in their character, the fulfillment of that need cannot satisfy what they lack in terms of the need that demands closeness to God. That can be fulfilled only by performing Godly deeds that are dedicated to the name of Hashem, with holy prayer and with the performance Hashem’s commandment and directives.

With the pity that we must have on all mankind, and in particular on our children and those close to us in race and spirit, we are inspired to straighten before them the straight road that leads to closeness to God. That closeness is acquired by means of the Torah: by learning it and keeping it.

And the more we attain this elevated goal, [i.e.,] the greater the increase of good and pure deeds that by their nature lead to implanting closeness to God into the power of life, the more will happiness increase in the world.

The Power of Faith
The power of faith of heeding well and receiving that which has been transmitted—exists in us so that we may develop as a nation and as individuals.

This ability stands ready to fulfill that which is lacking: that is to say, to bring into a person’s spiritual treasury illuminations that are intrinsically higher than he is, so much so that he cannot gain benefit from their light.

People whose intellect is weak, who recognize their meager spiritual ability that makes them unable to judge matters satisfactorily, are graced with a power of faith that is more elevated than that of people with strong minds, who are cognizant of their strength to know and discern, to distinguish among exalted matters.

But on the other hand, when these latter people who are wise of heart come via their intellect to a place where, in truth, an exalted power that their understanding cannot attain lies, they bring the power of faith from its concealment. And in that, they stand on a level that is not inferior—from the aspect of the natural character of the human being—to that of all of the masses of the nation in whom natural faithfulness is guarded in its purity.

True Life
Faith in life is found among the common people more than it is found among those who are developed, people of understanding. But that faith is illusory.

As for intellectually gifted people whose spiritual strength rises above the common avenues, they can by no means establish in their hearts faith in physical life. Instead, they are filled with the light and strength of a superior faith in a life of truth.
However, in order to be well-grounded, they must overcome all of the obstacles of physical life with the strong spirit that may be found among the wise who have attained freedom.

Then they shine like the brilliance of the firmament. Above all the clouds of illusion, the charitable sun of knowledge and wisdom—the inside of which is swathed with fine graciousness and serenity of the soul—shines for them.

A Separate Knowledge
Each of the different ways of understanding what the knowledge of God is has its place in the strata of life. The character of each person’s spirit is unique. In keeping with its aptitude, it is drawn to a particular path of understanding.

No individual can completely understand someone else’s psyche regarding the knowledge of God deep within him. External similarity that results from similar speech, similar ways of self-expression, and a similar way of life—that only touches upon the outer area of this knowledge. But in its interiority, in every human being this knowledge is always separate, with its own form.

Individuality and Affinity
We must always proceed on the path between individuality and affinity with others, and develop our views in such a way that every person will be able to find his unique spirit in them. At the same time, we must integrate ourselves into the temperament of affinity, which encompasses everything in one unit.

In a Time of Breakdown and Renewal
At a time of the nation’s breakdown—which is, simultaneously, a time of reconstitution and revival—we must engage in great spiritual work: the work of clarifying and refining our feelings and concepts—in particular, the work of clarifying our aesthetic sense: constraining the power of the imagination in order to strengthen it upon reliable foundations so that it will be useful and strong, and to expunging it where it breaks through its border and proceeds on an unpaved way.

Spiritual Streams
The root of all of the different spiritual streams in the expanse of the human world is in the Congregation of Israel, because it—in the spiritual sense unique to the yearnings of its people’s spirit, which rises to the heights of pure gladness—is the center of humanity.

Because of that, we absolutely cannot ignore any stream when we come to delineate the spiritual strength of the Congregation of Israel, the “bride” (kallah) who “is composed (kelulah) of all colors” (Zohar 3:96b).

Roots and Branches
But as we contemplate and study these matters, we must do so with a broad heart, a clear mind, and a fearless spirit capable of developing in a person who knows his purpose with a clear awareness.

Together with the study of these points of view, we must equip ourselves with the best and highest ethical aspirations so that we will have a worthy personal basis on which to build our elevated aspirations—aspirations in which the established concepts of the people (concepts that are planted like powerful cedars with roots of faith and the branches of the Torah and the commandments) are rooted.

Psychology
The psychology of the individual—as well as the overall psychology of nation and mankind—provides an important prologue to the ways of explaining the paths of the Torah and serving God.

In particular, we must enter into the depths of this wisdom of the soul in order to explain the content of the thoughts that affect us—thoughts that come as a result of our actions and our words, and via which we begin to understand the intent of the commandments and prayer, the great value of our moral education, and the rectification of the entire world.

Light Sown Within Us
Everything we say regarding elevated spiritual matters—in particular, matters of Divinity—is connected more to the status of matters in our personal state of being than it relates to the external world. But there is a certain level of connection between the status of our personal state—its being, its reality, and the ways in which it acts—and the outer world and all existence.
And that existence is deep within us—perhaps even more than it is outside of us. When we rise, all of existence rises, and when existence rises, we too rise.

Mundane life encloses us in a narrow circle of our limited senses until we cannot know our own might and greatness. And sometimes, in order to recognize some aspects of existence, a person must turn a blind eye to his own transcendence and greatness. The “light that is sown” (cf. Psalms 97:11) blurs many worthy individual lines for us.

But although it is true that we benefit from the light of those with dimmed eyes who recognize the individual lines more than we do, we will not be like them, but we will strive constantly to soar in the fullness of the light.

A Mistake in Comprehending Divine Matters
Although a mistake in comprehending Divine matters causes much damage, the essence of the damage that results from distorted concepts is not actualized to the point of killing a person’s soul—unless it coalesces into actions, or at least descends to form viewpoints and feelings that in the end will necessarily grow manifest in actions.
But as long as the mistake remains in its intangible form, there is no absolute uprooting.

Some Room for Error
In saying this, we are close to the view of the Ravad, who criticized Maimonides for calling a person who believes in the corporeality of Divinity a heretic.

And we can agree that, as long as this person who corporealizes Divinity does not make a statue or image and thus has not consummated his thought so that it still remains in the realm of spirit, this cannot be classed as uprooting and abandoning our religion.

The Errors of the Christian and Moslem Faiths
Regarding the faiths that move away from the whole of the Torah, such as the Christian and Moslem faiths, the essence of their toxicity does not lie in their concept of Divinity—which differs from that which is correct according to the foundation of the light of the Torah—but in the fact that they result the destruction of the practical commandments and the eradication of the hope of the nation of Israel to attain its complete revival.

Prayer and Intellect
A person’s best inclinations are all hidden and concealed in the core of his spirit.
But they must be actualized. And the best action to accomplish that is speaking, which affects his thought and imagination.

Thus, prayer is of preeminent importance, because it actualizes the highest feelings of the heart. Prayer’s form parallels the feelings of the heart, whose way of perception is different from that of logic.

When the spirit of the individual and of the nation is healthy, it has a fine awareness of its strength, and it is not at all afraid of logical contradictions, because it knows that the ways in which logic and soulful feeling express themselves differ.
Then prayer flowers. It rises of itself like a flame, without any foreign thoughts and sadness of the spirit.
But when the nation is impoverished and the power of national feeling is diminished, only logic remains in place and that, despite all of its deficiency, is what supports a person’s feeling.

Since the soul’s feeling is so weak that it must be supported at the table of another and it does not gain sustenance from within itself, contradictions appear, and a battle arises at every time of prayer, as a person’s thoughts grow ever more chaotic. Thus, his prayer loses its great value of reviving his soul at its core. His intent weakens, and all that remains is that which is “learned by rote” (Isaiah 29:13).

His prayer does not nourish his feeling well, just as his feeling does not nourish his feeling well. Therefore, his prayer wanders to the tents of intellect and calculation. And when intellect places its cold hands on warm prayer, which is the recipient of heavenly fire, it destroys prayer’s power, and it diminishes as well its own clear and cold light, and both grow deficient.

Clinging to the National Foundation of Israel
A person can only truly cling to Israel’s national foundation if his soul has been purified through repentance from disgraceful human sins and base traits, or if his spirit from the start has been a pure spirit.

That is because the true foundation of the character of the nation of Israel is the aspiration for supernal righteousness: the righteousness of Hashem in the world. If a person has been polluted by some sin, then—corresponding to the extent of his pollution—the desire for righteousness and goodness does not shine in him properly. Therefore, he is not truly connected with the national character until he purifies himself.

Above the Limitations of Ordinary Reasoning
When a person rises above the limitations of rationalistic thought, the level of goodness expands until it arouses a measure of a great flame in the entire stature of his soul.

When a person recognizes the spiritual oneness of existence with an inner, supernal awareness, that oneness draws his spirit to goodness, to good deeds and to lovely feelings that have a cosmic intrinsic pleasantness.

Faith expands within his inner being. And his sense of all goodness—which he increases when he engages in good deeds and in good thoughts and words, sweetening all of existence—encourages him and sweeps him up to the heavens.

He knows, as an abundance of holy inspiration flows onto his soul, that whenever he elevates himself—by means of good deeds or by means of a supernal inspiration to yearn for Divinity, wisdom, justice, beauty, and uprightness—he improves the spiritual character of all existence.

All people become improved in the hiddenness of their heart as a result of the supernal improvement of one of them. And the grief of a number of people sad in spirit is softened and is diluted by the droplets of that softening, when one soul experiences the strong arousal of a Godly consolation.
Even predatory animals and all harmful creatures are softened. Their venom is somewhat lessened as a result of the general propensity of this soul that takes delight in Hashem.

The best human beings grow in their goodness, and the joy they take in goodness and in uprightness grows. And all of the supernal worlds, the supernal angels, are aroused with a sweet, holy melody. They rise with a beautiful, gracious song, and the might of the supernal host grows more splendid.
All of these thoughts that expand the power of the spirit only have their place in a soul that is free—with an absolute freedom—from the shackles of the rational, which binds ideas and kills song.

Natural Self-Preservation and an Awakening Mind
Every living being on the face of the earth and in the entire fullness of Creation, wherever living beings exist, is subject to the law of the propensity for self-preservation.
This law must exist in nature. But it grows weak when an analytical mind develops, a mind that assesses the value of existence not with natural appraisal but with rational evaluation.
As soon as a mind awakens even slightly, even if it cannot yet evaluate and cannot strongly indicate what the path of life is, that natural propensity immediately weakens.

This law of self-preservation is for the good and for betterment, because it compels the mind to hold firm and to be helped by the natural propensity of the desire for self-preservation, which is not completely foreign to it.
We have seen this regarding the existence of faith: in the world, and especially among the people of Israel.

Religion was safeguarded for the entire Jewish nation, and faith was well-preserved among humanity because of the power of this natural propensity. Societal life and a firm nationality could exist only as a result of the power of the existence of faith.

But as life improved and mind and moral awareness developed, this natural propensity weakened. And now religion and faith no longer exist in keeping with that natural propensity but in keeping with an evaluation that results from the awareness of the goodness and truth of religion and faith.
This awareness has not yet matured, because spiritual development has not yet reached that level. But the beginning of the illumination has succeeded in weakening this natural propensity.
And since ultimately a permanent and full steadiness can exist only with the light of faith, which is more elevated than every type of human darkness, awareness must rise until it reaches its goal.
“And the faith of your time will be a refuge, salvation that comes as a result of wisdom and knowledge” (Isaiah 33:6).

The Elevation of the Soul
The elevation of a person’s soul must drive away his lowly traits.
The delight of the light of knowledge raises a person from the depths of an enslavement to delusion, something to which he is always connected.
Clear knowledge can be established only when the dross of a fearful heart, flattery and self-deception are removed from a person’s inner being.

Redemption and Revival
Essentially, Judaism in exile has no practical basis. It is only a vision in the heart based on images of hope and on precious ideas about the future and the past.

There is a limit to how much strength the vision of the heart possesses to bear the burden of life and, with that strength, to forge a path for the nation’s life. And the limit, it seems, has been reached.
As a result, Judaism descends; it plunges into exile. Its only hope is to be planted in the source of life that is within tangible life.
Even one spark of tangible life will enliven a great and broad quantity of visionary life.
And the tangible life of Judaism is revealed only with the return of the nation to its land. That is the paved road to the return to life.

Everything elevated in the nation’s spirit and in the vision of its heart will rise and live in keeping with the measure to which the foundation of action will participate in reviving the languishing vision.

A Natural and an Exalted Spirit
The more the world improves and man’s spirit within him develops, the more the demand to live in keeping with that natural spirit within him is awakened, and with a stronger voice.
That demand possesses a great deal of truth and justice. People with a perfected awareness must refine it and establish it firmly.

A person finds God inside himself, in his proper inclinations. And even regarding those inclinations that initially appear to stray from the good path accepted by a normative outlook, he can raise them so high that he will know how to establish everything in a program of might and happiness.

The Revival of the Congregation of Israel
When the Congregation of Israel is aroused to reach for its revival, it finds its might and honor within herself. All of the purity and holiness that are typically found in subjugation and compliance now shine in the soul-filled might of the manifestation of the nation’s power.
Then, with a pure awareness, we bind new and old souls together.

Protecting Historical Judaism
Protecting historical, traditional Judaism—Judaism as it expresses itself in deeds—is one of the greatest obligations of every concerned person who has any ability to act in accordance with his spirit.

The abandonment of traditional Jewish actions because of a weak spirit, the refraining from participating in the ways of life of the entire nation throughout its generations—in regard to maintaining the holiness of the Sabbaths and holidays, in regard to the details of avoiding forbidden foods, in regard to gathering in the synagogues and study halls—gradually diminishes the character of the nation and weakens its cohesion.

If these actions can be maintained only as a result of explanation and exposition of the concepts that preserve them, then promulgating the acquisition of those concepts is obligatory, equal to promulgating the acquisition of the actions themselves.

The Torah and the Spirit of Israel
The Torah is integrated with the spirit of Israel.
The unalloyed spirit of Israel contains everything: the light of God, the purpose of existence, the source of souls.

When the Torah grows strong, when its knowledge spreads, when its light radiates, when its feelings grow deep within every soul, then Divine light spreads throughout the world, grows magnificent, and is elevated. And the entire world rises, linked to the elevation of those elite few who possess an exalted spirit.

Thinking and Feelings
Unsullied thinkers reach their greatness due to the breadth of their thought. But they must elevate their feelings as well.
When they sink into the depths of darkness, they must call out vigorously. They must wake up and tell themselves to emerge from the gloom to the light. Then their hearts will cry out to Hashem.

Strength
Strength—physical vigor—must exist in the righteous people who have upright hearts so that the phenomenon of the impulse for good will impel its influence on the world.
Any weakening of the righteous, who must be girded with might, weakens the light of the world.

Fulfilling a Spiritual Lack
Sometimes we fulfill a spiritual lack not by engaging in any Divine service or repentance but by increasing our bodily strength.

A Spiritual Barrier
When a person proceeds on the path of pure contemplation of Divinity, he senses within himself a barrier separating him from clear realizations. And his soul itself recognizes that this barrier consists of his wrong actions and traits.
A yearning then awakens immediately in his heart for complete repentance. And that yearning is itself the finest repentance.
Frequently, that repentance does not grow properly active until it is attached to fresh prayer.
Then the wellspring of might once again pours onto this person’s soul.

Thought in Matters of Divinity
Thought in matters of Divinity affects positively all of a person’s traits. That occurs when the thought is pure—that is to say, when it is mature, with an inner yearning to recognize the truth and with a desire for justice and honesty, without any coarse ulterior motives.

Not only does it positively affect the particular traits of this individual, but it refines and purifies all existence—because this individual who is sincerely seeking God, who is constantly rising, is a component of existence.

Love for All Creatures
The more the search for Hashem gains strength in a person’s heart, the more his love for all creatures expands. He loves even the wicked and the heretics, and he desires their repair—and indeed, he truly repairs them with his great faith.

However, on a revealed level, a person only has the strength to exhibit love to those in whom he can find something good, because then he can attach his love to the aspect of good; and the evil, ugly side of people whom he loves from the aspect of his good trait of loving people, which includes being good and doing good for both the evil and the good, will not harm him at all.

The Faculty of Imagination
In praying and in performing mitzvot, we build the faculty of imagination so that it becomes pure and strong, and fit to be the basis of our active intelligence.

The Image of Divinity
The image of Divinity that a person visualizes is always alloyed by the dross of deceitful illusions. Consequently, that image undermines the life of the individual and of society. All evil counsel regarding the ways of life and all evil traits result from that.

That is a disease from which a person is rescued only when he accustoms his mind to involve itself with the paths of a good life and the ways of wisdom and morality. Then his concept of God will be the foundation of all his aspirations, but without any particularistic form.
Then he will always be filled with clear thoughts, and his spiritual strength will constantly grow, rising from level to level.

Excess
When a yearning for justice and a moral disposition greatly increase in a person’s heart, it may become a sort of disease that destroys extensive goodness as it drills constantly into the core of his feelings, finding blemishes in his moral behavior and threatening him excessively—until it stands as a barrier detaching him from the light of Hashem that shines in the joy of his spirit.

Sins and Unpurified Character Traits
A person’s sins and unpurified character traits dull his heart until, when his spirit is darkened, his objective sight cannot by any means broaden and expand.

A contemplative person who wants to rise to the heights of awareness will sense this intuitively, and he will sense the absolute necessity to repent completely so that his awareness will not be impaired.
Regarding all of his transgressions between himself and God, his spiritual repentance will immediately restore the gladness of the emancipation granted by the light of the spirit.
But regarding sins between himself and others, a person’s spirit cannot be whole until it is rectified, which occurs as a result of his engaging in proper action.

However, sometimes a person encounters stumbling blocks and barriers that he cannot overcome. And as long as his sins are not rectified, they withhold the light of knowledge and prevent him from recognizing God’s universal justice, and they prevent him from yearning for this justice to emerge from its concealment.

Nevertheless, when he makes a strong resolution to take care at least from now on not to sin against others and to strive to rectify the past, then, corresponding to the degree to which he repents in action, spiritual light will shine onto his soul until the striving of his spirit will itself increase the pathways that lead him to complete his practical repentance, so that the spiritual light will be able to rest in all of its fullness and all of its goodness on his soul thirsting for that light.

Yearning
A person’s yearning for spiritual clarity and for an expanse of supernal images itself arouses his preparation for the infusion of Divine inspiration.

When a Person Empowers His Mind Over His Spirit
When a person empowers his mind over his spirit, and the way that he conducts himself is not in accord with the way that simple nature would determine but in accordance with his mindful judgment, he embosses a portion of all existence with the stamp of that judgment, so that its most shining aspect reveals its light and governance. And so the world improves to the degree that this person is involved in it.

If he rises so high that—because of his spirit’s vast yearning for mindfulness and uprightness—his natural decision-making accords with his mindfulness, then the hidden light shines in the essence of existence, until many of its components that are ugly and lowly are transformed and become radiant and uplifted.

Delighting the Heart
The concept that all existence is solely a matter of Divinity and that there is absolutely nothing but Hashem delights the heart exceedingly.
This spiritual delight that this concept brings about is truly a proof expressing that.

Fearing Thought
A person’s sin causes him to be afraid of thinking, and so he doesn’t delve into exalted concepts at length.

However, the more a person removes himself from sin, the more his fear of thinking will diminish, until with his visualizations he will be able to rise to infinite vistas and matters that stand at the pinnacle of the world with his visualizations.

Complacency
Complacency—i.e., a person’s contentment with his concepts of Divinity marked by deceitful delusions embedded in his heart since childhood, the days when he lacked awareness—is due to his ardor for animalistic pleasures.

The Rarefication of the Soul
Deep immersion in Divine knowing that results from full knowledge clothed in the pleasant feeling and radiant garment of rarified imagination possesses a beauty and delight that cannot be surmised.

All seers of visions and all singers of delightful love would grow weary describing even a small portion of the soul’s satiety and its Edenic currents when it is in its exalted state as it stands entirely in its Divine world.

In addition to this endless elevated delight, which is a spiritual form that the soul wears as a result of being in this elevated state, the soul is filled with royal splendor and the entire grandeur of good traits, until it is scented by the Edenic fragrances of the most lucid and enlightened ethics in a whole and radiant form that has no equal in the entire imprint of the this-worldly ethics that comes through any learning or any other perception.

The rarefication of the soul in its supernal, Edenic state penetrates so deeply into the soul’s strength and the roots of its being that the soul with its might then rarifies everything that surrounds it and touches it—that surrounds and touches the soul’s essence and reality.

And when the soul shines and is made Edenic by Hashem, and the delight of recognizing Divinity and the joy of that recognition existing on earth, then every human soul, every animal soul, every bush and plant, and the entire power of life concealed in every element and inanimate object draws forth Edenic being and elevation.

This clear outlook, which is ultimately attained by means of Divine inspiration, which is prepared to appear in the nation of Israel and through it in the entire world, is even at present the chief source of all delights.

Imagination and the Mind
When a person’s mind acts upon his imagination, it clothes itself in a particular form.
That form is a holiness that form perfumes the world and purifies a person of his every uncleanness.

But when that form grows blurred and a person’s imagination is instead given form in accordance with its own character and without the mind’s influence upon it, then that imagination is the most tawdry source of every blunder, every transgression and sin in the life of the individual and in the life of the community.

The form of the imagination maintains its essential purity in accordance with the direct influence of the mind on those people who inherently possess the power to live a spiritual life in the light of the mind.

But that form can also improve and be built honorably when the proper ways of life and form of feelings that great people attain, as a result of the aspect of the influence of their mind, exercise an effect on average and small people, in keeping with the general influence of great people upon the small.
These deeds and images will direct the power of life—a power that attaches itself to imaginative forms—to the desired goal.

The Complete Mind
Indeed, a person’s intellect in its fullness, which is capable of directing the steps of his imagination on the path of life, is Godly intellect. From it comes the manifestation of prophecy with the revelation of the Torah and the light of Divine inspiration.

The drawing forth of the ways of wisdom onto all those who seek Hashem, all of the characteristics in a person that are affected by that influence, and a form of life in accordance with it—these elevate the imagination from its lowliness and illuminate it with the light of the intellect, granting a person happiness.

Serene People and Changeable People
There are some people whom God has made upright, whose character is calm, and whose unwavering way of life follows straightforward guidance and is marked by inner serenity. Yes, if they toil in Torah, in learning ethics and wisdom, they will rise to great levels. But at any rate, they are upright people, good and honest. These people must engage in practical employments or practical professions. Their moral aspect stands on its own, in its place, with its serenity. Possibly, it will not rise to an exalted height, but neither will it descend to a low level.

But there is another type: people who are not at ease, who are always on the edge, either rising to the heights of heaven or descending to the depths of the abyss. They must rectify their spiritual being every day. Those who find the path they need will rise higher and higher. But if they abandon it, they are liable to descend lower and lower. These people must constantly engage in Torah and service of God, learn ethical teachings and develop holy feelings. Heaven forbid that they turn aside to the way of this world and practical professions.

In the course of the generations in general, the general character of some generations is of the first type, of those with a tranquil disposition and a steady character. Their education should be like that of these individuals with a steady character.
And there are also generations of a changeable character, whose spiritual sustenance must be constant, with an ongoing flow.
Sometimes we find that in some particular area a person or a generation has an aspect of tranquility, and in another area an aspect of changeability.
We require leaders who are concerned for the good of the whole, who will focus their minds on how to educate each part of the generation in itself.

Thoughts, Imagination, and Intelligence
All thoughts that are spoken and expressed in accordance with an imagination that leads to an improvement of ethics and feelings of holiness will exist always—even as the light of radiant intelligence shines on them. But they are renewed in a new form.

From a Life of Instinct to a Life of Awareness
The Congregation of Israel is presently at a turning point, as it emerges from a life of instinct to a life of awareness.
Natural instinct is more assured in its procession and more directed in its activity to maintain life.

But a human being’s perfected character will not allow him to remain forever enveloped in his natural state. Against his will, he rises from his enclosure and emerges to a level of awareness in which he loses much of his natural qualities—but in the end, he adapts them into a more beautiful form.

This applies to all living beings and humanity: as long as they remain in their natural state, nature acts to give them the wisdom to protect their lives and perpetuate their existence. And the more they begin to acquire civilization and awareness, the more must they engage in all of their activities with an inner, clear awareness, and not due to a strong and blind, inner compulsion.

That has been the state of our nation in exile in relation to Judaism, to appreciating faith, and to keeping the Torah. In a state of slumber, the instinct of national self-preservation impels each individual to keep the religion and honor faith overall out of an inner, natural awareness that if each individual were to separate himself in regard to religious life the feelings of the nation would cease to exist and the nation itself would burst apart and cease to exist.

All of this was very much the case before the light of the national renaissance began to shine—with desire and awareness, on a practical basis, with a strong attraction to gather together in the land of Israel and establish anew the national life that had existed in earlier days. Earlier, when the times were not suitable for that, neither from our standpoint nor from the standpoint of the world, and when a clear awareness regarding the desire for the on-going existence of the nation and the pathways of its renaissance could not be attained, if some weakness would have affected the natural influence, the danger would have been very terrible.
Now the turn of clear awareness has come.

When this will grow complete, great things will begin—much greater than all of the activities of natural, blind awareness—moving towards the existence of the Divine light, towards the knowledge of Hashem unique to Israel, towards faith and towards keeping the Torah, which constitutes the entirety of the paths of life for Israel.

But for the present, after the spark of a small beginning, this has caused the cessation and weakness of the instinct regarding religion and faith even as awareness has not completely fulfilled its role.

Therefore, we are desolated at the sight of the destruction. But we must not be desolate and in despair, nor must we sit with folded hands, doing nothing. Rather, we must know how to grasp the roots of the renewal of the spirit and cause its branches to produce fruit.
If we cannot immediately restore all of the losses, we must at least strive to restore what we can.

When breaches come about due to a spirit of coarseness, brutishness and dullness of the heart, if we depend on being healed by the renewal of the spirit and enhanced knowledge without turning to rectify our actions, that can lead to malfunction, to thinking that the spirit and thought are sufficient in themselves. Then we will not absorb these well, and the turmoil will increase.
This is not the case when the inner cause of all of the failures is an inner illumination that is leading towards a clear awareness—which, with its being revealed, has weakened the power of instinct.
In truth, if we leave the situation this way, matters will go from bad to worse.

But when we begin to illuminate the spirit and perfect our inner awareness more and more, hastening to reveal it, then it will itself begin to restore more clearly all that was lost to us as a result of the fall of the instinct, and our spiritual life will again acquire a form that gives light, and the hearts of the sons will begin to return to the fathers (cf. Malachi 3:24, and life will begin to be more filled with the dew of the renewal of holiness and the awareness, honor, and appreciation of faith.

The desire to keep the commandments, to perfect Israelite life, will return to us with all of the beauty of its splendor and glory, and it will unveil its activity for the good in the site where the honor of the house of Israel flourishes: in the beloved land, in the places of its renaissance—particularly, in the cities of Judah, which are slowly being restored.

A Boorish Attempt to Understand the Divine
A barrenness of thought that results from a minimal amount of learning and knowledge causes a person to think extensively about the nature of the Divine. And he cannot imagine how much this thought is a terrible insolence and an appalling folly.
The more a person is steeped in boorishness, the more he thinks that with this he approaches elevated Divine knowledge—something that, he has always heard, all great spirits in the world yearn for.

Over a number of generations, the habit of pondering this errant thought—as though it is possible to contemplate the character of the Divine—has accumulated, until many futile breaths have woven together, the outcomes of which are many terrible evils, leading to so much trouble and darkness that even the individual loses his material and spiritual strength.
That which comes to purify the air of the miasma of this insolence and wickedness is absolute heresy. That itself is no better than the former, but it opposes the former with an absolute antagonism.

The confrontation between these two opposites helps humanity tremendously in coming to know Hashem with a shining knowledge, a knowledge that brings a person close to his happiness, both temporal and eternal.

Then, instead of a person’s barren thought that he will burst through in an attempt to understand the Divine, a clear thought will enter his heart about pure ethics and supernal might, which will sketch his pathways of life. And with that thought, he will stand in the light of Hashem.

Two Ways of Thinking About Godliness
There are two aspects of thought regarding Godliness.

The first aspect is in a form that speaks about the Creator and Creation, each in and of itself. It is as though each is a separate topic, but these are joined together, because the Creator gives life to Creation and Creation receives life from the Creator.

The second aspect is that Creation does not exist at all, and that the name “Creation” is only figurative, from our perspective. We are creatures only in terms of the constricted nature of our comprehension, whereas in truth everything is the Creator, God. The all is something different, a different content that cannot be compared with partial revelation. God is the all, and not any part in and of itself as a part. Each aspect of this thought has its own effect on a person’s spirit.

Logic and calculation come from the aspect of thought that evaluates the world and Creation as two entities, whereas song and an uplifted spirit come from the second view: that of discovering the nothingness of the all besides God, and God’s glory filling all.
Ethics is a branch composed of logic and song blended properly together. Should it lack one power, it will be unable to endure.

Therefore, when, in accordance with the guidance of the first thought involving a division between thought about God and about the world, the conception of God’s righteousness, of the greatness of ethics that appears to us in relation to the thought about God, is revealed, and the rules of that ethics are filled with logic and calculation—when, after this, once His righteousness and the splendor of an ethics filled with one’s awareness of Him has already been well-established in the soul, the second thought about Godliness comes, then song gains strength as a result of the supernal, impassioned discernment that “There is no other than He” (Deuteronomy 4:35), and it too contributes the fruit of blessing to ethics.

But if, at the outset, thought would be marked only by its single aspect of “There is no other than He,” no ethical form that has a relationship with Godliness would be able to affect us. We cannot recognize a moral value regarding one entity in relation to itself—rather, only in a relationship of one entity to others.

This elevation of thought is higher than the entire vista of the level of all ethics, just as it is higher than all thoughts and boundaries. However, a person cannot grasp the entire glory of a thought higher than his own finite level—that is why the values of ethics must constantly, repeatedly, be aroused in all avenues of life—and so a terrible danger can spread due to the second thought overcoming the first.
But even if the first thought, whose wings are clipped, is intensified, then too a person’s spirit can sink, and as a result, he can lose many precious things.

Therefore, there is no other remedy than to arrange the mind in such a way that the first thought will always clothe the second. The first should always be revealed only in the role of a garment for the second, which is higher than it. The spiritual level called Zeir Anpin clothes Erech Anpin, and “Hashem—He is God!” (Kings 1 18:39).

Elevating the Power of the Imagination
Every day, a person must purify and elevate his power of imagination.
To that end, we must pray.

One cannot imagine the pollution that proliferates in the spirit of the individual, in the spirit of the entire nation, in the spirit of humanity, in the living, overall spirit of the animals living with us on earth, and in the overall spirit of existence, that results from a lapse in the constant purification of the power of the imagination.
Unless we strive to raise it ceaselessly, this power is liable to contract impurity and descend to the ultimate baseness.

This has nothing to do with the intellect. The intellect stands in its intrinsic purity. It need only be connected with us. We must be illuminated by its light via our constantly employing our intellect with concepts of truth in Torah and wisdom.
But imaginative power requires purity and elevation. And so, at every period of time, it requires encouragement and illumination.

To that end, we must recite blessings, give thanks, and recite prayers at set times. Happy is the person who is careful to engage in these matters with good intention. He illuminates himself and the entire world.

Spiritual Pollution
Just as the pollution of the soul can coalesce in an individual’s spirit to dislodge it from its good character and transform it to something base, to drag it down to a mean stratum of life, so too can it coalesce within the overall spirit of an entire nation to turn it into a base and evil nation, despised and abhorrent, one that deserves to pass away from the world so that it will not interfere with the spreading of the universal beauty of the world’s loveliness.

The Spirit Requires Godly Purity
When Godly purity shines suitably, it cleanses everything.
Then, as a result of the Divine light that shines the rays of its light upon the individual’s soul powerfully and fully, it grows radiant, holy, and mighty.
But to the degree that the Divine light is far from it or obscured in it, is polluted and darkened.
The same applies to the soul of the entire nation. When a living stream of the manifestation of God flows in the nation, it is healthy, strong, and pure.
But when God’s Presence leaves its midst, it immediately degenerates, and the pollution in it is revealed.

The national spirit can become impure as can the spirit of an individual. It can have base and evil yearnings that, in keeping with the quantity of its power and greatness, will grow to a much more considerable evil than the evil yearnings of evil individuals.
Therefore, the spirit requires purity: purity in the holy source of the Divine wellspring.

Deeds and Traits
When the nation’s deeds are good, when its traits are clean, it dreams of supernal holiness, and its intellect shines with the light of God.

But when its deeds are diminished and its traits are sullied, its national yearnings too are lowly and ugly, and weak as well, because the only true strength is the strength of heaven above, the might of God.

God’s Assurance to the Congregation of Israel
God has made a firm commitment to the entire Congregation of Israel that it will never grow completely polluted. It may be affected by pollution, which can cause it to become blemished, but the pollution cannot entirely disconnect it from the Source of Divine life.

Revealing the Light and Holiness
Our national spirit has now awoken, and many of those who cleave to that spirit say that they do not need the spirit of God.
If they would truly be able to establish that type of a national spirit among the people of Israel, they would be able to establish our nation on the basis of pollution and annihilation.

But they themselves do not know what they want. So strongly is the spirit of Israel bound to the spirit of God that even if a person says that he has no need at all for the spirit of Hashem, the fact that he says that he desires the spirit of Israel shows that a Divine spirit rests within him. It is the core of his yearning—even against his will.
The individual can disconnect himself from the Source of life, but the nation, the Congregation of Israel in its entirety, cannot.
Therefore, a spirit of God rests in all of the possessions of the nation, which it loves from the aspect of its national spirit: its land, its language, its history, its customs.

But if, at any time, a spirit should be aroused that would lead all of these people to speak in the name of the spirit of the nation only and attempt to remove the spirit of God from all of these possessions and from their revealed source, which is the holy spirit of the nation, what must the righteous people of the generation do then?

To rebel against the spirit of the nation, even in speech, and to renounce its possessions is impossible: the spirit of Hashem and the spirit of Israel is one. But they must work with great labor to reveal the light and holiness in the spirit of the nation, the light of God within all of these people, until those people who maintain these thoughts regarding the spirit of the nation of Israel and all of its possessions will find that they are immersed, rooted, and living in the life of God, illuminated by holiness and the might of heaven above.

Knowing One’s Good Side
Prayer both fortifies a person’s will and weakens his will. That is to say, it fortifies his good, ethical, holy will, and it weakens his barbaric, evil will.

To reach the latter goal—that of weakening the will—a person need not greatly elevate his personal character. His recognition that his ethics are corrupt, his awareness of this in himself, causes him an inner anguish, and his spirit sinks within him. When he casts himself down in his prayer, his evil will is weakened. Then even afterwards, in the marketplace of life, he acts for the good.
That is not the case with fortifying the will. The recognition of goodness and the drive to reinforce it require the illumination of a great spirit.

Sometimes, as a result of constantly lamenting over his spirit and suspecting himself of having abandoned his ethics, a person views every tendency of a strong will within himself as evil and baleful.

Regarding this, a person needs a clear reckoning and the illumination of his might, so that he will know his good side, whose goal is that he will be elevated by his prayer and that he will increase his might.

Revealing the Light in Prayer
The essential cause of the distancing of people’s hearts from prayer, a problem that is characteristic of this generation, is that the core of life of the Congregation of Israel has increased in strength, and its desire for the general good has been fortified. Since prayer, which is always associated with ancient ideals, has been overwhelmed by the negative aspect of the weakening of the will, the generation does not find the might and beauty that exists within prayer.
We must reveal the aspect of light that exists in prayer, that aspect in which good desire is hidden. And with that, we must bind prayer to the idea of the intensification of the will.
Then many people will stream to prayer, and there will come about as well the goal of the weakening of the sullied will.

Instinctive Goodness
When the full light of the intellect shines, there is no need for especial guidance of rules and laws.
Then the absolute good in action is drawn after the intellectual light, and all of the obstacles of life straighten themselves out.
Rules and laws then exist not as commanded rules and laws but as natural movements, as matters upon which the light of the intellect shines powerfully.

Good and evil, all of their strata and divisions, and the great toil in navigating a middle path without adding or detracting—all of these came about after the intellect diminished its light and its place was taken by feeling, impressionability and immersion in the senses, which followed the primal sin of eating from the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil.

A person may not allow [one’s] fear of heaven to override his natural morality. Were his fear of heaven [to do so], it would no longer be pure. The mark of a pure fear of heaven is that it elevates a person’s natural morality – which is planted in one’s straightforward nature – to higher levels than that which it [could] otherwise stand upon. But if we imagine a fear of heaven of such a nature that without its influence on [a person’s] life, [one’s] life would tend to result in more good and bring about [more] matters that help the individual and the community, and the influence [of that fear of heaven] would diminish this active power – such a fear of heaven is a flawed fear.

The sign of a pure fear of heaven is that a person’s natural sense of ethics, embedded in his upright nature, rises in accordance with his fear of heaven to higher levels than it would have reached without the fear of heaven.

But if there may be imagined a fear of heaven of such a type that, without its influence on a person’s life, his life would tend to bring about more goodness and matters useful for the individual and the people, whereas under its influence the power of such activity would diminish, such a fear of heaven is invalid.

From Our Inner Being Outward
We must imagine all hidden matters in relation to how they are apprehended by our intellect, as well as to how they are apprehended by our power of imagination when it is illuminated by the light of our intellect.
When we do that, we enter the outer gate of all of the beloved types of knowledge about matters that lie beyond the senses.

Once the perspective is established within us that all things exist in a true spiritual existence that has a relationship to our intellectual images, we can broaden the boundary of our knowledge to the expansive existence of spirituality beyond our being.
But if we will not proceed step by step from the inner image within us to the outer world, we will not find anything at all of what we desire to gain from spiritual attainments.

An Inner Desire to Repair Everything
Purity of the soul causes us to feel all of our sins acutely: those whose way to be repaired is clear before us, as well as those whose repair is blocked before us.

Therefore, a person should not be at all alarmed when he senses the entire burden of his sins, and they should not cause him any negligence in attaining perfection in the light and joy of the Torah, and in gaining freedom of thought in the movement of his mind, because a person’s alarm when he apprehends the multitude of his sins is itself a sign that his soul is purified. And certainly paths will open before him so that he may transform into complete merits even those sins that he presently cannot find any way to repair—in particular, matters between man and man that involve money and that involves having caused others to err, which are difficult to repair.

When a person feels an inner desire to repair everything, everything comes about to help grant merit to him and to the entire world. Therefore, he must always be happy whatever level he finds himself on, since the inner nature of his predisposition and temperament is for the good.

Raising Holy Sparks
How do we raise holy sparks from the depths of the evil “husks”?

We purify our heart by means of the guidance of enlightened and pure ethics. We sanctify our heart by means of elevated ideas about clinging to Hashem and knowing Hashem to the worthy extent that a person can attain in accordance with his intellect and the power of his soul.

Afterwards, we peregrinate through the entire fullness of ideas that encompasses all of the chambers of our spirit, and among all of the ideas and concepts that are floating about in the world. In all of them, we distinguish what they have for the good and what they have for the bad.

Also, regarding ideas that a number of wicked people have used for evil, we meticulously discern the nucleus of good that they possess. And when we find the good kernel within the depths of the evil, we hold it, polish it, and expand it, and we extract what we can and bring it into actuality.
And with that, the spark rises to its holy place.

The Knowledge of Hashem
Just as the knowledge of Hashem transcends every field of knowledge, so too it lowers itself to bring light within the smallest of hearts, and it progressively illuminates all distinguished people, each on his level.
The very possibility of possessing knowledge of Hashem cleanses the entire world, even though this potential has not yet been realized.

The Spiritually Gifted
Those unique human beings who find within themselves a disposition to know Hashem must immerse themselves in that more than in any of the fields of the Torah and worldly wisdom. They do not have permission to turn away from this level that they are on due to any hindrance in the world—even if it seems to them that as a result of immersing themselves in the knowledge of Hashem they will forego a number of matters involving the performance of practical mitzvot and knowledge of the Torah, or that they will not fulfill their obligation in regard to their material well-being.

That is because all practical and Torah perfection only functions to guide a person and bring him to the supernal state of pursuing the knowledge of Hashem. And since this person has already reached this supernal trait, Heaven forbid that he should abandon a powerful holiness and engage in a slight holiness.

It is certain that via the supernal illumination of his soul that is truly immersed in the light of Hashem, all of the paths of knowledge will expand for him, and his heart will fill with the light of justice and bringing civilization to the world until he will find vast blessing and breadth of heart, making him able to engage with true holiness both in regard to the practical aspect of the Torah and in regard to his material well-being, which he will do with prodigious success—much more than those who are immersed in practical matters alone, who have not reached the measure of true thirst for the knowledge of Hashem.

Filling One’s Knowledge of Hashem
A person’s knowledge of Hashem must be filled with his powerful thoughts of Torah and wisdom, all of the wisdom of the world and the wisdom of life, of all natural integrity in ethics and culture, and of all preparation for strength of the body and vigor of the spirit.
Then, to the extent that a person’s spirit—which yearns for the light of the knowledge of Hashem—is capable, his knowledge of Hashem will become actual.

Imagination, Mind and Ethics
It is not only a person’s intellectual enlightenment with clear understanding of Godly matters that elevates his soul, but so too the visualizations of his imagination. However, his imagination must be illuminated by his mind as much as possible, so that his imaginative faculty will not extend beyond its proper boundary—in particular, so that it will not break through to act in this world of action in accordance only with its inner, envisaging character.

In addition, a person’s ethical purity must be truly strong and purified, and his good traits must be firmly established in his spirit. Then even his imaginative power, when it is truly devoted to Godly matters, will perform great wonders and salvations in his soul and in the soul of the entire people. It will be the fundamental factor in the renewal of the world regarding even the refined and integrated spirit of practical knowledge and positive societal intelligence.

The Material and the Holy
From barley, which is animal feed, comes the omer offering.
When the animal spirit rises to its supernal source, and with its mighty strength it inclines to holiness and true purity, then the powerful, Divine love celebrates its holy holiday of Passover.
As the entire nation offers up its material powers—which are spread throughout its entirety—so that they will be holy to Hashem, its will unites with the will of the eternal God, Hashem.

And a covenant of love—[together with] the consolidation of [the nation’s] dispositions upon the path of life in the course of God’s guidance of the world (which is perfect in its holy height) and in the course of the entire sanctified nation—is established as a result of this holy activity [of the nation].
And eternal love is established between Hashem and Israel, the nation close to Him.

Purity of the Soul and Ethics
A person’s soul has the power to attain true insights from deep within itself, from the very source of its spring.
These insights are high and pure to the extent of the purity of the soul in its deeds and in its wisdom gained by learning.

But more than all such purity, there shines before the soul the path of ethical purity that comes from a person’s good character traits, as well as the person’s possession of understanding in the area of faith that is in keeping with the feeling of his pure heart, a heart that is not artful with contorted ways.

Beyond a Superficial Conception of Nothingness
Certainly, no information and intelligence on our level has any connection with the Infinite One. Nevertheless, although, when we consider something beyond our ability to conceptualize, we can only conceptualize nothingness, we must extricate ourselves from the image of a superficial nothingness to which a lack of intellect leads.
And we do that by constantly involving ourselves in study of the Divine, to the extent that our spirit can bear.

Although our spirit gains nothing of a positive conceptualization regarding the truth of Hashem in terms of His being “the Infinite One,” nevertheless in that way it is rescued from the image brought about by the Divine height, which leads the spirit to be impressed with a sense of nothingness. And instead the spirit is filled with an endless light of being.

A Call to Authors and Activists
Listen, authors and all of the nation’s spiritual activists in whose spirit nests a concern for the existence of our nation in its material and spiritual form: we seek “counsels from afar” (cf. Isaiah 25:1),counsels that are certainly good—i.e., expansion of the Hebrew language and its literature—as we look for ways to inspire love for Israelite national feeling and elevate that feeling.

But together with these counsels from afar that are seemingly new—although in truth they were already among us in the past, but aged during the days of our national slumber and insensibility—we must strengthen as well the nearby counsel, the counsel that is in our hands and before our eyes: to guard the laws of Judaism, which affect the entire nation. All of these laws come from the source of the nation’s essential life and give the nation its essential life because, when they are kept and guarded, they guard the nation’s spiritual and practical character.

Lucid Closeness to the Divine
When a person sails in the heights of Divine thought, his soul is elevated. A person can reach those heights with the freedom of his spirit and the might of his imagination. With that freedom and might, a small gleam and slight spark of the splendid radiance of the universal goal of all of the good that is stored in all of existence, in the beginning of God’s thought and at the end of His deed, sparkles in his heart.

In accordance with the degree to which a person cleanses his practical being and character, and in accordance with the degree to which he purifies his intellect and cleanses his understanding, lucid closeness to the Divine enters his heart and mind, and he rises to the heights, he rises to the peak, from where he gazes upon all of the paths of the world, intellectual and practical, and from where he descends, filled with goodness and lovingkindness, filled with might and splendor, and he shepherds with love the flock of Hashem, “flocks of men” (Ezekiel 36:38).

Faith and the Supernal Torah
Faith in God gives people happiness, but only to the extent that the Divine greatness is studied and learned by that significant sector of people that is fit to do so, because then the soul is illuminated by the supernal light, since it clings with complete love and knowledge to the Life of lives. And then all feelings, concepts, and deeds are refined.

But when this sector of people ignores the supernal Torah—a teaching that leads to the recognition of God’s greatness and to a supernal perfection that is infinite and priceless—faith itself is blemished. It does not produce the good fruit that it should produce, and it does not openly raise souls from their lowness.

Then faith falls, and those who derogate it and desecrate it multiply. And it will only return to its vigor when the most elevated righteous people, the strong and wise among human beings most perfected in the knowledge of God, will strengthen themselves tremendously to intensify their yearning to examine the greatness of Hashem in all major pathways, intellectual and ethical, until faith will be elevated and will emerge from its darkness to great light, and will be a source of life for all of the highest and most refined souls in the world, as is the true nature of faith. And so its honor and preciousness will return to it as well in all human avenues.
And that which concerns the people of at this time is the entirety of the nation’s last resort: to restore its preciousness of pure, Divine faith, which is the entire foundation of its life.

Torah and Socialism
The inner soul that invigorates socialist doctrine in its present form is the light of the practical Torah in its full purity and character.
But the doctrine itself is in the midst of its growth, and it does not yet know its fundamental essence.
However, days will come when it will be an established institution on behalf of the fortitude of the Torah and the mitzvot in their full exaltedness and purity.

The Divine Spark and Anarchism
Anarchism comes from a higher foundation than does socialism.
Anarchism is not a foundation for the practical Torah and for keeping the Torah, but for supernal clinging to the Divine beyond all positive deed and order.

Therefore, it is farther removed from its source—which stands very far above the lowliness of present-day life—than socialism is. And anarchism, in its present state and in the state of life at present, is entirely disorderly, despite the exalted Divine spark hidden within it.

Dealing with Morose People
It is very harmful to pious people, those who are filled with the might of Hashem, to bond spiritually with base people who only have an external fear of God and who are filled with a miserable dread and lowly moroseness that spreads across the entire span of their spiritual lives.

Very great is the suffering of a pious person’s soul when he participates with them in conversation, in prayer, and in all matters of holiness. He requires an immense amount of preparation to bolster his spiritual strength and the Divine, clear light in his soul in order to protect himself, so that his soul will not be pulled down by the lowly smallness of people with this external fear, who have no powerful desire for God but only the weakness of their morose dread.

Light and Repentance
The inner light that shines in all existence must build its own world.

It runs along its circuit, paying no attention to its overall connection to the encompassing light outside itself, which is filled with worlds, paying no attention even to that which, in accordance with its measure, its inner being would be able to discern.
However, its inner being contains a permanent supernal yearning to be bound to the surrounding light, which is incomparably greater and vaster than itself.

When that yearning intensifies, it reveals the light of repentance on repentance’s supernal level, which is higher than complete righteousness. The inner being of repentance has never sunken but has always adapted to that which is higher than itself: to that which, in its might, encompasses repentance.

Practical Life
The individual and the nation cannot guard themselves against the blurring of their spiritual form that results from the weight of practical life, by running away from it. This refers to material actions regarding physical needs and to spiritual actions regarding keeping and knowing the obligations of the Torah and mitzvot with all of their precise details, which tremendously fatigue the wise spirit that seeks the light whose brightness is unlimited.

A person is caught by practical life. The more he wishes to be freed from his servitude to it, the more it weighs down on him—unless he accommodates himself to it in a structured form so that it cannot darken the noble light of his spiritual life.

A person must accommodate himself to material, practical life by means of a good perspective and proper alacrity based on the foundation of rectifying his income so that he will earn a living honorably and in a permissible manner, and by means of properly treating himself in guarding the health of his body and spirit.

And he must accommodate himself to practical spiritual life by accustoming himself to review halachahs with a broad perspective regarding their foundations and reasons, without growing too entangled by arguments and subtleties, but learning in order to equip himself with clear knowledge.
