The deep manifestation of the will in the blueprint of faith—a manifestation that comes from a very elevated inner recognition—is the source of the light of the will.
From that source, exalted thoughts emerge.

Via these thoughts, the entire spiritual world comes to a state of rest, with all of its wondrous certainties, which—in the great force of their freshness—stand higher than all the certainty in this world.
These exalted thoughts exist in the depths of the individual soul, which draws into itself the richness of its life as a result of the blending together of the overall gathering.
With that, the individual soul receives its abundance from the foundation of all existence. The wisdom of God pours its spirit onto the soul constantly, in vision and in actuality.
Righteous people, wise people, mighty people, beautiful people, wealthy people and ruling people will no longer be separated in their character.
Instead, they will all together bring forth the essence rising from the manifestation of all of them together, which is higher than all of life’s external and internal possessions.
That is because the essence of life comes about from all of these people. In that way, the essence of life grows wealthy and blends together.

The might that is found in the power of supernal life, a power that reveals its ability in the form of scattered sparks in every talented person and in every national and political group, will be revealed by means of the light of the will in all its completeness.
And that completeness will appear in its whole light, in which all of the details in their great wealth will be included in actuality.
And with every slight movement of spirit, full worlds will be created and develop. They will generate and give birth with great power.

Faith in the Proper Measure
Faith beyond the proper measure debilitates the world. Not only false faith, but even true faith, when it has too much of an effect on the individual and on the public soul—as it blends its power with other spiritual and practical powers—causes people to lose clarity.

Therefore, there are always many factors in the world that diminish faith—despite the fact that the tendency for faith is so strong—in order to establish a situation correctly. And then the world receives the goodness within faith in the proper measure.
This pertains not only to faith but also to wisdom and ethics, and to every other capability.
So we see that just as every good phenomenon has its helpers, so does it have its own disturbances.

From an isolated perspective, it appears that the things that help establish the world and the things that disturb debilitate the world. But with an overall perspective, we see that both build the world: the former with their positivity and the latter with their negativity.

The final generation of every era comes in most instances with negative power. That is because an era comes to an end only when the most refined spiritual power has served as an influencing power, and with its influence it certainly exceeded its measure, bringing a great deal of good that the world could not absorb. And that caused the world harm.

Therefore, the measure of the final generation comes, a generation that concludes an era and begins an era, a generation that is negative. As soon as it reveals its negativity and carries out its function to “level the heap,” the weakness and nothingness in the negativity are revealed, and it itself diminishes its place so that it will not spread profusely.
And the excessive spreading that it caused with its initial appearance is now rectified as a result of the overall blending.

In our world, we see the heretical movement and the insolence of the time in its foundations that imitate erudition with Biblical criticism. That is on the one hand. But on the other hand, we also see new discoveries and their being decided for the good of faith. These will give Divine balance to the spirit of faith and its proper blending.

The Value of Non-Obligatory Prayer
Prayer must well up from the walls of the heart so much that every obligation to pray makes it routine. That is the basis of the approach of those who state that the obligation to pray has no basis in the Torah (Nachmanides).
Therefore, the choicest portion in relation to prayer is the evening prayer, whose greatness is the fact that it is optional (Berachot 27b).

Prayer clean of any aspect of routine is called an “encounter”: “Jacob encountered the place of prayer” (Genesis 28:11). That is the trait of Jacob. “The house of Jacob’s God will be called a house of prayer for all the nations” (cf. Isaiah 56:7) “on the day that God will convert all the nations to a pure language so that all of them will call in the name of Hashem” (cf. Zephaniah 3:9).

The acronym of “pure language” (safah verurah) is shav, “return” to God. So too, in the letter substitute system called at-bash, the acronym is shav, with the letters reversed (but not the meaning, “because from the rising of the sun until its setting”—[backwards and forwards]—“great is the name of Hashem” (cf. Malachi 1:11).

“And they will fear from the [sun] setting [in the west] the name of Hashem, and from the rising of the sun His glory, because He will come like a river that distresses [them]” (Isaiah 59:19) uprooting all obligations, “the spirit of Hashem a waving banner in it” (ibid.), raising the flag of the optional, which is choicest of all, the secret of the benefit of approaching Mt. Sinai even without the giving of the Torah (Passover Haggadah, Dayeinu). “He brought me to the house of wine” (Song of Songs 2:8)—i.e., Mt. Sinai (Midrash Tanchuma, Bamidbar 10), “and his banner over me was love” (op. cit.): truly love.

The phrase, “And his banner over me was love,” permuted as an acronym and a gematria yields the word oz, “might.” And the final letters of that phrase permuted as a gematria yield the word tal, “dew.”

“May only goodness and kindness pursue me all the days of my life, and may I dwell in the house of Hashem for length of days” (Psalms 23:6). “Length of days” at its absolute foundation is a state of love and delight, which rise above every obligation and requirement.

The Temple and the Land
The power that gives life to the soul of Israel is the wondrous yearning for the building of the Temple and for the return of its glory, with its ultimate, hoped-for ideal wholeness. Only this anticipation elevates the spirit of all the generations: the knowledge that there is an exalted purpose to their lives and their historical continuance.
In this supernal point is hidden the entire strength of life of the nation’s connection to the land of Israel.
And all of the mitzvot that are dependent on the Land, to whatever extent that they apply, guard the moisture of this fundamental dew of life.

When Our Senses Are Purified
When our sense is purified, we see how the soul grows to wholeness, how it streams and flows, affecting and illuminating an entire world.
And the more our deeds are rectified, our traits are clarified and our intellect shines, the more the breadth of our strong and joyous, free and assured soul spreads.
The details of knowledge, feelings, facts, faith, intentions and will are only small streams. From them, many currents of light cascade, appearing as they come from the source of their life.

Two Failings in Nationalistic Thought
There are two failings in nationalistic thought. It must be made whole in order to provide wholeness for the failings. That wholeness will come from a place other than this thought.

One, nationalistic thought does not properly satisfy the aspect of the individual. At times an individual’s demands are great. When they are not fulfilled—whether in their spiritual form or in their material form—everything is flawed, and then as well the power of the totality of the people is not sturdy.

And two, this thought can only describe the life of this world. But the way to fulfill the soul and secure the bridge between the life of this world and the life of the world-to-come is something that nationalistic thought must receive from the supernal, spiritual influence that is philosophical, Divine, kabbalistic and societal. It is here that the depth of faith finds its substance.

Heaven and Earth, Soul and World
It is very hard for one person to contain within himself correctly arranged impressions of the external world as, together with that, the impressions of his internal world are well-arranged.

Usually, when a person turns to the outer world, he forgets his inner world. The rarefaction of his thoughts, the elevation of his feelings, the purity of his traits, the might of his will and his refinement are all matters that require the attention of his entire heart.

The Torah is unique, due to its Divine character, in incorporating heaven and earth, soul and world. As a result of its extensive influence on a person who learns it and knows it, his spirit is blended together and is made whole in regard to its various characteristics, external and internal. That is something that no other wisdom provides, nor any other education.

It is true that Divine thought is itself the foundation of the Torah and its soul. But that Divine thought can only be absorbed well in one of two ways. One is by means of a regimen of great and vast studies that prepare a person’s soul by giving it such an unrestrained leap upward that it can stand on a Divine platform to expansively study those ideas that this person’s finite intellect, taken from his habit and senses, contradicts.

Or the other is that, in a wondrous way, a person’s soul is graced with an inward ability of the spirit—so that, commensurate with its character, it is prepared to possess a Divine gaze—so much so that at times spiritual heroes arise upon the arena of life as a vision that arouses wonder, and they place their seal upon the face of generations.

Restoring the Alienated Sparks
The discerning eye sees how every institution that takes holy content from an Israelite source while sending its roots to another nation draws richness away from the Congregation of Israel, and in this way diminishes Israel’s might.

All of this is the case when the nation [of Israel] is not prepared to pour forth a flow of life in such a form that its giving will not diminish its strength but rather its strength will return to it with added vigor.

But even when matters are in a degraded state, people with a broad view notice the conduits via which the richness travels to distances. They recognize this richness in all its forms, and they constantly restore the original good to its root.

However, a person with a high soul must soar high upward in a rarefied state [in order to] engage in this mystical, tremendous enterprise. And while that soul is rising, it cannot manifest its light upon the many rows of souls [of Israel] that depend upon the power of its might. Only when it turns its gaze back to their circle, which is on an intermediate plane, do the hidden relationships [between this high soul and] these souls connect, and then they are refined and receive inner strength, even without their knowledge.

Therefore, the [high soul’s] supernal soaring [that results in] the return of the richness that had been drawn to foreign distances does not occur constantly but only on occasion, at the most propitious time, when the person with an elevated root soul knows with an inner sense that, in accordance with the situation, he has prepared a richness of life and might for the many spirits that depend on him, in a way that will suffice to establish them in their character and freshness until the cessation of the elevated soul’s soaring that raises it to the highest heavens.

The Emotions and Discernment
Sometimes a person exists in a such state that he must derive everything from his discernment, and he need not take into account his emotional traits and their corollaries, because a covenant has been made that when a person’s consciousness is elevated, all of his traits will be elevated, and when he is purified, they will be purified.

And an elevated person upon whom the light of knowledge pours from its many wellsprings may not measure the content of these traits within himself in terms of that content’s relationship to good and evil by the same middling measurement that is common among people whose life is only a life of emotion and imagination. That is because in truth the difference between them is greater than the difference between a life of sleep and dreaming and a life of wakefulness and clear thought.

Slow and Sudden Perceptions
Spiritual perceptions [of truth] are revealed to a person in a sudden way.

And just as they are not subject to time, so are they not subject to the gradualism of measuring possibility and impossibility in the same measure that such a truth is measured when a person has slow intellectual perceptions that come not in the way of a flow of rivers, but constrained, drop by drop.

The Expansion of Life
A spiritual appraisal contemplates the life of the soul calmly, with an increasingly clear consciousness, until a tier of life emerges from the framework of a shadow of life, a life that is in truth a description of death, and instead that tier of life is accentuated with all its splendor and might, with all its honor and delight.
Everything holy, good, ethical, and just is connected to this phenomenon, which rises to Godly heights that are filled with radiance and brightness.

This appraisal encounters the life of the soul at the onset of its existence, before the consolidation of its actions in bodily, finite deeds. And that appraisal knows, with increasing clarity, all of the soul’s ancient goals.
And so the thread of life proceeds and is drawn to supernal goals that expand throughout the entire course of life by means of a person’s liberated, supernal, Godly gaze.

And from that gaze comes a gaze toward full states of clarity regarding the progression of supernal life of the power of the soul, after the truncating encirclement of life subjugated to matters of the body.
And the blending of individual spirituality with overall spirituality, with the knot of life, increases in the way of the tranquility and serenity of righteous people.

The most impenetrable questions in the life of the spirit are solved, and tangible, bodily life grows more vigorous and becomes joyful and steadfast, because an end, hope and a broad goal stand before them.
And the refined light of the most holy feelings that completely sanctify life intensifies, until its sparks vitalize the tens of thousands of the nation with temporal life and eternal life.

Fear and God’s Kindness
When fear intensifies in a person’s heart from the aspect of the clarity of his perception, he must then conceal himself in the shadow of the Divine kindness by means of supernal repentance, which renews all existence from the depth of its root. That aligns with the form of the supernal wholeness that cannot be realized in actuality but which is always yearned-for, and a person’s heart possesses a sweet sorrowing to come to its level.
Although activity and life compel a person to walk upon a middle path, nevertheless the soulful desire “to draw oneself to the body of the King” (Zohar 1:217b) is without limit.

The Divine in Everything and the Intellect
When a person habituates himself to hear the voice of Hashem from everything, that arrives at the most supernal component in the human spirit, which is the intellect. Yet it is precisely the intellect that cloaks this Divine matter more than anything else does, because a person thinks that this voice is a special intellectual capability making these intellectual forms.

However, as a result of the beneficial habituation of paying heed to the voice of Hashem in everything, the voice of Hashem is revealed to a person in his intellect as well, and then it is precisely in his intellect that he will find the true Divine revelation.
And the more he increases inquiry and philosophizing, the more will he increase the holiness of his faith, his clinging to God, and an outpouring of Divine inspiration.

Serving God with the Imagination and Serving God
The nature of serving God has two components. There is service of the imagination and service in actuality.

Service of the imagination is based on drawing a person’s feelings to great matters—the greatest of which is, of course, the Divine. And since a person’s feeling is drawn to that which is exalted, the body and its abilities do not place a very great constraint on the intensification of his supernal spirituality.

But actual service actually gives life to a person’s will and strengthens the Divine soul—in the person and in the world—via his good deeds and true intellections and everything holy and true, in accordance with his intellectual purity and the manifestation of the light of the Torah.

With a person’s arousal that leads to this service, a content of life is revealed to him: that he has a role to play in increasing the most supernal good in the world, which includes every great element that leads to the overall good.

And if such an element is one of those in which the good is revealed and seemingly finite, that does not cause it to lose its value. Rather, much good is still hidden in it, and the value of its goodness is a Divine specialness: i.e., all of the details of the commandments and the supernal traits that the pious elite, warriors of the spirit, live in accordance with, in the blamelessness of their heart and with the joy of the upright and a spirit of supernal might that lifts them above all actions.

Thoughts and Feelings
The inner service of God has something of an order of thoughts, which is the essence of a life of contemplation, and an order of feelings, which is the life of poetry and song. It is involved with the relationship between these two different characteristics, in order to discern how they mesh and affect each other, in what way their interweaving succeeds, and in what way they must separate, each in its own system.

The Importance of Divine Inspiration
With a flow of Divine inspiration, we feel how the spirit of Godly life from the light of the Life of worlds proceeds in all avenues of life, in all wills, in all worlds, in all thoughts, in all nations, in all people, in all of the avenues of Torah and its commandments—practical, intellectual and emotional—in all of the offshoots that emerge from them and in all of the imaginings and personal sensitivities that are engendered through them.

Via this phenomenon, which is very much superior to the constricted intellect, we recognize the preciousness of holiness and faith, of doing everything for the sake of heaven. And we feel how spiritual life, which vitalizes and encourages, spreads from the holy names of the King, the King of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, to the entire Torah, to all of its letters, to every particular soul of Israel, and to the entire world, as a result of the letters becoming whole.

Without any assistance at all of Divine inspiration, it is impossible to explain exalted visions such as the pleasantness of the Torah and faith, the role of the service of prayer, and exactitude in the commandments.

Divine inspiration is clothed in wisdom: in wisdom of holiness and even in wisdom of the secular. These garments are at times fit for a person’s measure, and at times they have too little or too much. The latter occurs when they are secular upon holy. But regarding holiness that clothes holiness, everything is in accordance with the proper measure. “The cohen’s garment (middo) measure is according to his size (middah)” (Leviticus 6:3, Zevachim 35a).

Repentance, Redemption, and the Secrets of the Torah
Repentance will come from a variety of directions.
One of these aspects will be the pain that will be revealed for the insult to the great spirit contained in all that our forefathers bequeathed to us, whose might and glory has no measure.
And the source of this great spirit is the source of life, the Godly, supernal source that is continuously drawn from generation to generation.
When one focuses on this, one finds everything in it: all that is desirable and all that is splendid.
The heretical darkness has caused a detachment from this “fruitful and rich hill” (Isaiah 5:1) and led people to stray in foreign fields that have no moisture or life for us at all.

This great pain will explode in strength. And it will be accompanied by the power of calm and deliberation so that we will know what there is to take from all of the misleading ways in which we have stumbled.

The inner freedom within our soul will come forth from its imprisonment, and with a mighty thirst, every aroused spirit will begin to draw forth and drink to satiety from that living, supernal wellspring.

Then awareness and feeling, a meaningful life, a considered view of the world and a desire for the national renaissance, for the rectification of the blemishes of one’s soul and the intensification of one’s bodily strength, for governmental order and a pleasant society with civilized behavior and proper tolerance—together with a living zealousness against everything vile and evil, against everything perverse and ugly, and with an inner dedication on behalf of all the means through which the universal, supernal good can appear—all of these opposites will then be brought into being as a single unit.

And in order to support these means, we must prepare our hearts to receive the inner, true light of the Torah—the secrets of the Torah—which whoever has some talent to speak and write disdains so much and insults so much (although in truth there is cause to insult the influences brought about by people who have clung to these secrets without proper preparation).

It is precisely from this light of life, from which harm has always blossomed in the world, this that the nation’s salvation, its eternal salvations, the light of the good will blossom, giving life to the whole and to each individual, raising the fallen booth of David and removing the disgrace of the nation of Hashem from all the earth.

The Power of Our Imagination
When the power of our imagination is purified in the merit of our purity of thought, good deeds and good traits, and a yearning for the Torah and wisdom, we come to feel the abundance of life, how that abundance proceeds from the light of the Infinite One to give life to all of the worlds.
Then the soul begins to shine, and it is filled with wisdom and light from this holy delight. “Because with You is the source of life; in Your light we will see light” (Psalms 36:10).

The Greatness of Light
A person need never leave the greatness of the light of pleasantness that accompanies his supernal clinging to the Divine with a breadth of consciousness. He need not at all be concerned even if it appears to him that his deeds have not yet been purified and, how much more, his thoughts, his balance, his speech and most of his affairs. Even though he feels the weakness of his will, he should nevertheless perform his obligations, and he will cling to the supernal light, which is the foundation of the Torah.
If he can cling to the supernal intellectual point in keeping with his measure and his level, he is standing on a very respectable level.

He might feel some barrier in his intellect so that all of his mental images can only exist in keeping with his imagination. Still and all, an inner, Divine repentance rests within him and he recognizes that his fundamental will is to cling to the Life of lives, to exist in the light of the supernal Being from which come all beloved things, all eternities, all delights, all types of peace, all strengths, types of beauty, praises and radiances, and his soul pines for the holy of supernal holies. Thus, his imagination is the garment in which the supernal intellect, which is truly the light of Hashem, hides. And that is the foundation of the exuberances of the entire Torah and wisdom. Therefore, due to that itself, he will be filled with light and joy.

Sometimes, as a result of a person’s constant pining for the Divine, his body is weakened before it has risen entirely and as a result of this weakness he does not engage in Torah and prayer. Nevertheless, he should not allow his heart to be depressed, but he should rejoice and be strong in his good portion: the fact that his weakness comes from this holy and supernal source.

“His hope is in Hashem, his God” (Psalms 146:5). “Do not read ‘his hope’ (sivro) but ‘his breaking of himself (shivro)’” (Zohar 2:198a), with the diacritical mark on the right. And “the right hand of Hashem is elevated and deals valiantly” (Psalms 118:16).

What Does Prayer Accomplish?
A person who thinks that with prayer he changes the Divine is blaspheming. And a person who thinks that he is only changing himself diminishes the value of prayer, and together with it the entire value of service of the Divine.

But when a person has in mind that he is working to change himself for the good and he has the attitude that the essence of his being changes, then the entire value of all existence changes for him, toward elevation and toward good, because all existence is affected by one of its particular spiritual parts.
And the more elevated and inclusive the spiritual content that leads to the transformations, the more intense and effective are the changes in the flow of their goodness.
That is the way of a person who works with the proper intent: his soul is filled by it, and the world is blessed.

The Prayer of the Righteous Person
The righteous person whose soul is very great has an inner demand that all of his prayer will be in keeping with the depth of his clear consciousness, and that his imagination will serve it only in a subordinate manner. And when, as a result of various causes, he does not recognize his own worth and he wishes to pray as an ordinary person, with prayer built upon the superficial imagination, he feels immeasurable pains of the soul.
And this which applies to prayer applies to all holy thoughts and their feelings.

Imagination and Wisdom
When the torch of the light of consciousness is very great, a person’s imagination as well is transformed to something that is pure intellect. That adds more content of life, which is felt in the soaring of one’s wisdom, and with that, the imagination adds brightness to the wisdom.

Prayer and the Will
Prayer has an effect in accordance with the level of the character of the will of the person praying.
The entirely good will is the ontological necessity itself, and it is none other than that found in the supernal source, the light of the Infinite One.

And the vigor of the existence of every limited will is in accordance with the level of its goodness and in accordance with the level of the profundity of that good. And in keeping with the vigor of its existence, so is the vigor of its strength to act.

As for righteous people, who are mighty heroes, they and their desire are good. And in accordance with the level of each of them in his goodness, his prayer has an effect. And “the will of a righteous person who is the son of a righteous person is deeper than that of a righteous person who is the son of a wicked person. Therefore, his prayer is more heeded” (cf. Yevamot 64a).

Double-Valenced Thought
A noble thought is not complete in a person as he rises to envision the universal good and to strive to desire it for himself and for the entire world unless that thought seeks the possibility of a type of life that will improve the world by rectifying its societal character and, in addition, resolve for the good the life of the individual in its externality and in its internality, and establish a foundation that will provide a basis for a stance of life in which eternal life—which is connected to the purification of souls and to their absolute spiritual strengthening—will be elicited from the well-arranged rectification of societal and individual stances and from the treasury of thoughts that the Primal Thought causes to be poured out upon life.

Every thought that dismisses the rectification of the world and national arrangements, that blossoms in a spiritual atmosphere by itself and takes pride in the rectification of souls and their success is based upon falsehood that has no feet to stand upon.

And as for every thought that has nothing to do with eternal exaltedness but involves itself only with the material arrangements of life and their rectifications, even if it possesses ethical contents and just and upright ways, it will in the end grow murky because of its smallness and because of the pollution and stench with which material life is stricken in its nature when it is disconnected from the foundation of eternal life and its desire. In particular, such a weakness in communal thought may be recognized in the fact that it focuses only on young people, before whom material life plays with all its shams and caprices, and old people can only take a vigorous part in it with a fabricated will and a despairing heart.
And that is the Greek attribute: to gaze upon old people with a contemptuous gaze, as in Aristotle’s words in Rhetoric.

And how flawed is a public policy that cannot spread out well to all its parts. And the verse states, “Hashem of Hosts has reigned in Mt. Zion and in Jerusalem, and before His elders will be honor” (Isaiah 24:23).

Exterior Destruction and Inner Improvement
Sometimes there is a great leader but the generation is not rectified. And conversely, sometimes there is a leader smaller than he, but the generation is rectified. For instance, the generation of Solomon was greater than that of Moses.

However, the overall elevation is not in the generation itself but in the totality of the order of the world. And in keeping with the order of the world, everything then was rectified. “The moon was in its fullness in the days of Solomon” (Shemot Rabbah 15:26; Zohar 3:61a).

There is improvement of the world from the aspect of its inner being and there is improvement from the aspect of its exterior. Overall, from the aspect of the exterior, throughout all of the days since the Destruction of the Temple, “there is not a day whose curse is not greater than its predecessor” (Sotah 49a). But from the aspect of the inner being, the world is improving.

The era preceding the messiah is a situation of exterior descent and inner improvement. Therefore, it leads to the light of the messiah, in which everything is fulfilled, including exterior improvement, because when the inner being is improved, it is very easy to improve the exterior.

Masters of kabbalistic secrets must inform the world that its descent is only external, but within everything is rising, and so the illumination is great. And in essence, the souls are great, and greatness and holiness exist even within the insolence. And “when distress shall come like a river, the spirit of Hashem will be wondrous in it” (Isaiah 59:19).

At this time repentance is always an elevated repentance, repentance out of love, when purposeful sins turn into absolute merits (Yoma 86b). Transgression cannot cause as much damage as it did in the earlier generations, because of the great amount of improvement of the world and the abundance of compassion and kindness that shine in it.

And the righteous people in the generation can draw forth an abundance of great kindness to the point of erasing entirely all of the offenses of the generation and transforming them into merits, literally—even without open repentance from the aspect of the generation, but by means of the intellectual repentance of the tzaddikim alone, who do repentance on behalf of the entire generation (cf. Yoma 86b). In their thought, they bind all of the souls of the generation to themselves, until their souls bind with them, and they all become whole and purified.
And the exterior radiance that the people lack is fulfilled immediately by the dazzling light in the soul of the righteous people, which could not come about when the inner improvement was lacking.

The Divine and the Spirit of Israel
The overall will of the spirituality of the nation of Israel has its measure. Higher than it is the will of Divine content in the nation of Israel, which corresponds to the nation’s comprehension and its inner and outer life.

As long as the nation’s spiritual content is full and great, the light of the Divine content in what the nation comprehends grows in a higher measure, and the nation envisions that which its existence seeks in bright hues. Higher than that, that which is sought by all existence, which is the secret of the supernal knowledge, is revealed in bright hues.

When the nation descended into the bitter exile, its soul was darkened and the comprehension resulting from the inner search of its existence and of the desires of its life shrank, until the nation cannot at all find its paths. Nevertheless, the nation has within itself some weak comprehension of an impression of light from which dim light shines on some level to righteous people and wise people who seek Hashem in their hearts, even in the darkness. “When I sit in darkness, Hashem is my light” (Micah 7:8).

As for the Divine matter and the universal goal, if it would have stood in its original place and level, it would not at all have been able to bind with the nation’s essential goal. And then the nation’s life in exile would have taken a secular way for itself, without turning to connect with the Divine purpose of the Rock of all the worlds, the Righteous One in all the generations.
What did the Holy One, blessed be He, do?

Just as the shining light in the nation was diminished in relation to its inner content, so did the Divine, overall light descend in the world, and the elevation of the Divine matter, which is the light of the Life of worlds, only flashes with such a weak light that it can unite with the light shining in the soul of Israel even after the descent that has plunged the diadem of the beauty of Israel from heaven to earth.

And since the overall Divine matter in the role of the light of the world stands in such a position, matters again bind together, and the purpose of the existence of the nation in the spirit of its inner holiness and the great, overall, Divine purpose of all existence can unite as one. They bind together in themselves, and in the individual souls of Israel in particular and in the soul of the totality of the nation overall, and they are prepared together to rise with the salvation of the nation and its Godliness. “I and He, Save Us Now” (kabbalistic phrase from the siddur).

Repentance out of Love, and Forgiving Oneself
When a person repents out of love, he must forgive himself all of his sins, just as one must appease one’s fellow regarding offenses between one person and another in order to attain his forgiveness.
And after he will be exonerated and clean of transgression in his own eyes, the holiness from a supernal portion will be aroused upon him, so that all of his sins will be transformed to merits.

The Torah and the Beginning of the Universe
The clearer it will grow to a person that the Torah with its supernal spirituality is the supernal cause and instrument of all existence—in the entire breadth of the meaning of this word “existence”—of all the physicality and all the spirituality in the worlds, the more will his thought rise, until he will understand and sense that every holy thought and every holy word is much more exalted and firm in its might than all existence.

Then not all the images of the sensory world, of its borders and its demands, the vigor of nature and its processes, and any logical idea, finite and envisioned in keeping with the ways of the intellect and the search in the thoughts of the heart of a human being, will be able to hinder the greatness of the loftiness and dominion of the words of Torah and prayer and their attendant thoughts.

That is because a holy light higher than them all governs them all, manages them and determines them, and illuminates everything with its light. “The commencement of your words enlightens” (Psalms 119:120).

The Essence of Serving God Grows Clearer
The essence of serving God grows clearer to a person the more he knows that the light of Divine, supernal life provides the life-force for all of his spiritual affairs—in intellect and in will, in feeling and in disposition, in character and in attribute—just as it provides the life-force for everything in existence and in being.

Then the nature of permanent clinging to Divinity will be impressed into him, and that clinging will be made whole in the entire might of its activities corresponding to the size of his insight, corresponding to the amount of his spiritual wisdom, corresponding to the elevation of his traits and his deeds, corresponding to the rising of his will and the purification of his soul in preparation to see the ascent of all worlds in the glorious radiance of their spirituality.

And this holy nature will grow stronger the more that evil—individual and universal—will be transformed to good, and darkness to light—not only overall but in detail, as a result of a constant manifestation of holiness every day.

Evil’s Pain, as Good Prevails
Evil is pained upon the growth of the good. And aspects of evil in the soul and in the world shrivel and suffer because the pride of Hashem and the light of holiness expand and spread in the individual and in the world.

Due to that, a person feels pain when he begins his approach to engaging in supernal service. But he must then rise until he reaches this trait of holy severity and the greatness of vengeance—which is placed between two Divine Names, just as knowledge is (Berachot 33a).

And the will to burn away evil and diminish it grows more complete and reaches its goal by means of evil’s pain, which is the beginning of its fall. Then, the more that the evil element in the soul increases its pain, the more that the good in the person—and that good is his principal existent essence—increases its delight and comfort.
And a reflection of this activity in the soul will occur in the entire world, and then a likeness of the light of the messiah will shine.
“Saviors will ascend Mt. Zion to judge the mountain of Esau, and Hashem will have the sovereignty” (Obadiah 1:21).

Two Ways That the Soul Brings Light into the World
Sometimes, we must recognize the spiritual effect of our inner work and the light of the Torah and prayer overall on the interiority of our soul. And from our soul, the light emerges to the entire world.

And sometimes we must stand in such a way that our soul is only a measuring device, like that which measures land and vessels, and the spiritual manifestations shine upon the entire world. And in the end, honor will come as well to the manifestation of our individual soul, from which this light has welled.

This latter trait operates at times from the aspect of our state of greatness, and at times from the aspect of our state of smallness. It is impossible to hold the middle measure, and we must grasp specifically the supernal greatness, so that it will manifest light in all the worlds. “When I sit in darkness, Hashem is my light” (Micah 7:8).

The Righteous Person Gathers All Opposites Together
The righteous person who is in his proper state of being, whom supernal lovingkindness has granted the talent of a genius for righteousness (just as the talent for art and poetry are granted those who possess them) contains within himself all types of knowledge, thoughts, ideas and influences.
He gathers everything that is scattered. And that which appears to the entire world to be contradictory and in conflict is reconciled and gathered together for him in a united and unified gathering.
And from the depth of the oneness in his soul, he pours peace, love and oneness—external and internal—over everything.
His work is always to unify and connect. And every spiritual connection in his thought multiplies peace in all the worlds.

Healthy Bodies and Pure Souls
Bodies that are healthy, pure and clean, splendid in their measure, even externally, and souls that are pure and ethereal, vigorous and filled with grace—that is what we must aspire to increase in the world, and most of all among the people of Israel, and starting with the Torah scholars.

We must push away all thoughts that disturb our connection to this dual aim. And every goal of life must be to actualize this holy aim, whether via its practical and intellectual means, whether via its spiritual, metaphysical means.

Imagination Imbued by Intellect Creates Miracles
In each person, there is imagination that clothes his intellect and imbues it with a sparkling flash and splendor. “Any addition whose purpose is to beautify does not interpose” (Succah 37a)—but any excess beyond that goes beyond the structure of holiness, since the light of the intellect does not rest in that excess at all. And then Shadai (“Almighty”) turns into shod (“plundering”) (Isaiah 13:6).

But as for the imagination in which the intellect shines, it is the foundation of miracles. That is because all existence (delineated by its laws) exists only in keeping with our imagination. The light of the intellect of lower wisdom shines in that existence in such a way that the laws of nature are arranged by our imagination. Within this lattice, all miracles are made. They nullify the imagination because of the illumination of the supernal intellect that rules over the imagination and nullifies it.
And the words nes (“miracle”) and dimyon (“imagination”) have the same numerical value.

When Imagination Clothes the Intellect
Sometimes, we begin our service of God with joy and the light of knowledge, because our imagination is saturated by the light of the intellect. But after a short amount of time, the imagination totters because the illumination of the intellect leaves it, and a person feels spiritual weariness.

He must renew the light of knowledge from the sanctified, supernal intellectual source. And when there is no opposition from the aspect of any bodily weariness, the beautiful imagination will return to clothe the new illumination, and he can begin a new service of God “with joy and with gladness of heart due to the abundance of everything” (Deuteronomy 28:47).

A Renewal of Intellectual Illumination
In particular, we require a renewal of the intellectual illumination between the chapters of the prayer service.

And that is the basis for recitation of the Kaddish between the four well-known sections of the morning prayers: the prayer of Asiyah [sacrifices], Yetzirah [Psalms], Beriah [the Sh’ma], Atzilut [Shemoneh Esrei]. But in the day in the morning prayers, as opposed to the evening prayers between Beriah and Atzilut, no interruption is needed and so Kaddish is not recited, and then it is precisely the flow that is praiseworthy.

Holiness and Beauty
Whoever accustoms himself to look at the Divine illumination that exists in every spiritual creation finds the holy element that gives life to all wisdom, and he is able to bind the wisdom of the world with the Torah, and bring the attractiveness of Japheth into the tents of Shem (Yoma 10a).

And this attractiveness of Japheth is in truth the loveliness of Shem, the glory and splendor in the house of our God (cf. Psalms 96:6). “‘Beauty’ (Chronicles 1 29:11) refers to the giving of the Torah” (Berachot 58a).

Holiness, the Principal and the Incidental
We must look at the supernal principles of intellect and feeling. Then we find them congruent in their purity with the light of the manifestation of the Torah.

The details and the divergences change in keeping with climate, ethnicity, history, religion, politics and all other circumstantial differences, regarding which we must take care so as not to bring the mundane into the holy.

The Importance of Clarifying Exalted Matters
In our generations, a person who has a universal soul must present introductions that clarify the keys to every exalted matter.

He must present an introduction to faith overall: to understand its parameters, its description, its character, its effect on a person and on the world, and the good and bad aspects of its manifestation—in order to know how to put everything in its place.

He must present introductions to ethics, to ethics’ entire expansive and profound doctrine in all its various aspects: to Divine, manifesting ethics, to faith-based ethics, to natural ethics, to practical ethics and character-related ethics, to an individual’s ethics and to societal, collective ethics, to educational ethics and to family ethics, to practical ethics and to theoretical ethics, to ethics of the historical past and to ethics of the present, to ideal, future ethics, and finally to a collective, spiritual ethics that rises above all of these many categories of ethics together with their ramifications.

Clarifying Matters That Seem Questionable
Spiritual unity must necessarily come as an introduction to physical peace.
A person should not reject any viewpoint immediately when he senses a contradiction in it—even if it appears to him that it uproots faith.

But he should consider: perhaps the way that it appears to him is due to the haziness of his thought in understanding it. And perhaps by clarifying matters, he will find that it has truth, holiness, and the light of strong faith.

Torah Revealed and Torah in Existence
There is nothing in the world that will not arouse a person’s thoughts.
That arousal is embedded in the universal Creation. From that aspect, everything can be interpreted, and there is nothing meaningless in the world.
As for the Torah, it has been revealed in its luminous character in the light of Divine wisdom. And via its light, everything will shine in the future.
Those people who are wise of heart find Torah in all existence, because everything is the word of Hashem. Nevertheless, there is a graduated difference between revealed light and concealed light.

Differences and Their Transience
Differences exist within the totality of Creation.
The difference between the holy and the mundane, the difference between Israel and the nations—these are facts. Blurring their contour is catastrophic.
Developing a deep understanding and sense of this difference is the source of a fruit that is a vast spirit.

However, after all of these differences, we comprehend with clear knowledge that they are all transient, whereas the elevation of everything to holiness and to brotherhood, to equality and to refinement, is an eternal idea that lives constantly in every noble spirit.
And the ways in which one must be careful in maintaining the differences are flowing and transient, welling forth from temporal life.

The general idea of equality—which is the foundation of the goodness of a person’s heart and his pure love of all creatures—proceeds (in the frameworks of kabbalistic secrets) with the raising of the sparks that are scattered in all the depths of the “husks” and together with the great idea of the transformation of everything to complete and absolute holiness by means of uninterrupted, step-by-step work of lovingkindness, peace, justice, truth and compassion.

A Single Flash of the Light of the Infinite One
A person’s sound, unencumbered reason tells him that one flash of the radiance of the contour of a sparkling of an idea of the light of the Infinite One illuminates the thinking, living, intelligent soul and all worlds immeasurably more and more than all the plenitude of other thoughts that are clear and finite.

However, the degree which the supernal, abstract idea regarding the clarity of this supernal thought is grasped by a person’s intellect, even if it will grasp that in an apophatic way, depends on the quantity and quality of that person’s preparation in good traits and good actions, in much Torah learning, in the fear of heaven and in a sweet love for the Divine radiance, the light of the supernal God, the Source of pleasantness.

The Concealed and the Revealed
When we clearly recognize that which is constrained from being comprehensible, then we discern that the fact that it is stripped of comprehensibility does not constrain a person from being able to use its other parts that are revealed.
That is because if this utterly concealed part would prevent the merely hidden part from possibly being used, human beings would be like the beasts of the field, without knowledge and intelligence.

But the Holy One, blessed be He, performed charity for His world so that spiritual traits are divided into sections and each section has its own level—besides its great and universal level from the aspect of its being bound to the whole.

True Humility That Is Not Displayed
The mind of the truly righteous person is immeasurably humble, because he recognizes the great ugliness of the evil that is absorbed into him: whether from the aspect of the overall evil of the world as long as it has not been entirely purified, whether from the aspect of the essential character of the aspect of evil in his own soul, or whether from the aspect of the weakness of his will and his impermeability to the light of uprightness and justice, which does not shine in many parts of his attributes.

Nevertheless, he does not display his humbleness in a revealed way, and sometimes even “a person’s heart does not reveal something to his own mouth” (Kohelet Rabbah 12:10). There are two reasons for this. One is so that the good aspect in his soul will not be humbled and weakened, and therefore it will not be harmed inadvertently, as in the saying, “When the thorn is removed, the cabbage is harmed”(Bava Kama 92a). And the second is so that he will not take pride in the humbleness itself, and so that his revealed modesty will not arouse too much zealousness.

At any rate, since the One Who distinguishes hearts, blessed be He, knows how far this person’s inner humbleness extends, this person attains all of the virtues associated with modesty. Although, due to aspects of the above-mentioned constraints, he does not bring this quality of his soul from potential to actuality in its entire temperament and beauty, he is in the category of “a person who intended to perform a mitzvah but was prevented from doing so, whom Scripture considers as though he did do so” (Berachot 6a).

Ascent and Descent, Surge and Retreat
Ascents and descents are constant in the circumstances of an individual person and in the circumstances of the entire world. Yet at any rate, the overall movement is a movement of ascent and improvement.

Even at a time of great descent, fluctuations in a situation solely have a value of the waxing and waning of the moon, or the surge and retreat of the sea, or inhalation, which brings the breath into a creature’s interior, and exhalation, which expels the breath from within it, or of wakefulness and sleep, which, although they appear as opposites, both united generate a complete life.

Comprehension and Elevation of the World
When we comprehend how the details of the mitzvot and their branches, and all details of good traits and good ethics, and pleasantness, beauty and Eden, and all holy and pure enjoyments, and all spiritual phenomena in existence, near and far, everything that arises in a person’s mind and imagination, visualization and intellect, are all incorporated into a single overall thought higher than any division of images and higher than any spiritual boundary, we raise the spiritual branches of the world to the root of their existence and their being, and everything rises and is sanctified.

Spiritual Waves
Regarding the source of the spiritual waves in an individual’s soul and in the world—they come because of an inner exertion, as everything exerts itself to become aligned with the outpouring light of the Infinite One.

In a single moment, the light flashes and life spreads, because the will is fulfilled and the good is satiated. This satiety results from coming into alignment with the total goodness of the light of the Infinite One. And a calm spirit flows in all of the trails and ways of life and all existence.

Immediately afterwards, a recognition comes of how dark everything is and lacking all value, compared to the light of the Infinite One, and of how infinite chasms separate the Creator from the created, and how the desired alignment appears to be impossible. Then everything dries up and empties out.

As a result of this depression of spirit and as a result of a deep recognition of the nullity of everything, and a recognition of the all-encompassing nature of the Source of everything and the strength of the supernal reality of the supernal light, that light’s positive existence and clarity fill all the chambers of the three levels of a person’s soul: his nefesh, ruach and neshamah.

The suffering of a person’s paltriness, his total self-nullification, burnishes existence and expands its boundary. And the possibility of aligning with the light of the Infinite One returns to assure this person’s spirit.

The person rises, and the sureness of his soul and the eternity of his life grow stronger. He rises with a supernal elevation—but then he recognizes his brokenness and his depression, and he is broken and despairs. Then his spirit immediately returns and shines again, “racing forward and returning, like the appearance of lightning” (Ezekiel 1:14).

Abraham’s Lovingkindness
Every morning, Abraham’s lovingkindness shines in the world (Zohar 3:204a), and a person’s soul yearns for the light of supernal freedom, for the clear Divine knowledge that comes solely from awareness and love, from a breadth of heart enriched with spiritual delight that possesses a hidden wrath against idols, which depress a person’s spirit, dull his heart, and pollute his body.

Out of profuse love and mercy, and out of a profuse wealth of knowledge and uprightness filled with purity, Abraham paves universal avenues so that nation and man may call out in the name of Hashem (Genesis 12:8).
With a father’s love for his children, Abraham meets with a multitude of nations, and so he is called the “father of a multitude of nations” (Genesis 17:4).

From Abraham, the “head of the cliffs” (Numbers 23:9, Shemot Rabbah 15:7), we encounter the shining light of a fresh love that has not split into particularized rivulets of every statement and law and mitzvah.

Instead, we reach a state where, from the vast power of the outpouring and current of Abraham’s life, he gushes forth streams of exalted faith and desirable rivers, the performance of acts of lovingkindness and righteousness—on the pleasant way of Hashem, and with a constant yearning of soulful connection to the sweet Eden of the flowing forth of pure supernal knowledge, of its the might and splendid lovingkindness.

How good and how pleasant to dwell in this desirable palace, in the mountain where God desired to dwell (cf. Psalms 68:17). And how mighty and formidable is the power of life and goodness that erupts from the soul of Abraham, this “prince of God” (Genesis 23:6), to warrant everything, to elevate and raise everything. Abraham comes from “the day of lovingkindness that accompanies all of the other days, the other attributes,” with the “light of this day,” which is lovingkindness.
We walk in the light of Hashem, in the light of His countenance, from which “the Torah of life and the love of lovingkindness” (siddur) have been given to us.

The Elevation of the Will and of the World
Everything that is related to a person due to his essential, spiritual connection with all existence is connected to his inner will. And when his inner will rises, everything rises with it.
Prayer clarifies a person’s will. When it is elevated, all things included in it (with various connections that relate to reality at its source) are elevated with it.

All of these things are lights of life that flow forth from the Life of worlds. They are scattered in everything. They enter every person’s eating and drinking so as to be made into a mighty, living unit together with him.

From the chasm of the dark imagination, everything rises to the mountains of bright knowledge, which is connected to the righteousness of God, the living God. “You shall serve Hashem your God, and He will bless your bread and your water” (Exodus 23:25).

Eating and the Ascent of “Sparks”
Prior to the ascent of all of the hosts of Hashem—which are the sparks of holiness that relate every day to the depth of a person’s good desire—when they are connected to him via a bodily connection, they lower the level of his will and weaken it, and they themselves remain in their state of darkness behind his back.

Regarding the connection to life of those elements required for life and for health—they are always connected to life with the force of a person’s will as it is filled with the light of infinite wisdom whose supernal understanding has not turned aside from being refined in its Edenic streams. Then the universal life that maintains these elements and everything in them flows in the height of its unclouded might and purity.

As for everything that a person eats and drinks for healing and in order to fortify his failing strength that is required for the functioning of his life, it is intrinsically elevated and lifted. It connects itself to the radiance of the inner desire of the essence of his life. It gives him added beauty and upright light, and it rises with enhanced brightness with the revealing of his desire in his upright prayer.

It Is Impossible Not to Love
It is completely impossible not to love Hashem.

And it is completely impossible that the power of this requisite sweet love will not cause a practical plant to blossom: the love of bringing about, in actuality and practically, everything that relates to the goodness associated with attaining the light of Hashem.
It is impossible not to love the Torah and the commandments, which are so considerably connected to the goodness of Hashem.

It is impossible not to love uprightness and justice, the good and elevated order that brings goodness to all, goodness that is closely connected to the true being of reality and to the thought of the heart in the most elevated way—a relationship that, because of its greatness and its beauty, we call “the desire of Hashem.”
This relationship is something higher than all this and more special than all this. And that satiates the soul of all beings with pleasantness more than anything that any thought can rise to.

It is impossible not to be filled with love for every creature, because the outpouring of the light of Hashem shines in everything, and everything is a revelation of the lovely pleasantness of Hashem. “The kindness of Hashem fills the earth” (Psalms 33:5).

Five Types of Love
To the degree that the righteous person satiates himself with the Divine pleasantness, with yearning, with intellect, with feeling and beauty, so is the entire world filled with calm and breadth, delight and tranquility.

The Prophets and the Sages
In the prophecy of the prophets across the generations, prophecy comes at intervals (with the exception of the prophecy of the master of the prophets, Moses our teacher, of blessed memory).
At the time of its manifestation, prophecy is revealed in the entire might of spirituality, until the prophet’s senses flesh and functions of his body and vital soul are nullified.

However, when the prophecy leaves, its spiritual impressions remain contained in his soul, in keeping with which one can arrange a clear way of conducting oneself in all of the best ways of life, that go along the avenue that has been paved as a result of the manifestation of Hashem’s righteousness in the Torah and ethics, as passed down from generation to generation.
And when not prophesying, the prophet is as filled with bodily vigor as he is with spiritual vigor.
The character of the sages is different.

In them, spiritual manifestation never reaches a supernal intensification that destroys material order. But on the other hand, their spirituality is constantly ongoing. It weakens their material and vital power to a certain extent, and it illuminates their intellectual and ethical light in a moderate measure.

Of course, there is a superior aspect in this as well, because of the joint action of their intellectual and spiritual power, and because of the possibility for constancy. But it lacks the might and clear manifestation that reveal the force of God and magnify the rule of goodness and holiness over the societal community.

Higher Faith and Lower Faith
There are two pathways leading to the revelation of faith: a high way and a low way.
The high way comes from an inner awareness of the great value of Divine faith existing in the world: in personal and societal life, in spiritual, moral and intellectual life.
The clearer this awareness becomes, the more robustly does the sensitivity to faith grow and conquer people’s hearts, giving them heart and refining them.

The broader that this holy way grows the more will goodness increase in the world. And it will not encroach on the boundary of any good ethics, of any rectified order, of any wisdom and intellectual study, of any refined song and any glorious beauty.
Below that stands a vision of faith that comes from a weakness of spirit that critiques and judges exalted matters.

That is harmful in a large amount, although a small amount is beneficial (cf. Gittin 70a). When this lowly faith spreads beyond the boundary appropriate for it—in particular, when it vanquishes a pathway that is so broad that even gifted people filled with the light of spiritual life, who are qualified to go on the way of the supernal holiness of elevated faith, grow careless of that way and lull themselves to sleep on the knees of faith in its lowly state—then from the Divine wisdom a strong mechanism of intellectual and practical awakening is prepared that destroys all of the structures of that lowly faith.
The ruptures at that time are terrible, and the eye that looks on from the outside thinks that supernal holiness has stumbled and fallen. But in truth it has been purified and invigorated.

As a result, people who possess great spiritual power invigorate themselves at that “time to act” (cf. Psalms 119:126) in order to explain the Torah and manifest matters in the light of elevated faith. That builds, in a pleasing and rectified form, everything that had been destroyed because of the excessive spreading forth of the lowly faith that results from a weakness of the soul.
It is clear that a vigorous kernel of elevated and pure faith exists in every soul, even in the soul of the most common man.

The difference between a boor and a sage lies only in the level of the way that they convey faith. The sage conveys the images that elucidate the depth of his soul—to himself and to others—in a way of wisdom and good, elevated intelligence.

As for the boor, although the essential core of his faith, which is the work of heaven, shines with the Divine light and is the secret of the eternal existence of the soul—corresponding to the luz bone in the spine over which no decay and destruction hold sway (Bereishit Rabbah 225:28)—nevertheless, the conveying of his explanations of his faith is lowly because of the lowliness of his awareness.

The more he relies on his logic and the analyses of his heart, which are empty of all intellect and illumination of wisdom, the more he darkens the light of his faith, until at times it is necessary to endeavor so that people with coarse intellects will not engage at all in the inner contents of the spiritual secrets of faith.

It is preferable that they will allow the inner, holy kernel to develop within them by means of their performing acts of goodness and lovingkindness, and by means of their applying themselves to Torah and the mitzvot with simple straightforwardness.

Do Not Disparage the Imagination
Do not view disparagingly the development of the power of the imagination, its might and its lucidity, connected to the imagination’s holiness and its purity, because the imagination is the throne upon which the light of wisdom and supernal life rest.

Do Not Fear Striving for Great Spiritual Levels
A person should not fear great spiritual levels due to his presuming that he is unsuitable for such because of his sins. That is so even when his sins stand beside him in a form of a great darkness between him and the supernal holy light. And that is because “the wonders of He Who is perfect in knowledge” (Job 37:16) are infinitely great, and there is a place on the unique pathway of the righteous where everything is clarified for the good in a wondrous and supernal manner that rises greatly beyond what any idea can conceive.
The foundation of everything is the supernal might of truly clinging to God, which—in the merit of a single righteous person—binds the entire world to the knot of life.

A person’s broadening of his awareness must be constant. He must search for advice on how to increase the light of kindness in such a way that with its growth it will bring about only good, only repair and blessing.

The Delight of the Resurrection and an Even Greater Delight
The wondrous delight of the resurrection of the dead in the light of life that comes from supernal Eden—i.e., from the dew of “the lights of Your dew” (Job 33:30), gladdens the righteous and gives them an unceasing supernal joy, until they consider as nothing the entire interval between the present and that great future, including the tumultuous episodes in between, and they are literally nullified like a small spark before the globe of the sun.
And our forefathers handed us this entire great light when they instituted the blessing in the Shemoneh Esrei prayer on the resurrection of the dead.

But still, the entire greatness and radiance of this supernal delight is considered as nothing in relation to the form of the delight and wholeness of the very highest supernal awareness, that being the secret of Hashem’s desire and His love, to which the righteous are connected and to which the entire soul of Israel clings. The entire essence of the Divine light, which gives life to all creatures and prepares them for the supernal feast, resides there.

And these brilliances of the wondrous delight and the highest supernal awareness are filled constantly with wondrous gladness that is itself filled with glory and Edenic states, with colors each different from the others. And these brilliances pour forth a flow of great rivers and many, mighty seas, one upon the other. And their memory is sweet and pleasant, rectified and accepted. They open the gates of kindness and compassion, of light and salvation forever.

Insights Born from the Intellect
Everything born from the insight of the intellect is an actual reality. The greater the clarity of the insight, the stronger and more efficacious is its reality. And the higher and more encompassing the quality of that insight, the more it enlivens and fructifies the spirit to produce a fruit of life.

That which has an infinitely important quality is an insight into the Divine. And as for that which flows from that insight’s spirit, in keeping with the connection of this matter to its Divine source—the sturdier is its connection to life.

Thus, those who truly cling to God feel the sturdiness of their lives in the Divine thought. And the sturdiness of life strengthens them, refines them and gives them a supernal joy. “I will delight in Hashem, I will exult in the God of my salvation” (Habakkuk 3:18).

Individuation and Unification
In this world, human capabilities proceed to develop their spirituality. That development causes a division of those capabilities into separate domains. And that division into separate domains causes each domain to develop and be completed properly.
But the goal of this division is that all of the various domains will unite in their spirit, just as in truth everything is one and united in the heights of Divine emanation.

The spirit of faith, which requires thought about the Divine, was stronger in earlier generations, because disparate ideas did not branch out so much and everything was included together. In that way, the ideas were closer to the Divine matter. But because they were crowded together in a person’s vessels that receive the thoughts, the ideas emerged blurred.
The light of the world exerts an influence that brings the prisoner out of his confinement and redeems souls from their oppressive straits.

At the outset of this phenomenon, it seems as though the branches are separating from the root. But in truth, they are being blessed by it alone. And with much abundance from above, they will again be united in the unity of the light of the supernal wisdom, which gives life to everything.

With a penetrating contemplation of the secret of this supernal behavior, every wise person will understand how to restore everything to the good root, and he will know that Hashem alone is exalted, and His glory rests upon earth and heaven.

The Nature of the Tzaddik
The righteous are wearied with a spiritual weariness when their faith in themselves diminishes.

Then they think that they are similar to the entire mass of human beings. And even if they imagine themselves to be the more rectified and learned among them, they will not be spared that inner lowliness.
But they must know that the content of their soul is an entirely different, supernal content, and that yearning for the holy light and for clinging to the Divine is demanded of them at every moment.
And they must constantly influence all souls, who derive nourishment from the righteous people’s great and encompassing souls.
The aggregate of such righteous people includes all those to whom, by the nature of who they are, an inner yearning clings for the secrets of the Torah and for the thought of holy wisdom overall.

And although at times their light diminishes, and at times they fall prey to a number of unworthy matters, the verse states in regard to that, “Seven times will the righteous person fall and rise” (Proverbs 24:16).

And even after every such matter that such a person undergoes, he should not remove his faith in the essential holiness of his soul, but he should state clearly, “Know that Hashem has set aside the pious person for Himself; Hashem will hear when I call out to Him” (Psalms 4:4).

A Mitzvah Produces Fruits
A mitzvah produces fruits, and causes lights of holy life to blossom within the soul and in all of the worlds at all times and at every moment.

And when the joy of righteous people intensifies, they feel the blossoming of the holiness of the mitzvot that they and the entirety of Israel have performed in all generations and at all times: how that holiness acts to make new life flower constantly, without any interruption.
“The fruit of a righteous person is a tree of life” (Proverbs 11:30), and the taste of that tree and of its fruit is the same (Succah 35a).

The Initial Sparks of Thought
When a person’s sparking of thought in matters of supernal holiness, of Divine comprehensions, comes to be revealed, it appears first in the form of small points.
And everything is in keeping with a person’s merit, in keeping with the purity of his soul and the greatness of his Torah learning and wisdom—in keeping with them, these points are drawn forth.
And when these points find that the powers of his life are rectified and his character traits are clarified, the process of their drawing forth intensifies.

Souls Filled with Love and Kindness
The higher a soul is in its foundation, the more it feels the oneness that exists in everything. And separations and changes between entities do not cause it to ascribe to anything a state of being that is divided and separated.

In terms of ethics, these souls are filled with love and eternal kindness, and their desire is completely good. They recognize and sense the conduits through which the flow of the light of life proceeds from one being to another. And the closer a person is to their circle, the more their conduit broadens to benefit that person.

At times, a supernal light that encompasses in its oneness all of existence, that is higher than all of the conduits, shines upon them. This power of imagination is the holy of holies, and it brings goodness and blessing into the world. And when the unitive thought intensifies, the light of kindness and forgiveness grows manifest, and transgressions and sins are erased.

And when someone approaches the circle of such a good righteous person, the points of goodness hidden in the depths of the former’s soul shine and are emphasized, and the evil is entirely annihilated.

These righteous people are the foundations of the world, who judge the entire world favorably and shine the light of kindness on every being, who love to justify people and hate to condemn them. They are the true students of Abraham our father, who go in his ways.

At times, the light of the kindness within them is so great that it cannot appear in their deed, and due to its great influence, they feel weakness in their bodies, because by its nature materiality is liable to judgments and strictures. Nevertheless, they draw forth the light of life and might from the source of supernal kindness.

Although the world cannot receive their light as it is, just as the world is unworthy of making use of the light of the first day of Creation, nevertheless, the world is perfumed at present from the derivatives of this light.

Spirituality in the Time of the Temple and Afterwards
When the spirit of the nation is strong, it does not require extensive spiritual sustenance, because it is entirely well-rooted in its spiritual root, and its might shines well, and all of the deeds that it performs are watered by the dew of a sturdy spiritual life in which the supernal content is alive.

The link between the components of the spirit of the nation is great and strong due to the vast wholeness of its unity, such that the actions performed in the house of the life of the nation—i.e., its Temple—involving the Divine services, the sanctified songs and the entire Divine splendor and magnificence with which it is constantly full all affect the spirit of the nation in actuality overall, and enhance the spirit of each of its individuals.

The spirit need only be guarded from destructive ethical and societal harm such as idol worship and the grave transgressions of an individual such as murder, adultery, perversion of justice, and the unfettered corruption of traits.
When these are guarded against, the nation’s strong spirit brings the light revealed in holiness and in the Temple into the inner being of every individual.

But as a consequence of the weakening of the nation and the descent of its spirit, the nation requires constant strengthening: a great deal of Torah learning with the establishing of set times for the people as a whole, and constant application for its individuals, a schedule of frequent prayer, and all of the spiritual services of blessings and thanksgivings.
All of these are required in order to strengthen the nation’s spiritual disposition, so that the physical nature of reality will not harm it.

And when this matter [of focusing on the interiority] will reach its vigor, the demand for the reinforcement of the inner spirit will come together with a complaint against the frequency of that necessary sustenance and its various forms.

[But] in truth, the more that the inner spirit of the life of the nation pulses, the more necessary it is to explain to everyone that all of the details of strengthening brought about by the spiritual nurturing in their measures have a good effect as well upon the state of the nation’s overall spirit as it awakens.

Idea to Deed, and Deed to Idea
The proper order is for a person’s spirit to first be filled with thoughts and feelings.
And that which his inner thinking cannot sustain must necessarily break forth in the form of words. Those are the foundation of prayers and thanksgivings, learning and reading.

And that for which the level of verbal revelation is insufficient, because of the vast flow of its light, must be crystallized in deeds, which communicate with their allusions and actualize with their might the entire ideational content of the person’s elevated feelings and thoughts.
When reality exists in such a form, the world is rectified, and a straight light flows down onto everything.
But when the universal character is blemished, we must bring forth the content from below to above.
Then a person’s actions arouse his verbal level, and his speech arouses his ideas.

The light rises with heaviness, although at times it is helped because, in the midst of its proceeding, an idea suddenly awakens, which leads to the phenomenon of a straight light being sent down from its source. That causes the flow [downward] of a treasury of verbal thought, which in turn results in an awakening of deed.
Then matters become balanced, and harmony and gladness are revealed in the holy Temple.

The Nation of Israel in the Context of the Other Nations
The constitution of the nation of Israel must be examined to see whether the overall human character in the composition of mankind exists in the constitution of the nation of Israel as it does in all other nations, and the Israelite constitution that makes it unique is built on top of that—or whether, from heel to head, everything about the nation of Israel is unique.
To further this examination, we must make use of various sources: Torah, intellectual, historical, mystical, phenomenological, poetic, and sometimes political and economic as well.

Apparently, at first it was arranged that the constitution of humanity would be completed in its entirety, and then as an addition and enhancement the unique nation’s beautiful spirit would be revealed with holy splendor to that nation.

But things went wrong, and the spirit of mankind sank so much overall that the mundane could not be made into a foundation for the holy, lest it damage the holy. And so the exile in Egypt had to come as an iron crucible, refining the aspect of mankind in Israel until Israel became a new creature and its mundane constitution became entirely obscured.
Then the Israelite nation was born in an instant via the human kernel into a constitution that is entirely Israelite from head to heel: Jacob [the heel] and Israel [the head].

The Soul That Is Truly Great
The soul that is truly great is so expansive that the entire fullness of the finite world does not suffice for it, and it spreads through supernal, spiritual, intellectual worlds, where rivers of eternal refinements exist.
People with such souls live a life that is forever. “I will dwell in Your tent forever” (Psalms 61:5).

And they cause the flow of their spirit to flow to all generations, and their statements are constantly spoken in their name. And in addition, the foundation of their finite life rises above perceptible boundaries. “He causes the lips of the sleeping to speak” (Song of Songs 7:10).

Those Who Are Small of Faith
Those who are small of faith are the fools of the world—because, what does faith pertain to?

It pertains to the wonders of the goodness of the great light of the Infinite One. And what would lead a person to delineate a boundary and amplitude, saying that until a certain point he will believe, and no more?

Therefore, the entire foundation of spiritual life and its supernal might depends upon the power of a faith that has no end and culmination at all, a faith in the Source of the foundation, the Source of everything, without measure and amplitude.
