That faith arouses all of the life and all of the goodness in the world. It devolves in a number of devolutions. It descends and is clothed in a number of garments and rationales until it becomes the content of a faith that accompanies life, that establishes foundations for holy religiosities, and engenders characteristics of the fear of heaven and Divine wisdom.

Even Praiseworthy Leavening Is Forbidden on Passover
Faith without straits: that is the inheritance of Israel, who began to emphasize it with the exodus from Egypt, and impressed it into the blend of their lives at that moment of haste.

That supernal power returns and shines at every season of the holiday of Passover by means of the “bread of healing,” the “bread of faith,” the eating of matzah, which is crowned at the nullifying of leavened bread and its burning on the eve of Passover.
There is no room for any judgment and intellectual boundary that has been darkened by the turbid spirit of any created being.

Nor is there place on Passover for the leavening that is otherwise always kosher and praiseworthy, as in the fact that “fortunate is the judge who delays (lit., leavens) his verdict” (Midrash Tanchuma, Mishpatim 6; Sanhedrin 35a).

There is no place for that on Passover because the fundamental matter that gives life to everything transcends all adjudication and judgment. Instead, everything shines in an instant with a flow of the great light of “great fear: that is the revelation of the Divine Presence” (Haggadah).

The Improvement of the World
The improvement of the world overall and the improvement of the Congregation of Israel in particular causes the time of the strengthening of will in the world to approach and, with that, the strengthening of the body for elevated purposes, which corresponds to earlier generations’ programs of fasting and self-affliction.
Although the complete improvement has not yet emerged from potential to actual, it is nevertheless increasingly coming to light.

And as a result of a complete unifying of all of the groups of the people of Israel, the binding of all thoughts and feelings, high and low, in them and in the world, and the appearance among the masses of the light of the secrets of the Torah in rectified garments, the world will be prepared for the supernal light of the complete improvement of the light of the positive will in its mighty ascents, until the supernal governance of “As you decree, so will it be established for you” (Job 22:28).

Strengthening the Body for the Sake of the Nation
The exercise that the youth of Israel perform in the land of Israel to strengthen their bodies in order to be sons sturdy in strength for the nation perfects the spiritual power of the supernal righteous people who engage in unifications of holy names to increase the prominence of the Divine light in the world. And the revelation of one light does not stand at all without its colleague.

“And David made for himself a name” (Samuel 2 8:13) because, on the one hand, “David [was able to] perform judgment and justice for all his nation” (ibid. 15) [as, correspondingly,] “Joab, son of Zeruyah, was in charge of the army” (ibid. 16; Sanhedrin 49a).
And Abner was punished because he had “made the blood of his youths sport, telling Joab, ‘Let the youths get up now and play before us’ (Samuel 1 2:14)” (Jer. Peah 1:1).

But when young people engage in sport to strengthen their power and their spirit on behalf of the might of the nation in its entirety, that holy service raises the Divine Presence higher and higher, like its ascent via the songs and praises that David, king of Israel, recited in the book of Psalms.
Via the righteous people’s supernal intentions, the inner soul rises, and via the actions that sturdy the body of the elite few for the sake of the all, external spirituality rises.
And together, these perfect all of the holy structures.

Refining the Admixtures of Traces of Impurity
And do not be surprised if there are failings in the course of the lives of those engaged in fortifying the physical and in all of the earthly strengthening that takes place in the nation of Israel, because even the manifestation of Divine inspiration must be refined from admixtures of traces of impurity that mingle into it, and it grows continuously purified, sanctified and clarified, it redeems itself from its exile, until it comes to the entirety of the way of the righteous, and a radiant light “grows increasingly brighter until the day is full” (Proverbs 4:8).

Holiness and Remembering
The more that a person’s tendency toward holiness increases, the more the oneness of ideation and the unity of all powers gain strength in him.
And via that oneness, every thought in the treasury of his spirit is intensely connected to the entirety of thoughts, and forgetfulness does not rule over him.
But when he is distanced from aspiring for holiness, his ideas and powers scatter. Then his every thought blurs its counterpart and repels it, and forgetfulness increases.
And when Amalek will be erased, the power of forgetfulness will be eliminated from the world. “You shall surely erase the remembrance of Amalek” (Deuteronomy 25:9)—and then “you will not forget.”

That is because, when the Name is whole and the throne is whole (cf. Rashi on Isaiah 12:2), everything is a oneness with the ultimate connection. And memory with the light of clear awareness shines in all its goodness and radiance. And there is no place for any weakness, because “the right hand of Hashem is elevated” (Psalms 118:16) and “does valiantly” (ibid.), and all of the thoughts incorporated in the twenty-four kad books of the Torah are one with all of their corresponding vital forces.

“And I will make your windows of jasper kadkhoda and your gates of carbuncle stones, and all your border of precious stones, and all of your children will be learned of Hashem, and much peace for your children” (Isaiah 54:12-13).

Holy Literature
Prayer, outcry and repentance from the depth of the heart, and the manifestation of repentance in actuality upon deeds in their rectified state must necessarily precede every appearance of the light of a higher understanding.

It is impossible for a truly significant literature to come into being and appear with a light of life in the world except by means of the manifestation of the light of repentance, which renews the face of the entire world.

The truth is that the radiance of the literature of the future appears with a spark of awareness that precedes the light of repentance. That awareness fills a person’s spiritual might with complete freedom and supernal, exalted liberty, leading to perfect repentance, which draws in its wake redemption after the arrival of forgiveness, both inward and external. Healing, income, the ingathering of the exiles and the return of authority to judges and advisors—who are the pillars of literature and of its founders—strides forward.
Evil is subjugated and righteousness is elevated.

The heart of the nation begins to beat with the strength of its life in the direction of Jerusalem, and the blossoming of the crown of the perfected kingdom appears. And every desire of the heart is fulfilled via the prayer of the upright, which is suffused with the will of the Life of worlds, “Who spoke and the world come into being” Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur prayer.

Rebounding from Material Lusts
When the tendencies of a person’s material lusts first begin to be revealed, they appear in a manner that is near the ideal and they are incorporated into holiness. But when they induce the person to surrender to their swift and driving stream until his freedom and the purity of his independent control over himself are nullified, they become polluted. The person dives into the depths of the darkness, and all of the good powers of his self are taken captive by a coarse and tawdry materiality.

The darkness of his polluted thinking and the lack of clarity in his understanding of existence—the connectedness of all of the goodness of existence up to the supernal state of its origin—which extend to the darkness of idolatry and its branches, those being heresy, forgetting God, and all of the compartments of dark places that can and cannot be called by names, gain strength, and they seize his soul with its noble powers inn their net.

When a person’s mind grows settled, and Torah and prayer, the elevation of awareness and the elevation of his will exercise their effect on him, he again rises from his depths. He brings with himself portions of the aliveness and the feelings that he had come close to specifically because of his fall.
And when he returns, they return with him. They rise and are elevated with his elevations, and his soul becomes brighter and stronger.

And the light of the life of the world that relates to his portion in existence adds great wealth. Eternal joy grows continuously broader, and greatness of breadth of mind crowns his head with intellectual purity and noble Divine desire. Love for the worlds and their creatures and supernal clinging—along with the wholeness of all—to the source of delights, which is the root of temporary and this-worldly delight, continuously grows stronger within him.

And a world full of the gestation of the world and full of eternity shines ever more in the splendor of their beauty. And the person becomes the treasury of goodness and life for every creature, and the preciousness of the eternal God forever.

The Power of Imagination
The power of imagination of people with great insight is very great and exalted, and it is connected to the most universal visions in existence.

Commensurate with their spiritual might and personal purity, the power of imagination enables them to visualize supernal and exalted visualizations, via which the light of supernal truth is revealed with revelations that no rational intellect can attain.

Eras of the Comprehensive and of the Particular
The manifest stance of a person’s spirit that comes from the brightness of comprehensive conceptions—which also influence the state of his will—requires his bodily and psychological health to be whole.
That stance is a light that was revealed in the First Temple. It was at the foundation of prophecy and Divine inspiration.

It is a power that was reduced at its source and that increased in its branches due to a wealth of learning and profuse halachahs. Then practical content and exactitude began to gain ascendancy. The comprehensive light hid, and then health was not so requisite.

Now the light of the messiah is sparking. And when we safeguard the property of particularity that has already accumulated, together with the appropriate addition to it from every aspect for the good, the world again demands to be improved by those who improve the comprehensive, who unite a clear awareness with a heart that feels and desires great and noble things.
Therefore, might is required, and the function of the health of the body and the soul begins to be demanded with all forcefulness.
And that function has hope of growing great, rising and being elevated in its amount and in its quality, and rising to the heights of supernal holiness and might, of “strength to God” (Psalms 68:35).

The Propensity Revealed in the Congregation of Israel
In supernal righteous people, the entire propensity of whose desire and all of the ideas of whose hearts are filled with the sanctity of exalted goals that bring vast blessing to the entire world, this propensity that is revealed in them is revealed in the Congregation of Israel close to its true redemption.
This revelation appears at first specifically in fallen souls in the Congregation of Israel, who are accentuated in its corporate body, comparable to a person’s limbs of action.
Included among these ideas are also unclarified dreams and aspirations.

Elevated, Fallen Souls
The souls through which the insolence at the time of the “heels of the messiah” is revealed are those that are very high in their core root, but which have correspondingly become very lowly in their external self-expressive content.
The totality of their fusion with the whole is very excellent, but in their individuality they need much purifying and refining.

The prayer of the righteous people of the generation is directed to rescuing these people from Gehennom—whether those righteous person know those secrets and have them in mind, or whether they proceed simply, with their intent for the sake of heaven overall, with a love of goodness, kindness, compassion and the pleasantness of Hashem, with a love and fear that are bound to the Torah and to wisdom in accordance with their level.

The Inner Manifestation and the Mind
The inner manifestation binds itself to the clear mind, and the two of them together constitute the spiritual might in the world.

We Must Make Many Vessels
We must make many vessels for the inner light: vessels of deeds, of ideas, of inner and outer images.
The broadest vessels are what we make by means of the Torah on all of its levels.

Indeed, additions to the physical and spiritual power of Israel, the power of its bodily health and might, the power of its wealth and breadth of mind—the overall glory in the nation’s unique qualities with an inner and piercing examination of the uniqueness of its soul, which is distinct from all of the nations—all of these are instruments that prepare worthy vessels for supernal light that brings life and blessing to the world.

Easy-Going Learning
At times, a person’s learning must be expressly easy-going, fluttering over topics like a dove hovering over its nest, so as not to submerge the supernal radiance, which is higher than any individual matter, into the particularity of limitations.

With that, the comprehensive light, which radiates within the midst of all of the details, emerges and appears in a great light. “And the heart of the sage knows a time and judgment” (Ecclesiastes 8:5).

As Understanding Enters into Details
When overall comprehension penetrates into the analysis of details, it relinquishes something of its level, and it bends over to nurse its children.

Contra Those for Whom the Desire for Life Is a Disaster
The wicked are unable to look at the light of kindness at its source in supernal wisdom. And so for them the desire for life is merely a disaster—whether for themselves or for the world and all of existence. And for them, all that can be rescued from the sexual drive that brings life into existence is its lustful husk.
And that is the vileness of the foreskin and the root of the impurity of lewdness.

For them, the essence of life is nothing worthwhile, and so the drive for bloodshed is great in comparison to the drive for illegitimate sexuality, and both are intertwined with the drive for idolatry, which is “other gods,” harsh judgments, blind and evil, driven by an errant will that tends to do evil.

But righteous people are the opposite of all that. They reveal the light of supernal kindness in its being, and in the sexual drive they see supernal holiness in the heights of wisdom, shining in kindness and filled with the richness of the dew of knowledge.
And life is immeasurably precious because it wells from the source of supernal preciousness, the hidden good, which vanquishes all eternities of eternities.

And kindness and love for people comes in place of the drive for bloodshed. And splendor of holiness and “walking in modesty” (Micah 6:8)—with inner knowledge girded with the might of a flame of holiness—is in place of the drive for illegitimate sexuality.

And they are both intertwined with the source of supernal knowledge, which nurses from the eternal kindnesses in the hidden thought, the source of all delights, of the purified lights, which develop all goodness and all generosity, all beauty, all might and joy, and all supernal pleasantness in all of the worlds.

When the Soul Rises by Itself
Sometimes, the soul rises by itself with its own qualities, without the person engaging in any service that can be sensed.
And all of that comes about because this was preceded by many levels of service—intellectual, emotional and material—in the light of Torah and awareness.

And afterwards, the soul takes delight in its good situation and draws forth the dew of lights and supernal tranquility, such as the holiness of the delight of the Sabbath, which is “an exemplar of the world-to-come” (Berachot 57b) and which is revealed to the righteous and the upright of heart every day.

And just as on the Sabbath, Gehennom is annulled (Zohar 2:150b) and no sin that a person committed holds him back, so too the illumination of the supernal Sabbath raises a person above every transgression and sin, and the richness of the supernal delight rests upon him.

Relaxation and Space
Sometimes, a person must consider that he should not be pursued constantly by his this-worldly and Torah learning obligations, but he should allow himself relaxation and space, so that his soul may rise by itself, and spread out on its inner excursion through the richness of life that is stored within all deeds and learning, within all service and prayer.

And after such a respite, which contains the holiness of the Sabbath, the soul strives to return with much power to spiritual and this-worldly service, all of whose details will be fresh, drawing from the source of life of full knowledge, illuminated by the light of life.

The Human Soul and the Angel
The speech of the ministering angels is weighted to the natural. It comes from their stream of a steady spiritual life.
And the story-telling of souls is weighted to artifice, to an intentional thought. It comes from the source of free will and inner contemplation.
The friendship of angels with souls elevates life to the ultimate supernal height. “You who sit in the gardens, friends heed your voice; let me hear!” (Song of Songs 8:13).
And when the Torah unites with a person’s soul, and all of the Torah’s expressions are transformed into his inner nature, then he is clothed in angelic being.

There are two angels in the firmament who are the pattern for two Talmudic sages on the earth (Bava Batra 75a). “The ministering angels—who are they? The rabbis” (Nedarim 20b). And the Torah sages in Babylon are similar to the ministering angels (Kiddushin 72a).

The superiority of Elijah is that he contains two acquisitions together in a perfected form: the soulful and the angelic. He reveals secrets of the Torah to us. He gives us tidings of salvation by Hashem, and the joy of the redeemed. “How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of the herald who proclaims peace, heralding good, proclaiming salvation, saying to Zion, Your God has manifested His kingdom” (Isaiah 52:7).
And the nation proceeds upright with two statures (Bava Batra 75a): the stature of the soul and the stature of the angel. And they are both revealed in actuality.

When they shine, first there exists “I broke the pegs of your yoke,” and then “I led you upright” (Leviticus 26:13). “And He will bring us to peace from the four corners of the earth” (siddur), by means of Elijah who rises with four flights (Berachot 4b). “Quickly lead us upright to our land, because You are a God Who implements salvations” (siddur). These are two salvations: the salvation of the stature of the soul and the salvation of the stature of the angel, “the seed of man and the seed of beast” (Jeremiah 31:26, Chullin 5b).

The Aspect of Good in Wicked People
When a person bonds with lowly souls of renegades and wicked people, he is damaged.
But if there is something good in them, and he intends to bond only with the aspect of good in them, then if his power is adequate, the wicked person rises.

And even in regard to looking at the face of a wicked person, which is forbidden (Megillah 28a), if that wicked person has aspects of good in him, and the onlooker intends with his looking only to gather the good, it appears that there is something of a mitzvah in this.

And even when a wicked person has some connection to a righteous person in a way that is loving, the righteous person’s prohibition against looking at the wicked person is removed, because by means of the wicked person’s connection to the righteous person, it is considered as though the wicked person already has a good portion.
Elisha said to Jehoram son of Ahab, “If I had not raised up the face of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, I would not gaze at you and I would not look at you” (Kings 2 3:14).

That implies that as a result of Elisha’s raising of the face of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, who was associated with Jehoram, Elisha gazed at Jehoram as well and looked at him, and he was not concerned for the prohibition against looking at the face of a wicked person, a prohibition that we learn from this verse.

Holy Eating
When we eat for the sake of our material appetite, our sadness intensifies, as in the hidden meaning of the verse, “those who eat the bread of sadness” (Psalms 127:2).

That is because the spiritual sparks in the food, which were capable of rising, descend. And when they are sad at their having descended, the person eating feels their sadness as a result of the interchange of a number of ways of feeling and transpositions of spiritual letters, until the sad feeling is recognized in a psychological disclosure within himself.

But when one eats in holiness and intensifies the supernal goal of attaining purity and clarity of the soul, the happy spirit and joy of the person eating is enhanced as a result of the joy of the spiritual sparks that have risen.
With their joy, his soul that raises them and rejoices with them shines as well. And his heart feels this via a number of pathways and various conduits, and the gladness of Hashem overtakes him.

And so “Boaz ate and he drank, and his heart was glad” (Ruth 3:7). “What is the meaning of ‘and his heart was glad’? In words of Torah” (Yalkut Shimoni, Ruth 604). That is because, besides the fact that the propensity of the heart to intensify the spirituality associated with raising the vitality hidden in foods leads a person to spiritual desire, which is fulfilled with the love for the Torah and learning it, in addition the sanctified content of this holy eating is itself words of Torah. “This is the table that is before Hashem” (Ezekiel 41:22; Pirkei Avot 3:3).

Growth as a Result of Damaging Viewpoints
There are viewpoints that necessarily, in accordance with a person’s nature, cause the spread of harmful consequences, although they themselves are useful and true.
To deal with this, something was created in a person’s spirit that battles for his existence and opposes these viewpoints, so that he will not be harmed by their spreading branches.

And the battle is protracted until the person attains a more supernal might that comes from his spiritual source. And then he feels that his bearing will not at all fear the spread of those viewpoints that he has battled against.

The very power that strengthens his spirit is given to him by the battle itself, and so he knows how to deeply appreciate the value of the battle. And he knows how wretched he would have been had he not battled against the expansion that harmed him then.
Afterwards, he comes with the contents of a vitality of courage and he accommodates the viewpoints against whose spread he had battled.

But just as the person is elevated, so are his spiritual concepts elevated. And so although those viewpoints themselves appear to be the same viewpoints that he had battled, in truth it is not so. They are similar to each other only in keeping with their exterior expressions, but from the aspect of their inner level they are distinct, like the distinction between the holy and the mundane, and between light and dark.

As for the fact that he had distanced them then, he finds that he had distanced them justifiably, and as for the fact that he draws those viewpoints close after they have been elevated, he draws them close justifiably.
And it is precisely in the rejected viewpoints that now appear proper that we find a very vigorous and holy dew of life.

A Person Great in Thought
The greater a person is in thought, the more connected are the parts of his soul and all of the levels of his life with each other, and his power of speech and all of his movements are connected in a greater weave, sensed with an inner sense in his entire interiority and, commensurate with that level, in all existence.
It is entirely impossible that an original thinker would permit himself to engage in empty speech and mundane conversation. All of his words are necessarily filled with Torah and knowledge.

Even Vague Knowledge Is Valuable
Even a vague knowledge of the secrets of the Torah is of great value.

That is because everything is founded on the supernal ability, which has no end and limit. And everything that is beautiful and wondrous is a revelation of spiritual manifestation—on which, in one form or another, the light of the Life of all life rests.

Indeed, matters rise especially high commensurate with the elevation of a person’s holiness of wisdom, counsel, spiritual might and practical and mental holiness, until he attains the illumination of the manifestation of the imagination shining in the light of the vigorous spirituality above it. “In His palace, everything says, ‘Honor!’” (cf. Psalms 29:9).

The Knowledge Possessed by Holy People
The knowledge possessed by holy people is the foundation of the spiritual illumination that appears in the world in all hearts.
These holy people, pure of thought and idea, unite in their inner perception with the spiritual goodness that fills everything.

Everything that is revealed to them is a supernal revelation and manifestation of light that adds life and might—eternal life and spiritual might—and that enhances the entire world with the scent of its perfumes.

From the source of Torah—which has illuminated the world from the height of the Divine, supernal illumination as it folds together spiritual goodness with physical goodness, the temporary with the eternal, the ethical with the practical, the individual with the communal, the detailed particularity with the universal cosmic—lights of life constantly well forth, vitalizing all entities that touch them and guarding those entities so that they will remain pure.
A deep gaze and a moral accord will necessarily connect with each other in those people who are fit to attain that state.

And those people absorb the light of the world that is immersed in all souls and establish it in a complete unit. And then these people appear in their light by means of the lifelines of their existence and their company, as they send forth their will and the greatness of their spiritual self via their humility and their love for all creatures, for the entire treasury of life and goodness for all.
These straight-hearted people are pathways that transmit light and life to every created being.

They are vessels for the illumination of the light of the Life of worlds. They are servants of Hashem and those who perform His word (cf. Psalms 103:21), that are His angels who do His will (cf. Psalms 103:20), vivifying everyone who inclines to death, strengthening every weak person, awakening every person who is asleep.
And they call in the name of Hashem, God of the world, Who tells every created being: “Be alive and joyous for all the good. Arise and be elevated, higher and higher.”

The Overall Light and Details of Light
A person visualizes supernal spiritual imagery in accordance with his state of awareness. What he sees is in the way of a general light.

As for all of the details that arise in his mind from his feelings and from his conceptions, they are only sparkling details emerging from a general imagery that cannot be represented. These details are comparable to the stars in the firmament.
Tefillin prepare a Jew’s body and the powers of its life to receive a general spiritual illumination through which details will shine well.
Insights that transcend conceptualization—which differ for every individual in accordance with his level—and that are grasped only for a flash are comparable to tefillin.

On Sabbaths and festivals, tefillin are not worn. An intellectual illumination shines so that general illuminations change into details. These, which glow all the days of the week only as a general sign, are themselves the sign of the Sabbath or festival that replaces tefillin, and through them details are emphasized. On the Sabbath and festivals, one should not add a general inclusiveness that hides and swallows up details. But on a mundane day, that general inclusiveness assists the emphasizing of the details.

Everything Fits Together
Sometimes a person thinks that there are thoughts that contradict his thoughts, and as a result he cannot grow settled in his mind and be faithful to his ideas. And that can lead to the fall of his spirit and carelessness.
A person must be aware that every contradiction is only apparent and limited to specific conditions, but in truth everything fits together and everything is united.

And then he will be happy and cheerful in the portion of the blending of his individual thoughts, and he will strive constantly to broaden them and to purify them until they will be filled with light, filled with clear and significant knowledge, and close to exalted feelings that pour gladness and goodness on him and on everything besides him in all that he touches, spiritual and practical.

Visualizing Supernal Wisdom and Supernal Justice
When a person is in a great state of thought, he visualizes the spirituality of supernal wisdom and supernal justice, and all of their sources overall, and he visualizes everything from Torah and wisdom in the role of their wings that emerge from them—[kabbalistically speaking, as the hairs of the head in [the realm of] wisdom, and of the beard in [the realm of] justice.

The Fear of Seeing
Every sin brings a diminution of knowledge, because of a person’s inner fear of looking at the freedom of clear knowledge.
And repentance is what opens the gates of understanding broadly.

Ten Stages of Thought
We must divide the workings of thought into specific parts.
One: Review of ideas and feelings that are already known.
Two: Their purification and clarification.
Three: Their arrangement and relationship to each other in a proper form.
Four: Additional innovation in each of them.
Five: Adding overall illumination to that which arises from the assembly of all of them together.
Six: Additions of new ideas and feelings from the Source of knowledge and feeling.
Seven: Bonding of this addition to that which was already stored.
Eight: New phenomena that are engendered by the bonding mentioned above.
Nine: A supernal spiritual elevation that emerges from the totality of all of these phenomena.
Ten: A complete world-outlook that comes from all of the spiritual factors mentioned above.

The Nature of the People of Israel
The national tendency of Israel is “a field that Hashem has blessed” (Genesis 27:27). Although it does not yet possess complete growths due to the great desolation of the exile, it is capable, via its spiritual and practical work, of having all of the good growths in the world sprout in it and of having great and supernal souls that illuminate the entire world with their glory go forth from its influence.
And there exists, in contrast to that, a national tendency of the nations that is barrenness and desert, and that cannot grow good plants by any means.
And pernicious plants like the vine of Sodom, the poison wine of serpents (Deuteronomy 32:33) and bitter grape clusters (ibid. 32)—is their lack not preferable to their existence?
Everything in them is absolute lack and absolute destruction, and those “nations will be surely destroyed” (Isaiah 60:12).

However, the influence of the holy that is mixed into the national tendency of Israel refreshes those human tendencies overall and returns them to the good, until they too attain an elevation, and they will be capable, by means of the closeness of their bond to Israel, to blossom spiritually.

“Desert and wasteland shall rejoice over them, and the plain shall rejoice and blossom like a rose” (Isaiah 35:1). All of that will come about as a result of the complete redemption of Israel that will soon arrive.

The Waters from Ein Eitam
Ein Eitam is the highest location in the land of Israel (Zevachim 54b).

David and Samuel considered building the Temple there, until others proved from Scripture that it must be lowered a little, in order to fulfill the verse, “the Temple will dwell between Benjamin’s shoulders” (Deuteronomy 33:12). “And there is no part of an ox more beautiful than between its shoulders” (Sifrei and Rashi on Deuteronomy 33:12).
Apparently, Ein Eitam remained in the realm of the mundane. However, the mikveh for the cohen gadol on Yom Kippur used water transported from Ein Eitam (Shabbat 145b).

That mikveh was in the loft of the Parvah Chamber. “Parvah was the name of a Persian sorcerer” (Yoma 35a), and that sorcery is the darkest aspect of evil, the blasphemous, about which a person may not learn (Shabbat 75a) even if he wishes to do so in order to understand and to teach.

Nevertheless, that too can be brought into a supernal inclusiveness and fulfillment of a universal need that purifies with its inclusiveness and prepares for the highest holy service—which, at the apogee of its holiness, vanquishes all destroying forces and establishes the world on the basis of the holiness of its purity. “Indeed, the world is established and it will not waver” (Psalms 93:1).

In the rabbinic traditions, the word shor, “ox” has the numerical value of the word ya’ar, “forest,” “in which rustle all predatory animals” (Psalms 104:20), which are outside the structure of this world and that to come, which latter is built with the first two letters of Hashem’s name, yod-hey. These predatory animals only receive their influence from the latter two letters of Hashem’s name, vav-hey, with which this world was created. That is prior to the supernal light appearing in its might, when the sun has not yet shone but when instead “You make darkness and it is night” (ibid.).

But the purifying thought anticipates the salvation brought about by the Life of worlds of a day that is “neither day nor night; and it will be that at the time of evening there will be light” (Zechariah 14:7).

When the Doors of Repentance Are Apparently Locked
There is a person who truly desires to repent, although how he might do so is deeply concealed from him, since he apparently finds the doors of repentance locked before him—whether because of obstacles caused by his sins between himself and God or, even more, because of obstacles caused by his sins between himself and others, such as outright theft or doubtful theft, a stolen item that he has consumed or has not consumed (Chullin 89a). His mind is in a turmoil, and he is immersed in anguish and frantic thought, an inner shame that holds him back from all good.

But if he will nevertheless strengthen himself with an illumination of wisdom and with doing good, he is assured that he will attain absolute and complete repentance that will bring healing to the entire world (Yoma 86a) and that will lead to universal forgiveness for every sin of all Israel, for its every individual.

A Preciousness That Is Revealed Only to Hashem
The purpose of serving Hashem is to produce in this world a complete quality that is such a precious active agent that its preciousness is revealed solely to Hashem.

In order to produce this quality and all of its branches, we must dedicate ourselves to all goodness and uprightness, and to all deeds of the Torah and serving Hashem, and all of their particular details.

And the more that the human being—as a whole and as an individual—rises, the more some part of the preciousness of that quality is revealed to him, which he actualizes by means of the flow of his life and his practical and spiritual deeds.

And so too his soul, the might of his spirit and his inner gladness grow together with his trembling and his yearning, in order to increase service and improvement: “To inform you of the beauty of words of truth, to respond with words of truth to those who send you” (Proverbs 22:21).

The Light of Hashem in a Faithful Heart
Since no thought can contain the Divine itself, therefore every thought connected to the knowledge of this exalted fact and to faith in it is a vessel with which to receive the light of Hashem.
Therefore, the Divine light exists in every faithful heart, commensurate with that heart’s uprightness and sincerity.

The Supernal Effect in One’s Lie of Learning Torah
When a person engages in much Torah learning, that connects supernal holiness with his spirit, even if he does not fully comprehend the material.

Sometimes it has a supernally good effect on him, even when he does not know the simple meaning of what he has learned, but he is thirsty to attain the word of Hashem, to learn a great deal, and he slakes his thirst with much learning, and then his soul rises.

And when he learns the secrets of the Torah, although he does not understand the details of the material and it appears to him as though he is dealing with imagery that distresses his spirit and his spirit’s feelings that yearn for comprehensible matters, nevertheless, after he learns, the light appears to him, and he is in the category of “a person who engages in Torah learning at night: the Holy One, blessed be He, draws a thread of kindness upon him by day. As the verse states, ‘By day Hashem will command His kindness, and at night His song is with me’ (Psalms 42:9)” (Chagigah 12b).

Grandness
Sometimes, we need not fear grandness at all, because it elevates a person to accomplish great things.
And humility is entirely based on such holy grandness.

The Righteous People Who Cling to Hashem
There are some righteous people who feel an inner thirst to be crowned in tefillin the entire day, for whom wearing tefillin at the time of morning prayers does not suffice.

They are righteous people for whom clinging to the Divine in a revealed way in their spirit is their abiding measure, and not only from time to time. And the entire day, they pray in the interiority of their spirit.

For these righteous people, who are the foundations of the world, and these supernal sages, factors may come about that hinder them to a degree from bringing from potential to actual the desire of their heart with a revelation of supernal holiness and clinging from potential to actual, and sometimes as well their yearning to wear tefillin the entire day will not succeed because of a number of obstacles. Nevertheless, the inner ardor in their soul for the light of the tefillin shines a great deal in the world, and the light of kindness spreads in the world through them to increase pardon, forgiveness and great graciousness.
They are those who truly love the people of Israel, those whose spirit thirsts for salvation from Hashem and for the building of the land of Israel.

They tend to kindness for all and they judge all sinners favorably, even the greatest heretics and willful rebels, because they see in the sincerity of their own spirit the spark of goodness that is hidden in every spirit—and, how much more, in the spirits of Israel, and most of all in the spirit of those who wave the banner of love for the nation overall. And these righteous people tend to goodness and uprightness, which are very meritorious.

And the content of the natural Divine clinging, which is the level of the holiness of tefillin, is the love of Israel, which constitutes the tefillin of the Master of the world (Berachot 6a), in which the praise of Israel is written: “Who is a great nation” (Deuteronomy 4:7) and “Who is like Your nation Israel, one nation in the land?” (Chronicles 1 17:21).

The light of the Torah shines in these spirits in a brilliant fashion—not at all in accordance with the measure of their knowledge but in accordance with the measure of the special nature of their pure, supernal spirit.

The Spark of the Whole and the Source
Our mind and our will, like everything in existence, is a spark of the whole and flows from the Source of the whole. When we view it as a model, a shadow of a shadow, we rise from it to make inferences about the supernal light. In the same way, we make inferences from it about the core of our will. That core is bound to our mind, and it constitutes the character of our search for the goal. That search too is a spark of the whole, and that spark flows from its Source.

We do away with all of the boundaries and deficiencies that exist in the search for our goal, and we come to find the aspect of nobility and exaltedness that exists in the search for that goal. That goal gives a fitting form to all our ongoing deeds. And we say that our goal is found at the foundation of the whole, which is the supernal center, the sovereignty of the Infinite One—in a manner of speaking, the beginning of all constrictions—which leads to the foundation of the whole, and which is indeed the whole: the entire beginning and the entire end, all existence and all that is sought of existence.

The Body and Prayer
The health of the body is part of the rectification of our realm, called Asiyah. That corresponds to the halachah that a person should relieve himself before engaging in prayer.

When, over a long period of time, due to damage in people’s reasoning they do not pay attention to rectifying their bodies and so their bodies grow impoverished, a great blemish is created in the world regarding the need for prayer and its being possible. A powerful force that opposes the essence of prayer and the thoughts and feelings associated with it is created.
That continues until the balance will return and the importance of the values of the body will be recognized, and health will return to its place in the totality of the Jewish nation or of the world.

Then the spiritual and practical need for prayer to be born will return, together with the need for song and praise—an example of the process being that Hallel is recited specifically on a full stomach (Ta’anit 26a).

From that, we come to the supernal spiritual service of prayer which precedes every bodily matter, and which nullifies our casting away behind our back (Berachot 10b) the supernal holiness that bears the name of Hashem and the sign of His oneness—an act that is expressed in the verse, “You have cast Me away behind your back” (Kings 1 14:9).

Everything in Torah Must Be Preceded by Civility
Everything in Torah must be preceded by civility.

If it is something upon which intellect and natural conscience agree, it must pass on a straight path with the inclination of the heart and the approval of the pure will deep within us. Just as we can learn about thievery, adultery and modesty from the ant, the dove and the cat (Eiruvin 100b), how much more can we learn from our inner recognition and spiritual sense.

If it is something that transcends intellect and heartfelt inclination, it too must pass through the conduit of civility, in regard to the connection between every detail and total inclusiveness, so that [it is an integrated unity,] like “a good deed that draws another after it” (Pirkei Avot 4:2).

Also, the fact that a sense of justice based on sensory factors is connected to Torah with the supernal, Divine will as it is revealed within the light of Torah; and the fact that we are bound to the totality of the Jewish people throughout its generations (as it is connected in the paths of its life with the holy conception): all these are paths of natural civility.
And these paths prepare us for illuminations that are more inward than the paths themselves, which will shine with a glowing, radiating clarity.

The Divine Names and Peace
At every time—at every day, hour and minute—we can distinguish the components of those aggregations that the power of our soul makes until that power rises to the unalloyed holy Divine idea.

These components are the many and different Names—as the cosmic mysteries branch out with their treasuries of life—upon which a person’s immaculate and shining service always builds its towers of high stature, “built as a cynosure” (Song of Songs 4:4).

“Because Hashem is righteous, He loves [workers of] righteousness, whose faces approve of the upright [way]” (Psalms 11:7). The Hebrew word for “upright” is the acronym of the Hebrew for “day, hour, minute.”

And this illumination of the unification of the Names always brings about the blessing of peace because it nullifies conflict at its root, and all of the components unite with a unity at their origin.
And the end-letters of the Hebrew for “whose faces approve of the upright way” have the numerical value of the Hebrew word for “conflict.”

And peace, which incorporates all of a person’s scattered thoughts into one exalted and wealthy conception, awesome in its splendor and filled with powerful life in its content, guards the Torah from all forgetfulness, which corresponds to conflict and scatters everything into its components and causes forgetfulness.

“The kindness of nations is a sin” (Proverbs 14:34). “When these evil mice [see produce], they call their fellows and eat” (Jer. Bava Metzia 3:5). “[Mice even] gnaw at cloaks, [which do not provide them with nourishment]” (m. Horayot 13:1).

The Divine Names
The Names are the relationships via which every being relates to the light of the Infinite One.
These Names maintain everything and call everything into existence. “I call to them; they stand together” (Isaiah 48:13).

Sometimes this relationship is so weak and dim, congruent with its descents, that the consequences that emerge from it in regard to the entity to which it relates tend to destruction and dimness. Those consequences are the names of impurity, which come about via numberless exchanges.

In the end, everything will return to light, and be maintained via the Names. “By your name they will call you, and in your place they will seat you, and from your own they will give you. No one touches that which is prepared for another and no sovereignty touches another by even a hairsbreadth” (Yoma 38a-b).

Shame and the Divine
The righteous, the true sages, are abashed when they think of visualizing some content in Divine matters.

That shame in itself purifies their mind and draws a thread of kindness onto them until they reach a station of light, of praise to Hashem. “Praise the name of Hashem your God, Who has acted wondrously with you; and My nation will never be ashamed” (Joel 2:26).

Studying the True Wisdom
A person is obligated to study analytically the true wisdom, which is the supernal, Divine wisdom: to be precise in its letters, in its statements, in its images and its phraseology.
The light of supernal happiness shines increasingly in keeping with the amount of a person’s toil in these matters in which the cosmic mysteries of the Divine greatness are concealed.
And when these matters elevate the individual soul, the whole world is elevated with it, and a throng of many souls rises.
There is no end to the extent of the goodness that is brought about by means of an inner, supernal illumination of one universal soul.

Raising the Sparks of Life in Food
All sparks of life that are scattered in everything—and especially “in every food that is eaten” (Genesis 6:21) that is liable to come into the hand of a supernal holy person (a tzaddik), who is wise in the name of Hashem and connected in his good thought to the absolute good—rejoice, and song and gladness awaken within them.
The open ear hears their song, and the discerning eye can also gaze at the light of their joy and their cheer.
And even if at times the tzaddik does not succeed in eating everything with revealed holiness, in the end, via his repentance out of love, he will restore all things from their fall.

Sleep
Sleep—and, generally, the overall natural character of the night, which causes sleep and which is appropriate for sleep—influences the aspects of life within a person in two opposite directions.

Our higher, spiritual aspect can rise very high. Our imagination is freed from the framework of the senses. If it is constantly connected to the intellect and to a supernal, holy desire, it can visualize and imagine, gaze and recognize that which it cannot sense when we are awake.
On the other hand, the power of life within our body lacks its connection to our spiritual aspect, and the body acts alone, expressing its natural actions in a dark, cloudy form.

Archetypes cling to these two points. Pure lights cling to our supernal soul from a higher illumination; and darkness, the drops of pollution and gross negative energies, cling to the vital spirit, coming from the dark trash that the spirit had been immersed in as it trampled through the mire of a solely physical life.

Every morning, we deal with both these ways to serve God: to purify our vital spirit and to connect our additional lights to the supernal human soul—and once again to fuse the two polarities in felicitous harmony.

Prepared to be Purified
When the living soul descended, sparks of pollution clung to it. Although we strive to eject them and remove them with all of the means at our disposal, it is nevertheless proper to consider that contact with an entity that is connected to the supernal light—such as the spirit of a person, who is created in the image of God—will not remain without any positive effect.
These sparks leave is much richer than they had come—and some such sparks have already been elevated.

They are already prepared to be purified, and that which is postponed today can rise tomorrow or, after some time, rise and receive a bright form that is fit to connect with a holy connection to this-worldly “victory” and “splendor,” which gains pride in the totality of “harmonious beauty” in the “crown,” [which is] “supernal knowledge,” which keeps rising, “keeps shining brighter until the day is whole” (Proverbs 4:18).

Holy Imagination
The outlook on the world of imagination whose foundation is in holiness is holiness and a complete Torah. The seal of the pure mind will always be impressed upon it, and it constantly rises until it returns to its supernal foundation, the source of supernal wisdom, in the illumination of its purity.

The Sweet Offerings of the Future Times
We comprehend the sacrificial offerings as not only external, symbolic ways of serving God but as rectifications, actions through which the world gains a firm basis.

It is true that the symbolic content is their form, their garment and their body. And it is clear that there is a significant relationship between the need for the symbolic and the need for the interior.
But when days will come that the need for the interior will cease at the time of the nullification of the sacrificial offerings, the symbolic power too will entirely cease its activity.

And in its place a symbolic object with a richer content will be created, which will connect with the most supernal service of God, which will contain within itself all of the effective, rectifying work that was performed by all of the offerings, but now in a more supernal form.
That is the sweet offering of the future, when “the offerings of Judah and Jerusalem will be sweet to Hashem as in the days of old and former years” (Malachi 3:4).

Sacrificial Offerings and Prayer
Rectified prayer whose value is equal to the inner content of the sacrificial offerings mirrors such a sacrificial offering as well in its symbolism and in its active work.

The two of these together—the symbolism and its active work—make prayer a living unit that is active in the world, and they stamp it with the noble seal of the people of Israel, which is entirely suffused with the light of our knowledge of the Divine in a pure form filled with the light of ideal life that turns to the eternal. And the eternal rises and absorbs worldliness within itself in a raised, supernal form that purifies and cleanses all levels of the world, man and life, and all existence.
The people of Israel will yet again pray and sing a song of holiness with perpetual joy, with the joy of the righteous who are glad in the pleasure of the supernal God and of all creatures.

Heretics and Believers
Sometimes, a heretic may be found who has a strong, inner, shining faith that wells forth from the source of supernal holiness, more than that of thousands of believers who are small in faith.
This occurs in specific individuals, and generations as well. Regarding them all, the verse states, “The righteous man will live by his faith” (Habakkuk 4:2).

When That Which is Beyond Language Is Misunderstood
Those spiritual, inner matters upon which the holiness of faith is based are truly higher than all language; and all verbal discourses only provide a weak shadow of their content.

Sometimes there are souls that apprehend the shadow of the hues via these words in a form that is entirely the opposite of their identity. Then their heresy is truly belief, like the reverse of a seal.

Books of Weak Believers and of Strong Heretics
Sometimes books that were written by people who are small of faith, whose souls lack the holy might of the supernal, flaming fire damage a person. And books that were written by absolute heretics, people suffused with a spirit of unclean might of heresy will rectify him and arouse his inner, slumbering soul, and he will find himself filled with life and power, with the entire flow of supernal might, and a tremendous true faith in the light of the living God.

Extracting Holy Souls from the Midst of Heresy
When we look into the depths of heresy, we see how, in the midst of its unfathomed abysses, holy souls filled with Divine, supernal light in their inner being are sunken. And they cry out in a terrible voice that arouses vast compassion, “Save us! Rescue us!”

And those who rise to the side of those needy people to deliver them and rescue them from their corruption are the choice servants of Hashem, mighty heroes who have a reputation in all worlds, so that all supernal angels above are prepared to fulfill their desire, and all powers of evil and impurity below fear them with an awed fear, with very great trembling. Such are people like Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa, Abaye, and their colleagues.

Light out of the Darkness
The way of Rav Hamnuna Saba was to speak words of foolishness before words of wisdom (Zohar 3:47b).
In order to recognize the light out of the darkness, the trait of foolishness must exist at its most penetrating depth.
We should use the blackest darkness when we want to know “the advantage of light over darkness” (Ecclesiastes 2:13).

In truth, that is a trait that is specifically fit for “the fish of the sea” (Zohar 1:252b), which do not even need the protection of ships, and for whom proceeding in the depths of abysses and all deeps is a jaunt and delight that gladdens God: “You created the Leviathan to play with him” (Psalms 104:26).

Filled with Power and Inner Joy
With our senses, we see how every sin darkens the eyes of the intellect and removes the refined radiance of pure feeling.

But completely righteous people know how to return constantly out of love. And although they feel in themselves the heaviness of all of the details of human sin with great bitterness, nevertheless they are filled with power and inner joy in the goodness of Hashem and with delight that comes from the great supernal kindness that fills everything.

Disconnecting from a Dark Outlook
The darkness of a person’s outlooks causes a single point that shines with the light of truth to draw after itself a number of dark lines, which become the foundations of falsehood and evil.

But the more that the person’s light increases and the more his will extends to supernal anticipations, the more these bent lines attracted to the ways of darkness are disconnected from their connection with the shining point in him. Instead, an eternal light of truth appears in his soul with complete greatness and force.

Freeing Oneself from Smallness and Weakness
A person must liberate his faith and fear [of God] from their smallness and weakness, which they acquire due to his lack of awareness, the debasement of his personal qualities and his bad traits.

The Supernal Nature of Speech
A person can feel how speech that leaves his mouth brings about great things, and that it comes from the heights and it returns as well to eternal dwelling places (cf. Kings 1 8:13).

The Quality of the Spirit of the Congregation of Israel
The quality of the spirit of the Congregation of Israel is essentially separate from the quality of the spirit of every other nation and language.

Regarding every other nation and language, the interior point of the desire of the collective entity is based solely on economics in all its forms: on the basis of a person’s inner concern embedded within him to bolster the circumstances of his physical life.

As for the supernal spirit that enlivens and illuminates that point, it is the spirit of order and beauty, which is the desire for the delight of the senses consonant with the requests of a person’s heart.
And when people are in some collective group that shares a single style, that common denominator creates the group’s national quality.

However, it is in the depths of the nature of the soul of the nation of Israel that the Divine quality rests. Its thirst for knowledge and Divine feeling at its ultimate height and purity is the point at which it feels life.
The refinements that arise from this entire picture and that spread across all the breadths and depths of life are the aesthetic goals.

The inner knowledge and recognition that with the fulfillment of this supernal yearning everything will be fulfilled, that there will be nothing of all the goals of life and refinements of life, the configurations of life and its programs, that will not be included within this eternal point—that recognition is something unique to the nation of Israel, resting in the nature of its soul, until it is even revealed to the inner awareness of its broad masses, and grows ever more comprehensible and clear to its most exceptional people in every generation.

The Divine in the midst of the entire scope of life, in the depth of the nature of the soul consonant with the richness that enlivens the national history: that is what makes the nation special, by virtue of the fact that the Divine grants her choicest children the ability to attain the creation of prophecy. That is what leads to the level of “an eternal nation,” the special nature of whose soul all humanity will come to recognize. That is the Israelite essence, whose forms are revealed in all of the nation’s different movements.
And the spirit of the messiah activates the culmination of this nature until the time of the completion of that culmination.

The Israelite Intellect and the Light Sown for the Righteous
From the aspect of the source of its spiritual, Divine place of origin, the Israelite intellect is a Divine intellect, and its will is a Divine will. The yearnings and love of the entire nation are infinitely awesome and deep, directed specifically toward the Divine, supernal wholeness.

This love is emphasized in the Song of Songs in the splendor of its colors, which the world does not deserve. This content-filled light is revealed in the supernal tzaddikim of the generations, whose will is the foundation of the world and whose words are the words of the living God. Not one word of their words will return empty, because the word of Hashem, the everlasting God, is in their mouth always.

Only supernal wisdom with all of its freedom, with all of the feeling that it possesses from its refinements, rising above the spheres of Divine recognitions, which are elevated in the entire glory of their beauty forever and ever—precisely that supernal wisdom gives life to Israel.

And in the crevices of the entire Torah, in its totality and in its details: when it combines with the illumination of knowledge, which is the Torah’s foundation and its soul, the “everything” shines, is revealed, redeems, improves, brings eternal salvation to every creature, and shines forever from the supernal glory of the One “Who rides on the heaven of heavens of old” (Psalms 68:34) and gives life to the ends of the earth, causes all types of salvations to blossom and encourages all the humble of the land, girds Israel with eternal might and restores them upright to their land, to renew them as in the beginning.
One light, one soul, the soul of all existence, the arm of Hashem, is increasingly revealed (cf. Isaiah 53:1), calling Israel to life, to again build and be built.
In the supernal soul of the tzaddikim, who are the foundations of the world, whom the light of the mysteries of God enlivens, rests the spirit of the revival of the dead.

From the source of life of this light that pours forth, a life that has absorbed from all of the concentrations of the treasures of life in all worlds, proceed streams, fine and various rivulets, to insert a light of life, a spirit of hope and a tendency toward unity, an awakening of repentance and great encouragement into all avenues.
And in the supernal light sown for the tzaddik, the messiah will appear to elevate the might of the eternal nation.

The Conversation of the Forefathers Is Hidden in the Insolent People
A small remnant of a large matter is more precious and elevated than a small matter that is complete.

One spark from the light of the life of the forefathers, from their holiness and from the supernal, Godly might in their greatness—a spark that shines increasingly at the end of days to restore Israel to an eternal revival, and together with Israel the entire world, in an orderly and progressive manner—is higher and more exalted than all of the revealed holiness in the content of faith and fear, Torah and mitzvah of the continuation that is copied from the derivatives of the derivatives of the sons.
“Finer is the conversation of the servants of the forefathers than the Torah of the sons” (Bereishit Rabbah 60:8). That conversation gives life to the final generation with a hidden love.

Here is revealed the tremendous content of “He Who recalls the kindnesses of the forefathers and brings a redeemer to the children of their children for the sake of His name with love” (Shemoneh Esrei, siddur).
The faint lights, “a candle at the height of the day” (Chullin 60b), are flung far away. Insolence expels them. But within the insolence, the spirit of Hashem is wondrous (cf. Isaiah 59:19).
The great and holy people in the world will recognize this mystery and will show the righteousness of the holy.

In their supernal wholeheartedness, they will bind the Torah of the sons to the conversation of the forefathers and their servants. And then a Torah crowned with all glory and with all might, with all grace and with all beauty, will be revealed as being “a crown of beauty and a diadem of glory for the remainder of His people” (Isaiah 28:5).
“Be strong, do not be afraid!” (Isaiah 35:4). The light of the messiah gleams. Eternal redemption appears from all of the cracks.

From the darkness of the wickedness and the contemptible, debased heresy of wretched people will surely come a supernal light that will cause the feet of Israel to stand in an expansive arena and that will elevate with mighty glory the nation that knows its God, that will shine light upon all dark places and encourage supernal holy people with true salvation.

Only the kindnesses of the forefathers will remain. And all the humble of heart, who will know how to view themselves as subservient and mighty at the same time, will recognize the light of the supernal Torah that wells from the conversation of the servants of the forefathers, which is the redemption of the sons.

Secular Literature
All of the secular literature that has commenced in recent times—which possesses much of the nature of “the wisdom of the scribes will rot” (Sanhedrin 97a), as well as many sparks of light and traces of redemption—all of it comes from the conduit of the conversation of the servants of the forefathers.

And this conversation, which is so precious, was greatly debased in the mouth of [Abraham’s] servant [Eliezer]. Although he had gone from being cursed to being blessed (Bereishit Rabbah 60:7), his origin, which was not blessed, still made some impression, and he harbored resentment in his heart (cf. Chagigah 15b). (See Rashi on Genesis 24:29, regarding the way that the word ulai is written.)
From of the bitter kernel within the great sweetness in this supernal conversation flowers all of the rot that affects the wisdom of the scribes during the time of the “heels of the messiah.”
However, this rot too will be transformed into a fertilizer that propagates and cultivates, fructifies and moistens “the field that Hashem has blessed” (cf. Genesis 27:27).

And goodness will conquer in its essence, and it will transform the living conversation in the mouth of Israel and all the seed of Jacob into holy conversation that provides the light of life, that rises in its greatness above the Torah on its present level, and from which will blossom the light of the Torah of the messiah, before which even the Torah in this world is insubstantial (Kohelet Rabbah 11).
“In this world, I have given you Torah; in the future, I will give you life” (cf. Yevamot 78b).

Instead of “Torah of life” in the sense of Torah that accompanies life, an intrinsic “light of life” will be revealed—“like the dew of Hermon that descends upon the mountains of Zion, because there Hashem commanded the blessing of life forever” (Psalms 133:3).

And all of this will be revealed and seen by means of the revelation of the supernal—the most supernal—mysteries of the Torah with great abundance, and of a flow of holiness upon all of the mundane in order to sanctify it.

And the abundant flow of all the wisdom, all the song, and all the treasury of life—the beauty and the eternity, the might and the beauty—will be revealed and seen as it comes from the dew of the supernal heavens with absolute, supernal freedom that is awakened, coming from the illumination of the soulful jubilee that proclaims freedom for the land and all of its inhabitants (cf. Leviticus 25:10)—“it is the jubilee, it shall be holy for you” (ibid. 12)—without activity and work, without acquiring property and servitude, without the yoke of the taskmaster, and without worry and fear, but rather with supernal trust, in refined delight and with absolute gladness, in the pride of Hashem. “From the field you shall eat its produce” (ibid.).

The Emulation of God’s Ways
The path of holiness is built upon the foundation of emulation: of a person emulating the supernal path of Hashem on his own individual path.

This applies to matters in which emulation is practical and intellectual, such as walking in the path of Hashem with good character traits, and performing all of the commandments dictated by the Torah and by the intellect, all of these coming from the elevation brought about by utilizing a matter in this world by emulating its Maker (Bereishit Rabbah 27:1). And it applies as well to the content of the imagination: when a person’s imaginative power arranges a matter in keeping with that matter’s nature, within the imagination’s parameters.
The more a person or the nation sanctifies itself and the purer and stronger its imaginative power, then the stronger the demand upon it to engage in this imaginative emulation.

A multitude of paths of pleasing and rectified piety will emerge from that for the totality of the people in keeping with the beautiful ways of the arrangements of serving God and beautiful ways of keeping the commandments.

And from that, the righteous ways of the supernal holy people will branch out for each one in keeping with the level of his soul and in keeping with the wealth of life of the power of his imagination, in which as well the light of the Life of worlds, Who grants life to the living (cf. Yoma 71a), is revealed—on all of the levels of the lives of all of them.

The splendor and beauty of the loveliness of the world found in the Temple (cf. Zevachim 54b)—the magnificence of the cohanic clothing and the holiness and purity of the body of each cohen on his level—all of those are a branching out of the aspect of the great level of the power of a healthy and strong imagination, which stands in its realm and performs its role in the world as a rectified garment for the Divine, supernal light, which alights upon the soulful and intellectual light in a person and in the world with the glory of the pride of that light’s might.
And here is the great need for balance to distinguish between one image and another image, and between one beauty and another beauty.
“And the way of the righteous that shines like light” (Proverbs 4:18), as “the gates are variegated” (Zohar 3:129a), rests upon the world with that supernal radiance.

Perfecting the Imagination and the “Beautiful Abode”
The supernal status of the perfection of the power of the imagination—overall and in the individual—is a crown of beauty that is appropriate only on the level that exists when the practical and intellectual have already been established perfectly.

It is impossible to visualize the complete character of the wealth of the imagination while boorishness governs and the strength of practical evil is ascendant. Only when there is spiritual and practical elevation that is significant and permanent is it possible to restore the structure of the Temple to its place.
As for the earlier improvements, they act to provide the foundation for the “house to dwell in” (Kings 1 8:13), the “beautiful abode,” where God’s magnificence rests.

Correspondingly, the demand for the wholeness of the glorious beauty and perfection of the imagination in its entire vigor—with everything before it and everything behind it, with everything above and everything below it—is the vigorous foundation of the demand made by life. The lack of the content of that foundation generates the terrible outcry when “the Holy One, blessed be He, sits and roars like a lion: ‘Woe to Me that I destroyed My house, burned My palace, and I exiled My children among the nations.’ As the verse states, ‘Hashem roars from the heights, from His holy dwelling He makes His voice heard. He roars mightily over His abode’ (Jeremiah 25:30)” (Berachot 3a).

Light of the Details and Light Overall
Evolutionary development causes light to appear upon all the ways of Hashem.
All of existence develops and rises, as may be recognized in its parts. And its rising is universal, just as it is in each detail. It rises to the height of the peak of the absolute good.

It is understood that the good and the totality are bound together. And existence will attain that measure when it will entirely absorb all of the good of its entirety with all of its entirety’s details.
And that is its overall elevation: that no detail will remain outside, no spark will be lost from the bundle, and “everything will be prepared for the meal” (Pirkei Avot 3:16).
To reach that goal, we require perfection of our spirit: to possess the Divine, supernal yearning that is created by our faith-filled service of Hashem.

Praise and Prayer
The praise of Hashem is demanded of us: in and of itself; because it satiates our soul with the radiance that comes from the image that is supernal beyond everything supernal; and from the aspect of the essence of life.
That is the inclination of Israel; and the Holy One dwells amidst their praises (cf. Psalms 22:4).

In order to purify such praise of all its dross, of all darkness and weakness, of all pollution and habituation to foolishness, of all inferior and murky desires, in order to set that praise up in the arena that the inner demand for great holiness and for the clear light of the soul with its entire freedom and might demands that it stand, a person must learn the entire Torah, from beginning to end.

Even in a case that the tractate Uktzin, [a technical treatise on ritual impurity,] is missing from a person’s learning, we say that he cannot utter the mighty deeds of Hashem, because one must tell all of His praise (cf. Psalms 106:2, Horayot 13:2).
Attaining that totality is the strongest demand made on us, and all spiritual sufferings in the world come to bring that out of the potential to the actual.

Every expansion of perspectives and every improvement of life helps a person attain this supernal goal: to increase in the world the happiness that will come with inclusiveness, when everything will be surveyed in its totality, in its completeness—and yet with every nuance and detail, the large and the small in the entire fullness of their fullness.

Prayer begins by addressing the missing details, and it must be made complete by drawing from the treasury of existence in the entire wealth of the elevated totality of existence, when the flow of abundance comes down from its source to be established below.
Prayer constantly rises to the beginning of praise, where it finds the greatness of its stature, its great stance.

And every day, the spirit renews its deeds: in a hidden way in every animal; in a revealed way in every person; and with a vast light in the few, the warriors of God, the nation of those who know Hashem and seek Him, who delight in the radiance of the light of the eternal God and in the lovely matters of holy yearning. That light straightens, sanctifies and purifies all of the paths of their lives and causes the light of their soul to shine always.

The Soul’s Journey Through the Prayer Book
The section of the siddur that transfers the thought of the person praying from Pesukei Dezimra (Psalms of Praise) to the blessing on the Sh’ma brings about a tremendous meeting of two worlds.

[The first, of Pesukei Dezimra, is] the world of Formation (Yetzirah), which is artistic, poetic, emotional, associated with rich imagination, a world that lives and exists, that receives its abundance from all of the impressions of the sensory worlds and contents of their life.

[That proceeds to the Sh’ma and its blessings,] to the world of thought and higher spirituality created by the word of Hashem, by His spirit and by His statement expressed with thought, which is exalted and elevated, sanctified, and transcending every border.

Then the songs of poetry [Pesukei Dezimra] and the elevated thought [the Sh’ma and its blessings] unite with the fullness of those worlds. Purifications and richness of delight satiate the worshipper, who proceeds in the lands of inner life in his spirit and unflawed way—in the light of his neshamah and the gladness of his ruach and nefesh, [the three levels of the soul, from top to bottom].
The light of the Life of worlds appears to him in its radiance, and “it all speaks [of God’s] glory” (Psalms 29:9).
And his soul is enflamed and filled with tranquility, might, strength and life, silence, and supernal song. It is filled with knowledge and wisdom, counsel and might, majesty and beauty.
And with all its heart, it wishes to express the feelings of its joy and the recognition of its thanks with much radiance and the inner, primal kindness to bless Hashem, Who is blessed.

And the soulful flow of temporal life presents the soul with greatness of spirit and knowledge that rises above every worldly and temporal endpoint, rhythm and measure, and blesses the Source, the Life of worlds, with [the statement proclaimed between Pesukei Dezimra and the Sh’ma and its blessings,] an eternal blessing: “Blessed is Hashem Who is blessed forever.”

Developing Acceptance of the Yoke of Heaven
We must sweeten—by means of organizing our subtle feelings and shining and pleasant thoughts—the content that is born in our spirit as a result of accepting the yoke of the kingdom of heaven. We sweeten that content by engaging in thought about Divine faith and all of the spiritual and practical pathways that branch out from that thought, until the word of Hashem is sweet and pleasing to our spirit.
And this sweetness depends on the great people of the generations, on their inner thought, on the arrangement of their lives and on their literary activity.

The Light from One End of the World to the Other
The practical and intellectual service of the Torah comes from the Divine, supernal wisdom, in which wisdom and life are united in the entire fullness of their wholeness and their delight on the level of supernal refinements. These are the sources of the intelligence that surrounds everything and permeates everything, so that the life of the will of the total, absolute and elevated good brings down into the depth of the soul and all of the worlds a light of life that, with all of its sparks, fills everything.

The brilliance of the light with which a person sees from one end of the world to the other (cf. Chagigah 12a) is hidden in the treasury of life of the light of the Torah. It gleams like lightning flashes in the souls of those pure in awareness, holy in thought and mighty in spirit, for whom the supernal nature of the pure, Divine gaze that comes from the streams of Torah is the life of their spirit and the joy of their hope.

It is they who continuously make and create salvations for individuals and for the public. The spirit of the anointed of Hashem, which is the spirit of the radiance of the world, the Life of lives, continuously pulses within them.

As a result of their spiritual and practical touch, it pulses in everything around them and in the entire world for their sake, in every avenue in keeping with its closeness or distance from them, like the amount of the sun’s light on the planets in its pathway, which changes in accordance with its distance and closeness to them.

The Spiritual World Grows Full by Itself
The spiritual world in its greatness grows full by itself.
In and of itself, it needs no preliminaries, studies, and descriptions.

All learning and ethics—which prepare the individual and the populace for eternal life—are in truth no other than a negative factor that removes wickedness and boorishness, so that the supernal light may spread in all its might and the breadth of its expansiveness.

Sparks Swallowed in the Body
Swallowed in the body and its physical and limited powers are sparks of supernal and elevated light that come from the “essence of the heavens for clarity” (Exodus 24:10). And it is they that are prominent in every “awakening from below” and that give supernal might to the spiritual, heavenly, expansive light.

Necessary and Discretionary Existence
From the aspect of the necessary existent that is the Divine, there is no universe at all, and “there is no other than He” (Deuteronomy 4:35), and every entity that exists is solely due to the fact that the extension of His will causes it to exist.

Therefore, there is no aspect whatsoever of a necessary existence in anything in existence [of either what can or cannot exist]. Everything that is impossible is so only in a relative sense—but in essence, everything is possible.

And the route that leads from the [Divine] necessary existent to discretionary existence is not incremental but a sort of instantaneous throw, like “the snow below the throne of glory” that God threw and commanded, “Be earth” (Pirkei Derebbe Eliezer, chapter 3; Job 37:6).

But since in truth “there is no other than He,” everything is a necessary existent, because in truth nothing discretionary exists. And that which is a necessary existent is the opposite of that which is regarded as being miraculous.
