In [this second point of view of a] profound good is hidden the root of roots of an evil that denies miracles and non-determinism, that claims that the existence of everything is necessary and dictated by nature, that denies creation ex nihilo, and promulgates the eternity of existence. That is because an inner spirit that is high above high gleams within that evil.

Every occasion of great ascent is preceded by a descent such as this, which causes the drawing forth of abundance from the wellspring that is supernal to everything, the wellspring from which everything is purified.
Afterwards, matters return to their place, but this time in the entire splendor of their holiness.

And existence with its components is increasingly understood as relating to God’s supernal, teleological governance that rises above every elevation and ascends to the heights. “Eye to eye they will see when Hashem returns to Zion” (Isaiah 52:8), “and all flesh will see together that the mouth of Hashem has spoken” (ibid. 40:5).

Compulsoriness and Free Will
Compulsoriness comes from the aspect of the absolute supernal, [from] truth in itself. Will is from the aspect of the relationship to the form of an existent. From the aspect of the levels of existence [as they relate] to each other, the compulsoriness returns. [However,] from the aspect of their relationship to the Source of existence, will manifests itself.
Souls are from the interiority. In them, free will reigns, and they possess the mystery of free choice.

As for all [other] existence, [even] its spirituality, such as angels and the like, [those entities] are propelled by [their] relationship to the way that the levels of existence [relate] to each other. [Those levels] are the pillars of compulsoriness.

When souls and their will participate with each other, the entire lower compulsoriness rises [until it] comes to the final ultimate [level] of the supernal compulsoriness—i.e., “clinging to the body of the King” (Zohar 1:217b). The conduit exists in particular in the souls of Israel. It consists of the foundation of Divine will and of the free choice that rests in [Israel’s] awareness and the content of the inclination of their heart.

The Divine Will and Human Will
We rise ever higher in regard to the level of the will, until we say: the cause of necessary existence [in this world] is the goodness of the absolute will of Hashem, Who is righteous, eternal, the foundation of endless worlds.

And via the human will, everything rises. “If the righteous ones wanted to, they would create a world. As the verse states, ‘Your sins divided you from your God’ (Isaiah 59:2)” (Sanhedrin 65b)—implying that if not for sins, there would be no division.

And everything rises with a supernal unity, happiness and delight, higher than all lower unity and all purifications, in keeping with the root of the soul of the righteous, who “will sit with the King in His work” (cf. Chronicles 1 4:23).

The Good Will Is the Foundation of Being
We recognize good will as the foundation of being. We recognize that all of existence is founded on its essence.

This foundation of the world is revealed in the will of a person. His influence grows the more that he develops it. The goodness of the will that lies in the depth of a person’s faith in Hashem is the kernel from which everything blossoms. Its roots, its trunk, its branches, its leaves, its buds and its fruit are his deeds and Torah teachings. It is they that multiply vessels to increase the richness of life for all being, for all souls, and for all deeds.

The point of righteousness in every heart is the seat of life and the foundation of the existence of the worlds. And when that point is made whole in the heart of the elite few until it expands over all of a person’s desires and it is crowned in every area of knowledge and imagination of his soul, he is in truth the person who is the foundation, whose hand holds all of the goodness of the world. And the light of Hashem that bolsters the power of life of all actuality appears through him.
Thus, “the Holy One, blessed be He, called Jacob El, meaning, God. As the verse states, ‘He called him El’—and who called him that?—‘The God of Israel’(Genesis 33:20)” (Megillah 18a).

All speech that emerges from the point of goodness of a person’s will in which Divine ethics rests—consonant with the depth of the truth of that speech, consonant with the greatness of its expansion in deeds, and consonant with the height at which it is recognized in the mind—creates and acts.

The drawing forth of life of existence, the making of creatures [by a righteous sage], of a fatted calf and of a man (Sanhedrin 65b), comes about by means of the elevation of the yearning of the holiness of the point of [the sage’s] will to its very apogee.

The teachings of mysteries in Sefer Yetzirah [with which the sage produces these creatures] help provide a basis for his will, so as to produce a vessel [with which his will may perform] its action (cf. Isaiah 54:16).

The Supernal Soul
Every day, [a righteous person’s] thought soars from the beginning of its growth. It spreads to all the extremities of its borders until it returns to the place from which it had emerged.

It starts from [focusing on] supernal kindness, from recognizing the light of the Life of existence, from how that light shines upon the worlds, from its radiance upon the human soul, upon the mighty desire of [a person’s] goodness, upon the energy of his life, upon his talents, upon his ability to rise.

[This righteous person’s] spirituality flames. It has so much universal light that it comes to express in detailed words, in prayer, in established expressions, its elevated desires. It praises, beautifies, sings, prays, pleads. It rises and descends, it waxes and wanes.
It penetrates into the depths of the mind, into the depths of Torah, in order to know life and goodness in their details.
It bestows refinement and nobility upon the coarse physicality of the body.

It fills the environment with radiance and light where it rests, through the sensory means of speech, teaching and guidance, and most of all through the propitious means of bestowing the power of its magnetic spirit.

This supernal soul requires a renewal of life, which is caused by a multitude of details that come to its hand. It requires measured training, the growth of its strength, and an independent stance. And for that, it needs counsel and guidance.

It takes these [resources] from the treasuries of its experience. It is assisted by the support of society, and it attains their completeness as a result of the manifestation of the Divine light that comes from the Source of eternity, which teaches this soul its worth and the worth of all of that it is attentive to: the contents of minutes that are manifestations of eternity, and the length of the spark-like points in its life that are lines that encompass infinite worlds.
This person’s inner life becomes powerful, consonant with the extent of his awareness, consonant with its inner freedom and consonant with the might of its governance over the world of life and deed.
His every word is a treasury of light. His every act and movement is the planting of the tree of life, which bears branch and fruit for blessing.
The pride of Hashem appears in his every step, righteous humility in every flutter of his eye.
“Every soul will praise God, hallelujah!” (Psalms 150:6).

Five Levels of Learning
The enterprise of learning Torah is necessarily divided into five parts: (1) soaring, (2) racing, (3) reading, (4) learning, and (5) study.

Soaring is the flight of a person’s thought without boundary, without an allocated position. Everything is in accordance with the extent of his idea, in accordance with the power of his intellect, in accordance with the sharpness of his understanding, with the purification of the power of his imagination and depth of feeling. That soaring contains endless matters. It assesses them with a swift overview that would not be believed were it to be told (cf. Habakkuk 1:5). It raises radiant pearls from the floors of the seas and reveals treasures from the darkness, and hidden riches (cf. Isaiah 45:3).

Racing is a type of reading with great swiftness, with a glance at the topics that allows a person as much as he can grasp, even as many topics pass through his mouth and thought. Sometimes he skips over a few words and topics, yet he grasps them via his thought. With that, he enriches his knowledge with a quantitative wealth, and supports the life of his spirit to become an entity of greatness and broad expansion.
Reading is bounded: to know the simple meaning without study and clarification. Nevertheless, a person is pleased with the limitation and clarification, and with the speed that is possible.
Learning proceeds at a moderate pace and elucidates a topic well in its local boundary.
In-depth study spreads out, together with its local depth, expansively from topic to topic. It is fastened to its boundary, and attached to the other branches with an inner attachment.
All of these have a multitude of sections and branches.
This paradigm of the five paths in [learning] Torah has analogues in service, in guiding [others], and in prayer.

Spiritual life in its totality spreads out in accordance with this deep-seated division, and practical life too is characterized by this echelon. Thus, there are five books of the Torah, five books of Psalms, five parts of the soul—nefesh, ruach, neshamah, chayah, yechidah—the five kabbalistic partzufim, and the five iterations of “Bless, my soul” (Berachot 10a).
And the five worlds rise in an aggregate with this prescriptive [schematic], which is both scholarly and practical.

The Soul and the Body in the Revival of Our Nation
The configuration of the redemption and the revival of the nation in the land of Israel must proceed in accordance with the order [of things as] prophesized in “I will sow the house of Israel and the house of Judah [with] seed of man and seed of animal” (Jeremiah 31:26), as explained by the Sages: “The seed of man by itself and the seed of animal by itself” (Chullin 5b).
A completeness of the [nation’s] form must be created.
Souls that tend to practical construction, to populating the land and eager anticipation of a government, must be formed with all of the strong dimensions required for that measure.

And people who have ethereal psyches, who revive the spirit and delight the soul, who communicate and radiate the supernal light of Hashem onto the nation and onto the world, are also actualized in their entire fullness.

It is precisely these two fully realized types who influence each other beautifully and bind themselves together to form a great, organic national body upon which the light of the life of the holy soul, tremendous in power, shines.

When supernal, ethereal life is filled with the entire beauty of its might, then “from its foundation up to the beams” (cf. Kings 1 7:9) it is higher than the life of the masses. Even the sage and scribe [of the masses] is in the end plebian, earthy and practical. His entire focus is on temporal and worldly life. A spiritual, universal scope will not be formed in his spirit.
But regarding the realized type of the heroes of ethereality, by means of rays of radiance that are manifested from them, they emanate the splendor of their holiness onto the heroes of physicality.

The exile could not bring about the emergence into actuality of complete two types: not a heroic populace, because it must tremble at the sound of a rustling leaf, and not holy sages are at the height of their strength, since prophecy has been taken away and Divine inspiration has been turned aside. In addition, the sparks of the might of the remnants of holiness are hidden within them like dimly glowing coals.

But already at present, the end has awakened. The third coming has begun: the type of person who is the “seed of animals” is gaining his form before our eyes. However, he can only attain the wholeness of his might and, how much more, he can only absorb the spirit of his inner refinement and reach his goal of binding himself [to all Jews] in order to establish a vigorous nation by means of [the influence of] the “seed of man,” the type of people who are called upon to attain his form by means of the greatness of holy strength. “Behold, I and the children whom Hashem gave me as signs and tokens in Israel” (Isaiah 8:18).

The Kabbalah of Intellect and Will
We assess the totality of the will and [its] blossoming from which details of the extensions of the will are drawn forth. When these details are clarified, they must draw sustenance from a chasm deeper than that which is encompassed by the totality of the will.
The same applies to the intellect: to its totality and to the details of its intellectual extensions.
Between the drawing forth of one detail and the drawing forth of another detail, we recognize an interval that is filled with overall intellect and will.

These intervals are holy rectifications that come from supernal phenomena. In the ways of Kabbalah, we envisage the intellect and the ways that it is drawn forth as, respectively, “the skull” and “its hairs” (Zohar 3:136a). As for the will, we envisage it as the lower part of the head, and we refer to the individual ways that it is drawn forth as the “rectifications of the beard” (Zohar 3:131a).

The inception of the revealing of the will-related, Divine, supernal ideal in all of its splendor, with the way that all of its details are drawn forth from beginning to end, is “the era in which the Holy One, blessed be He, augments His ‘beard’” (Zohar 3:134b).
“Fortunate is the person who awaits, and who will arrive” (Daniel 12:12).

It is understood that, due to the exalted and infinite differentiation between these Godly concepts and everything that any formed and created entity can envision and assess, the terms “will” and “intellect” are not sufficiently inclusive to explain even a trace of this great light.

We are prepared at every time of favor, a time when there is an illumination of the soul, to add many designations. These round out the descriptions for our understanding, adding light and wholeness in the depth of faith to our understanding.
“New in the mornings, vast is Your faithfulness” (Lamentations 3:23).

We may say that there is a difference between, on the one hand, the supernal, purposeful thought together with the phenomena that emerge to prepare existence and improve it, and, on the other hand, the progeny of the solitary thought, which turn upward. They are similar to the hairs of the head—which, only when they proliferate and are pushed out, turn downward. In other words, with the magnitude of the purposeful light that is revealed, existence appears in its various forms, and the streams of a rich and multitudinous life are drawn forth, like the hairs that extend from the height of the head.
And the phenomena that improve existence descend directly by their nature, and they are envisaged as the hairs of the beard.

Delving into God’s Greatness
The delving of a person’s intellect into the greatness of God’s wisdom and guidance must be whole: in the depth of its judgment and in the exalted greatness of its righteousness.

From that aspect, besides the moral benefit that is drawn forth, every person who is wise of heart must delve into the depth of [Jewish] law, which includes all the teachings of the fear of punishment in all of their hues and forms, in accordance with what the intellect and the clarified power of imagination can explain.
It is precisely on the foundation of this depth that the light of kindness is firmly based.
“Your righteousness is like the mighty mountains; Your judgments are the vast deep. You save both man and beast, Hashem” (Psalms 36:7).

A person’s might and the girding of his spiritual and bodily fortitude are completed only after all of the pathways of Divine might in all of their extensions—in accordance with what he can bear—have passed before him.

Then he knows the greatness of the supernal kindness and of the pleasant, Divine strength, which sweetens all of those who are embittered, until everything is transformed to absolute good and to a double joy.

Serving God, from Civilized Behavior to the Highest Levels
One of the foundations of serving God is that it should refine a person’s will, sanctify it and fortify it.

The foundation of the elevation of all existence to its highest level is interrelated with the level to which a person’s soul rises. And the fact that a person’s soul is united with every place it is in, every world and stratum, is a fundamental concept, because in spirituality there is no intrinsic obstruction.

All of the Divine counsel on how to serve Hashem and all of the secrets of the Torah regarding the levels of [its] laws—all of that is built on the principle regarding this elevation, which must always be based on the revealed principle that “civilized behavior precedes the Torah” (Vayikra Rabbah 9:3). The ethical aspect of upright traits and political rectification must precede kabbalistic levels.

The Temple sacrifices and all of their preparations assemble the highest aspects of Kabbalah, which enlivens and elevates the entire world. When people’s deeds are impaired and human morality stumbles, these sacrifices have no value. “I will not partake of your pleasant fragrances” (Leviticus 26:31). However, the world will again rise, until “the offerings of Judah and Jerusalem will be pleasant to Hashem, as in the days of old and early years” (Malachi 3:4).

Knowing About God, and Knowing About Everything
When we know about God, although we do not know about anything, we know about everything. And when we know about everything but we do not know about God, we do not know about anything.

A Fine Line Between Light and Darkness
Freedom of thought regarding [a matter of] truth is the light of the world. But we must differentiate between it and the destruction of thought, which is the darkness of the world. Only a hairsbreadth differentiates these two opposites in their external appearance, but infinite depths differentiate their inner being.

Do Not Be Intimidated by a Lowly Fear
A person should fear [God] with a supernal fear, in order not to have a lowly fear [of God] wherever it suppresses the expansion of supernal fear, which is the entire foundation of life and goodness, truth and light.

Raising the Holy Sparks in Eating
The sparks of life in a person’s eating are liable to descend and to rise.
When prayer—which reveals of the original will for absolute good at the peak of its holiness—relates to food, it elevates the level of all of those sparks.

When the sparks’ lifeforce unites with the treasury of life of the person eating, a holy torch rises with a shining flame, and it warms with a holy warmth all truth and all goodness, so that they will be “illuminated in the light of life” (Job 33:30) and will be bound in a bond of life (cf. Samuel 1 21:29) with Hashem, the eternal God, and draw forth from the abundant light of His goodness a life of pleasantness and holiness to all levels of life, in all of their changes, temporal and eternal.

The Israelite Recognition of the Divine
The superiority of the Israelite recognition [of the Divine] over the general philosophical recognition of the entire world is embedded in the inner demand of the soul at every moment for an increase of Divine greatness.
The elevation of this greatness is the uniquely Israelite.

Righteous People on the Level of the Sabbath
There are some righteous people who are always on the level of the Sabbath. They are capable of constant delight, of delighting in Hashem. And they are not capable, due to the intense clearness of their soul and the holiness of their body—which is sanctified by the manifestation of their supernal soul—of weekday work. They work only in order to taste the bitterness of life, to participate with the world in order to raise life.

The entire substance of their errors is always that they do not recognize their own stature, and they are not elevated to the height of the rich delight of supernal holiness that is proper for them, because of the smallness of their faith in themselves.
They constantly engage in a repentance out of love.

And the more they engage in repentance, the more they experience delight. They draw onto the entire world the great delight and pleasantness of repentance, which makes the entire world a new world, beloved and moistened entirely by the dew of Edens, watered with the elan of love and supernal pleasantness, altogether sweet, its palate desirable (cf. Song of Songs 5:16).

Surprising Matters from Supremely Righteous People
There are supremely righteous people, spiritual people—who intrinsically are not affected by any of the affairs of this world because they assess well the supernal power and radiance. It is absolutely true that they intend to refine it more and more and draw it into the entire world—the way of their work is not at all equal to the ways of work of everyman, who is always immersed in the boundaries of this world and its desires, and the imprisonment of the body and all of its inclinations.
When we see surprising matters from these righteous people, we should not question them at all, because all of their ways emerge from a very supreme holiness.

Holy Esthetic Experience
It is precisely those wondrous righteous people who are not at all affected by this world’s limitations, lowliness, and constrictions who appreciate the world and honor it. That is because they see in it a supernal world, pure radiance from the source of life. Its beauty and goodness rise with great elevations, and their awareness of its pleasantness and beauty grows with a growth of holiness and supernal sensitivity, so that they always live a full life that possesses the entire rich spirit of all esthetic pleasures that grant delight to life on a truly supernal level.

Even in comparison to the regular esthetic [sense], to appreciation of the beauty in vistas, in song, in order, in governance, in morality, and in every value, their spiritual senses are tremendously multiplied, until these senses are themselves sources of the beauty and order in life.
The world shines in its beauty and rises in its harmony as a result of the flow of radiance of their soul.
And all artists in the disciplines of beauty rise, and are refined and blessed by their influence.

That is because they themselves are immersed in the sphere of Divine harmony, which includes in a single unit the entire majesty of heaven and earth. And that harmony continuously spreads upon all Creation and upon all their deeds, upon all of the rustlings of their hearts and inclinations. And “the light of the King in His beauty” (Isaiah 33:17) continuously reveals itself to them.

How Sinners Help the Righteous
Ignorant people and purposeful sinners have a strong will that comes from the aspect of a limited forcefulness, bodily or spiritual, that governs them in the constricted core [of who they are].

Due to the connection between these people who possess lowly powers and the entire nation, and due to the refined desire of those who are pure of spirit to benefit these lowly people and bestow refinement and illumination upon them, these lowly people are connected to the genuinely righteous and wise. In that way, these lowly people bestow upon the refined, righteous people something of the strong might of their own will.

The spirit of the refined people in the world, who are righteous and have an upright heart, is filled with purity and holiness. They are always prepared to yield their will before all—in particular, before any truth and any goodness that will be revealed to them. That readiness weakens their will. However, they at last gain a strong and vigorous might as a result of the core of vigorous will that they absorb from the aspect of their universal binding together with the nation, which includes the wicked and the purposeful sinners, or boors and ignorant people.

However, the core of this might is only like yeast in dough. It consolidates an independent mighty spirit stored in the place of the holy, a might unaccompanied by any lassitude, hidden in the very root of the souls of righteous people, in whom the might of worlds appears.
Still, an ordinary person is required to bring a flame in order to kindle that holy might. And that comes about via the universal connection of the refined people to the nation.
And in terms of the totality of mankind, that holy might comes about via the connection of the human soul to the soul of the strong beast among the mighty animals.
And so that connection proceeds to encompass everything, until the light of peace with its radiant holiness, greater than the light of faith, manifests itself upon sturdy faith.

A Call for Divine Inspiration
It is impossible to refrain from making proclamations for the sake of the most supernal purposes, for the sake of arousing goodness and life in the world.

Regarding the people of Israel, we must at present—at this time of the beginning of its national blossoming—arouse its yearning for the spiritual, supernal goal, which is that the majority of capable people of the nation will be prepared to regularly experience Divine inspiration.

The proclamation of each spiritual word will arouse various interpretations, and each of its aspects will shine with its own light. And for the most part, every interpretation will reveal some part of the great and living truth of this good and holy treasury.

Love for [God's] creatures must be alive in the heart and in the soul - a love for each individual person and a love for every single nation, a desire for their spiritual and physical elevation... It is totally impossible to come to the lofty spirit of [the daily recitation of] "Praise the Lord, call out in His name, make known His wonders among the nations," without an inner love from the depths of the heart and soul to do good to all of the nations, to improve their wealth and to enrich their lives. This characteristic is that which uniquely qualifies Israel to have the spirit of the Messiah dwell upon it.

Hatred must be directed only at the evil and foulness in the world. We can by no means arrive at the uplifted spirit of “Give thanks to Hashem, call out in His name, make His deeds known amidst the nations” (Psalms 105:1) without an inner love from the depths of the heart and spirit that desires to help all nations, to perfect what they possess, to secure their lives.
This trait causes the spirit of the regal messiah to rest upon Israel.

Wherever we find allusions in the Torah toward hatred, we must clearly know that the intent is solely towards evil, which so strongly binds together many nations. This, which is presently the case, was even truer in earlier days, when the world’s pollution was even filthier.

But we must be aware that the central point of life, light, and holiness is never disconnected from the Divine image with which humanity as a whole is graced, and with which every nation and people is graced, each in accordance with its nature. This seed of holiness will elevate everything. From the midst of this central point of life, we desire the world’s complete elevation: the light of justice and uprightness, which is united with glory and beauty, might and victory, and the perfection of all Creation, beginning with humanity and all its attributes.

This desire is the innermost soul that exists within the depth of the consciousness of the Congregation of Israel. With the supernal spirit of God, we awaken this desire so that it may exist within both this-worldly and spiritual life.

The People of Israel Can Unite the Nations into a Single Family
Humanity is fit to unite entirely into a single family. Then all clashes and all evil traits that emerge from the partitions among nations and their boundaries will desist.
But for that to occur, the world requires the concentrated refinement through which humanity is perfected, together with the wealth of the unique character of every nation.
The Congregation of Israel, whose content is like that of a great storehouse of souls that contains every ability and every supernal tendency of the spirit, will fulfill that lack.

With the absolute fulfillment of the Congregation of Israel—in particular, through its connection with the entire world—all of the good that emerges from the division of nations will be conserved forever, and there will no longer be a need for actual division. All of the prevalent nations will be a single unit—and over them, in the role of a holy treasure, “a kingdom of priests and a holy nation” (Exodus 19:6), “the paragon of all the nations, as Hashem has spoken” (ibid. 5),.

Our Two Souls
The teaching that a human being is a creature with a composite spirituality—with two souls, a good Divine soul and a bad animal soul—is one of the most eminent principles that illuminate the way of human understanding regarding the character of the soul, and the most travelable route to the way of a moral, complete life.
A person can find constant satisfaction on this path, whether at the time of his serenity or at the time of his sufferings.

When the good expands, he connects his thought to his Divine soul in order to expand it, elevate it, and strengthen it. And when his distress intensifies, he turns his face to his bad animal soul to scrub away its filth, to rejoice in the fact that it suffers and in that way is purified.
With that, a person accustoms himself to look at his deficiencies as standing outside his essential self—and when he does so, he judges himself correctly.

A person’s aspiration to transform the nature of his animal soul, to a state of elevation, to goodness and purification, is a unit of an important service, whose necessity he always feels in the entire depth of his being.
With that, he finds himself constantly engaged in useful work that is necessary for him and for the world, in all holy undertakings, all of which rise to purify everything that needs to be purified.

The Soul of the Individual and the Soul of the World
A person must grant absolute freedom to the spiritual tendency in his soul so that it will spread forth and expand with all of its powers.

Corresponding to the soul’s many unencumbered activities, its strength will be fortified, and it will reveal the wonders of the splendor of its mighty holiness in this person’s life and in all of his deeds and thoughts.

With that freedom, the soul will raise, along with itself, all of the powers of life: those that are scattered and those that devolve from it. And all of them will, in one bond, rise to the holy, supernal height.

This trait proceeds to illuminate everything, consonant with the extent to which the light of this person’s Torah learning penetrates existence and shines. In particular, the more that the inner secrets of the Torah—whether from the aspect of this person’s knowledge, emotion, or imagination—are revealed and spread, and are prepared for the person to engage in them in an established and ongoing way, the more in general will his soul rise.

The soul of the world, the light of life of the Divine presence, will shine more brightly, and it will shed its light on all people and on all of their deeds. And the people of Israel, who from the deep nature of their soul grasp supernal holiness with the supernal, spiritual goal of attaining the most ethereal life and existence, will be elevated by means of the intensification of the inner light that emerges from the light of their supernal knowledge. They will rise and grow beautiful. Divine might will encourage them with the splendor of its harmony, and they will be increasingly prepared for the light of redemption, for the light of the messiah.

And the splendor of universal peace and the gracious love for the entirety of the nation of Israel and all of its individuals, its activities and the breadth of its life will proceed to spread throughout the world, until from the inner splendor rays will burst forth to the external glory. And the entire external world too will begin to recognize the light of the beauty of our power. And the hidden honor that lies in the depths of the soul of all of the nations who have attained culture in the light of Israel—an honor that is impeded by many hindrances—will burst through all of its obstacles and flow like a burgeoning stream to crown Israel with beauty and gird it with might.

Knowledge
Knowledge in its totality is the acclimation of the spirit of a human being to all existence.
Practical knowledge is prepared to teach a person about the pathways in his life, in keeping with that acclimation.

But greater than that is the function of spiritual knowledge, which completes the spirit of the human being so that he will not be detached from the entire world that surrounds him, in order that he may take vital, spiritual nourishment from all being—only after which he will find his complete existence.

That is the secret of the thirst for knowledge, the pinnacle of whose crest is the thirst for the knowledge of the light of Hashem, which is the foundation of all being, and infinitely more than all being.
And the essence of the demand of the spirit is to acclimate itself to true existence, to the Divine being.
That is the secret of the supernal work of those with an upright heart, who rejoice in the knowledge of Hashem and delight in the glory of His name.

The Highest Point in a Person’s Spirit
The highest point of a person’s living spirit knows its inner value. When that spirit is healthy, it delights in Hashem.
In consequence of the demand made by that supernal delight, a person’s mental awareness emerges and develops, in keeping with his experiences and studies.

The character of freedom of a person’s fundamental will depends on that supernal point. If the interior of his will turns to the good, that point abides in its correct state, and the delight of the knowledge of Hashem lives within it.

But if in its inner being his will deviates from its path, his sense of delight (ONeG) will deviate and be transformed to plague (NeGA). The entire procession of his mind will traverse the roads of darkness, and “the pride of Hashem will not be seen” (Isaiah 26:10).
Therefore, great is repentance, which reaches to Hashem (Yoma 86a), even if a person has denied the essence of faith. “Return, Israel, to Hashem your God” (Hosea 14:2).

That is because, when a person turns his will to the good, immediately the supernal point in the character of his spirit shines with its natural light. The stream of spiritual delight illuminates the paths of his mind, and the light of thanksgiving and essential faith shines and illuminates the weightiest obscurities—and light will shine in the dark for the upright (cf. Psalms 112:4).

The Distillation of the Entirety of Existence
It is an evident and straightforward understanding that all events in the world, all creatures, all of their actions and all details of their affairs, their natures, their characters, their traits, their ways of life—material and, how much more, spiritual—constitute a distillation of the phenomenon of the entirety of existence.
A person’s mind and the power of his spiritual assessment are prepared to find the roots of these at their source.
That is the basis of “the secret of Hashem is to those who fear Him” (Psalms 25:14), and of supernal clinging to God at its highest level.

Existence Is Constantly Filled with Movement
Existence is constantly filled with movement, physical and spiritual. Existence activates the levels of its vitality from above downward in a straight path: from the overall, supernal constituents to the lowly details. And it activates them as well from below upwards: from the details to the overall, from the lowest to the highest.
We see an example of that in a living organism, as well as in the human spirit: in its spiritual stance in itself, as well as in the joint relationship between the body and the spirit.

Restoring Our Memory
When forgetfulness grows stronger, the letters of thought scatter. They only return to their overall gathering when a spiritual illumination restores memory to its place.
Just as this pertains to individuals, so does it pertain to the public: to the nation in its entirety.

When the differences among the many perspectives and aspirations are in a single vessel, they illuminate each other. And when there is some diminishment of light and fundamental damage, forgetfulness intensifies. Then each one can only grasp its own portion, and gazes with wrath at that of its fellow, and quarrel ensues.

It is the holy work of Torah sages to increase peace in the world, to restore overall memory, coming from its spiritual source, to its abode, to gather everything scattered and to assemble everything driven away, to make them a single unit in the world—as they are in truth, at their essential foundation. “A choice vine is entirely a seed of truth” (Jeremiah 2:21).

Two Types of Clear Sight
When a person’s eyes grow acute, the first thing they see is how the entire Torah, written and oral, spreads forth from supernal wisdom. Afterwards, a person gazes with a clear eye at how the entire world, with all of its actions and events, branches out from that spreading forth of the Torah.
A person who is an expert in the first act, “seeing,” learns Torah and performs the commandments “for the Torah’s own sake.”

As for a person who is also an expert in the second type, “gazing,” he acts together with God constantly in all of his ways and events. All of his conversation constitutes words of Torah, and all of his actions constitute mitzvot and acts of holiness. That is the pious person, who derives his way of life from the foundation of the kindness of Hashem that fills the world.

Rest and Toil
At times, there is a person for whom it is impossible to be at rest, but whose true rest is toil.

Upper Illumination and Lower Illumination
There must be a partition between upper illumination and lower illumination, so that all of the details on the lower level will be clearly visible.

The partition’s thickness must accord solely with the need for the light to be mitigated so that the details on the lower level will be visible, and will not be swallowed up in the flow of the upper brilliance.

Whether in regard to a manifestation of Divine inspiration soaring in the upper heights or the comprehension required to understand Torah—in hermeneutics, halachah, and every practical intellectual field—some interval must exist.

This state of affairs will not succeed if we seek to nullify the spiritual interval. If it were nullified, the details would be blurred and a person—who must so appreciably enrich himself with details that shine with the light of Torah from the treasury of complete life—would be stupefied, and the straits of Sheol would overwhelm him.
However, during periods when the partition grows so thick that it becomes a palpable darkness and the upper illumination doesn’t penetrate into the lower worlds at all, it must be attenuated.

Sometimes this is done in a proper and gradual order. But sometimes the matter cannot be established in an ordered fashion, and the dividing firmament must be split apart so that the upper lights will be revealed in their splendor.

Following the flash that results from that splitting apart, everything returns to its vigor. The details are accentuated, and a measured light that vitalizes them satisfactorily shines upon them to illuminate them in accordance with their measure.

Increasing Grace, Kindness, and Blessing
How elementary is the realization that it is impossible for anything purposeless to exist in the world.

And how illuminating is the thought that every thought and idea—and, how much more, speech and deed—that we engage in while we cling to the Divine in will and in mind is alive and active. And its activity is certainly for the good: increasing grace, kindness, and blessing in the world.
And as a result of bringing blessing to the entire world, the individual who is the cause of that blessing is certainly blessed himself.

A Lack of Divine Inspiration
In truth, a lack of Divine inspiration in the people of Israel is not [merely] a lack in wholeness but a blemish and illness. And in the land of Israel it is a painful illness, which will necessarily be healed, “because I am Hashem, your Healer” (Exodus 15:26).

Clinging to the Divine: A Personal Observation
I cannot move away from clinging to the Divine, and so I have an obligation to strive to see the Divine light and its pleasantness in all mundane matters, in all speech and in every deed and movement, whether my own or of others, and certainly to feel the revelation of the supernal light as it comes through the conduits of truth and righteousness within the entire Torah, including its simple meaning, halachic discourse and Talmudic disputation.
And that is why I always tend to align such Talmudic disputation with the character of conceptual logic, which includes the feeling of the heart.

And all of this is out of an inner tendency: the fact that I desire with all my heart that the Divine light, with its delight and light, should be revealed to everyone, and that everyone should be refined by it and take delight in it.

I need constant encouragement not to move from that level, and to increase its light and to pave its path well, and to incorporate all the paths of learning and Torah leadership on this general path, which is the path of the righteous that grows ever more illuminated until the fullness of the day will arrive.

And the effort of proper direction in the essence of the portion of the Torah that belongs to oneself, an effort supported by the natural tendency of the soul, is the most assured path of going in the direction of the root of the soul, and of guiding it in the manner fit for it.

Even though everyone in whole world may think that he has no connection to this at all, nevertheless there exists within the core of a person’s heart a tendency to shine the light of Hashem in that point where feeling and intellect and every power of life join.

In order to cause this light to shine well, in order for it to truly perform its task, a person must repent fully out of love. And then, due to the great value of repentance, the power of its influence onto the entire world will increase.

And the path of that repentance must go through everything: it must exist in deeds and in traits, in speech and in thought. And at any rate, one must not push away any good point. And whatever part of repentance comes to mind, one must hasten and actualize it, with mindfulness, joy, trust in God, and a depth of faith.

Divine Inspiration and Mind
A person’s Divine inspiration must be bound together with his pure intellect. When both together produce constructs of comprehension, matters emerge well-developed and properly clarified.

The Connection Among Souls
The inner feeling that there is a connection between the individual soul and the entire knot of life of all souls, and that the souls of the past are connected with those of the present, and that all of them are connected with the souls of the future, and that in the totality of all of them the good and the holy shine strongly and radiate like the radiant firmament—the more this feeling grows and the more that it will draw to itself all of the deeds and feelings of the spirit, the more a person will be prepared [to receive] ethereal influence.

When the Soul Connects to Supernal Existence
The individual who yearns for the goodness of Hashem must feel within himself how the soul of his life is the great quintessence of a supernal and elevated existence—that his soul is connected with all of those supernal factors that impel its existence and its form. With that, his soul’s thought and the importance of its will soar upward, and the supernal good that comes from the inward being of supernal kindness is revealed upon it.

There Is No Stinginess in Heaven
A person must always feel that in heaven above, there is no stinginess, only kindness and compassion, light, felicity and goodness, constantly pouring forth—and the person can receive: when he opens his mouth wide, God will fill it (cf. Psalms 81:11).

And in everything good, in all Torah and every mitzvah, he will see with his own eyes how there is no end to the treasury of life and goodness that he draws forth, and he will constantly be filled with radiance and pleasantness, and he will rejoice in his portion, whether much or little, because the great value of even the very slightest amount cannot be imagined.

Then the supernal work of improving all existence with all its wealth and honor, which is given into his hand from the hands of the Rock of worlds, will elevate him with salvation, and he will unceasingly raise the banner in the name of his God (cf. Psalms 20:6).

The Tamid Offering and the Reciting of That Offering
The totality of the sparks of life of the animal spirit of all Israel was incorporated in the tamid sacrificial offering. When the tamid was offered, it rose in its entirety, and with it rose all of the sparks of life that had descended in each previous half-day period due to the lowly procession of life.

Furthermore, debased powers—and the feelings and wills, thoughts and deeds, which had been dragged along with them—rose higher and higher. Sins gained atonement, their imprint was erased, and they were transformed into merits. And via the ascent of “My offering, My food for My fires” (Numbers 28:2), the light of Hashem clung to and bonded with the soul of the entire nation.

Each person of Israel may feel a great imprint of this ascent on his level when he recites the tamid passage daily. That reciting accomplishes, with its special quality, something of the supernal effect of the complete deed.

To the extent that an absolute deed is stronger than the reciting of that deed, the powers of life were then stronger, including as well these animal powers. Their deep descent was stronger, and so too their ascent was more robust, and required more expansive power.

As may be understood, life that pulses with vast power has an almost incomparably and inimitably higher value than life that is only a shadow of life when contrasted with an absolute life filled with its own might, as God’s glory is at its full stature and the radiance of its life, in the House of our life.

But God’s supernal kindness does not leave us, and He chose us as His portion in our present service as well. Our small deeds with the speech of our lips bring about great and strong matters, whose exalted value will be revealed only when life grows full in all its character.

Do Not Let a Lack of Practical Repentance Delay Your Spiritual Growth
A person must engage in complete repentance for his every sin. It is proper as well that he implement all of the parameters of repentance with all of the most exacting details, to the best of his ability, with all of his exertion and with a proper assessment. That is most particularly germane in interpersonal issues, matters such as stealing and the like, where repentance is exceedingly necessary and requisite. If a person continues to feel a lack of wholeness in his repentance and its fulfillment, and he finds himself impeded from attaining it, he must be pained by that failing and strive to redress it, even if that applies to many situations. Nevertheless, should he not succeed in consummating his repentance—even regarding interpersonal matters, which certainly hinder his practical repentance—still and all, he should not let any hindrance in the world adulterate the breadth of his supernal knowledge and his spiritual joy in his spiritual attainment and in his clinging to the supernal light.

He should always consider that he is benefiting the entire world by virtue of the fact that he is increasing Divine light in his individual spirit, which is constantly incorporated into the totality of the worlds and into the totality of spirits, and particularly into the totality of the spirits of Israel.

With that, he illuminates and benefits even those who have been misused by him. That too is somewhat of a rectification of interpersonal damages. Although it is not enough, he should nevertheless not be confounded and immobilized as a result of making assessments of his situation that aren’t perfectly clear or that he is not yet ready to implement.

And this is certainly the case if, as a result of putting an end to his sinning against someone else he has only removed the spiritual barrier before himself, but in this-worldly actuality he has not yet rectified more than if he would not have risen spiritually. He should not withhold benefit from himself and from the totality of the people, but he should lovingly accept the entire flow of the light of Hashem. And then Hashem, Who is good, “will not withhold good from those who walk in simplicity” (Psalms 84:12).

From Animal to Human, Keeping the Animal Strength
When we emerged from Egypt, we elevated the foundation of the animal soul—our own and that of the entire world—little by little, starting with the season of our emergence from having been subjugated to a nation “whose flesh was the flesh of donkeys” (cf. Ezekiel 23:20). And we continue to do so always during this time of the year.

We begin with the counting of the barley offering, the omer. Barley is the food of animals, the source from which they draw their power of life. Our animal soul and the animal soul of the entire world is elevated little by little. It is elevated, purified of its pollution, refined, and elevated. It emerges from animal form to receive the light of human form. It emerges from the character of barley to the character of wheat.
And we come to celebrate the festival of Shavuot, the day on which we stood at Mt. Sinai in our complete spiritual stature. The radiance of that upright stance is renewed for us every Shavuot.

We are armed with the entire powerful might of life of the animal soul. And it itself has been elevated, ameliorated and refined. It possesses might and beauty, it is purified and polished, and it is prepared to connect with a robust bond to the entire form of man, upon whom rests the light of supernal knowledge that is absolute etherealness, supernal knowledge in its two overall levels: practical knowledge and intellectual, spiritual, contemplative knowledge.
Both of these elevated states rise, bound together, in the two loaves of wheat offered on Shavuot: human food, food that gives knowledge.
An infant knows how to call out “Father” and “Mother” only after it has tasted any sort of grain (Berachot 40a).

But knowledge whose clarity is outstanding exists specifically in wheat. The Hebrew word for “wheat,” khitah, has the numerical value of twenty-two, which alludes to the twenty-two Hebrew letters of speech. In lieu of animal muteness, “The voice of the turtledove is heard in our land” (Song of Songs 2:12): “Turtledove”—tor—is the “Torah,” complete speech.

We Have a Relationship with Spiritual Realities
Only blindness prevents the character of Divine service from being visible to everyone—specifically, the service that is in keeping with the kabbalistic approach, because precisely that approach, which presents the highest and most profound of explanations, is the simplest of the simple.

It is impossible to say that we have no relationship with the existence of spiritual substance but only with the impressions that it makes on us, just as it is impossible to say such a thing regarding material substance.

The only ground that such an approach—one that casts doubt on all perspectives on existence—has to stand on is its innovativeness and its skepticism. Even if its words would be correct, that would bring about no loss regarding our ability to attain the supernal reality that we seek.
Ultimately, these impressions do exist, and they possess a structure in our inner being. And this inner being includes a great many things. Behold, worlds lie before you.

When spiritual substance expansively pours forth its influence, when it is well-arranged, when the processes of life and existence do not contradict each other, and they do not contradict any of the spheres of existence that are and that can possibly be, everything is in order and everything stands peaceably.

The supernal universal and originary thought gazes upon a universal, supernal, and supra-supernal goal, and it gazes as well upon goals whose details and sub-details are infinite. It yearns for everything to fit together, for everything to assist everything else.

That which is supernal heeds that which is below. The keener that heeding and the more that its conduits are opened, the greater will the happiness be. Then delight, wholeness, refinement and blessing will gush forth in everything.

The yearning for the highest of the high, the thirst for the fulfillment of the counsel of the Holy One of Israel—the counsel that comes from the revelation of His thought, elevated beyond all thoughts—establishes its seal upon the world. Its seal is stamped upon intellect, uprightness, ethics, service and life.
Everything engages in the service of the Infinite One, and draws life from that service.

The Great Soul
When a great soul rises, it impresses a seal of ethereality, purity, and supernal greatness upon all being. That is the foundation of the vision of “the righteous person, the foundation of the world” (Proverbs 10:25).
The lucid and exalted soul is the inner point. All other souls and all of their deeds, all powers of being and all revelations of life proceed only in order to improve its being.

The world lacks a goal as long as this supernal soul does not shine in it. And when it comes and shines with its precious light, the world is improved, and heaven and earth rejoice, as they rejoiced at their creation.

Inner Purity and Egotism
A person need have no concern about being egotistical when he feels inner purity in the depth of his awareness and a revelation of his soul.

The Greatest Delight
We experience the greatest delight when we take delight in Hashem’s delight—“which is comprehended by the desire of the heart” (Zohar 1:103b), although it is not comprehended by any thought.
The entire purpose of all Torah concepts and ways of service is to open up trails for this bright, supernal delight, whose ascents have no end and whose levels have no limit and end.
Whenever a person’s soul visualizes one drop of this most supernal of Edens, it is suffused with delight, as the light of love comes from that drop.

The Song of Songs is based on this point, which is revealed in “love in delights” (Song of Songs 7:7). And all delights of all worlds are only slight sparks of the radiant light of the Eden of the streams of that point’s delights.
Happy is the person who awaits the light of this Eden. “No eye has seen a god except You Who performs for the one who waits for Him” (Isaiah 64:3).

A Torah Awakening and a Personal Awakening
Different periods of time are unlike each other in their influence on a person’s spirit.

Sometimes a person is capable of absorbing the spiritual light in the Torah. He then feels a great manifestation coming from everything in the Torah, and he is then incapable of sensing the spirituality in the progression of his own natural spiritual intellect and feeling.
Sometimes it is specifically in a person’s natural aspect that such a spiritual manifestation is intensified. Then he conceals himself from the aspect of the Torah.
Each person must proceed through whatever door has been opened before him at that moment.
Now, if a person wishes to rise from his own natural feeling to the Torah, there is not very much of an aspect of loss in that.

But when a person’s sense of the Torah’s light intensifies and the light of his natural feeling disappears, he must not set aside the manifestation coming from the Torah in order to turn aside to the vision before the eyes of his natural feeling. Regarding that, we have learned: “If a person is walking upon the road and learning Torah, and he interrupts his learning to say, ‘How lovely is this tree’ or ‘How lovely is this field,’ Scripture regards him as though he forfeits his life” (Pirkei Avot 3:7).

A person should always be inclined to develop within himself the sense of the brilliant flash of the light of Torah. “Her breasts will satisfy you at all times; you will always be intoxicated with her love” (Proverbs 5:19).

Binding the Two Torahs, and Shining into the Darkness
I have a great aspiration to bind the spiritual Torah with the practical Torah.

In earliest days, in the days of the prophets, the two Torahs were certainly bound together absolutely, and so too as well in the days of the Tannaim and the amoraim. The approach of the Jerusalem Talmud is certainly in the form of the unification of these two parts of the Torah.
However, the finalization of the Babylonian Talmud came to make it possible for the light of the Torah to shine as well in the dark places.
And the present time demands that [that the original] phenomenon will return to its state of vigor.

A Whole Person
Whoever has a soul—all sorts of letters shine in him: great, medium and small.
Therefore, he looks upon the secrets of the Torah and wisdom. He performs very great deeds and yearns for them with all his heart and with the essence of his character.

He understands, and he hones his grasp of wisdom and Torah in every way, with greatness in the quantity of learned knowledge, with incisiveness and proficiency, with great yearning. And he also knows about the affairs of the world and all practical proprieties, and he is expert in the physical wisdoms and all of their forms.
And all of these positive qualities are connected with each other.
Even a person who has not reached this measure must aspire and yearn to reach that supernal level.
And repentance paves the pathways so that one may rise with an actual elevation. “And the soul of the Almighty will give them understanding” (Job 32:8).

Placing in Order the Fluctuations of the Mind
Fluctuations of the soul’s letters and flashes of thought, again and again, rush like flames.
The more that a person engages in Torah and in mitzvot and refines his traits, the more will the swiftness of the scintillations be set in order and lead to a settled mind and an elevated goal.

Eternity and Clarity
A person’s thought about eternity and his aspiration to feel a propensity toward it in the interior of his character brings a fine clarity to all of his temporal affairs.

Sometimes a Coerced Deed is Very Good
A person requires all of his states of being in order to improve himself and to improve the entire world.

A person should not bridle against any situation he is in, but he should act to fulfill his obligations in keeping with the demands of his situation. Even if there are obligations not in keeping with his spirit and the character of who he is, nevertheless, since the situation demands it, he should perform these matters willingly and calmly. He should not think that he should only act in areas where spiritual delight may be recognized, because at times a coerced deed is very good.

The Encompassing Will
Even if we designate everything in terms of will, we are called upon to say that even all perspectives outside our will are included in it. And the entire meaning of life is to attain alignment with the most universal will, the will that is the most elevated of all, the will all of whose tendencies are realized in actuality.
That is, in truth, one of the understandings via which the moral will at the foundation of holiness is revealed.

Aligning with God’s Will
The purpose of each body of knowledge is to align us with true being. Since the foundation of that being is God’s will for that being to exist, therefore aligning with God’s will for that being to exist stands at the most supernal height.

Necessarily, all of the tendencies of our lives should be directed to adapting ourselves to that. And in that way, we come to rejoice in the joy of the Torah and mitzvot more than in an abundance of all things.

Looking toward the Cause of All Causes
However, our supernal knowledge must rise even more, and it must state with a humility that comes of righteousness that the designation of “will” is only one of the designations of greatness that we seek, and it is only a constricted emanation of the light of the Infinite One.

And although the supernal crown “is a pure light and a burnished light, it is black in comparison to the Cause of all causes” (Tikkunei Zohar 70). Not with sycophancy but with purity and with might do we say this, stating it fully, because that is the totality of true wisdom.

After Destruction, Renewal
When we rise to such a height of awareness that our abilities, even our moral ones, appear to that awareness as having failed, we are afterwards renewed in the light of a new life and a brighter radiance. That is comparable to the angels that are incinerated in the Dinur River [of fire] and renewed. Ultimately, there is an infinite elevation. And the renewed elevation comes after the destruction of the elevation that preceded it.
That is the depth of the supernal good, the might of kindness (as kabbalistically alluded to in the letters that have two shapes: mem, nun, tzadi, pei, kuf).

The Torah Is the Culmination of the Divine Light
Everything worthy of being done is already embedded in the essence of the [Divine] mind and of the spiritual existence connected with the entire foundation of reality.

If a person does the opposite of what is worthy of being done, that destroys the universe. He may be compared to someone who treats the structure of his body in a way that contradicts the conditions that it requires in order to live.
However, if the revelation of the descent [caused by his actions] does not make an impression on his spirit, the destruction is not actualized.

The entire Torah is the apotheosis of the outcome of the Divine light, which streams through worlds and penetrates the inner being of life. The people of Israel have been purified so much that they feel that this encompassing and penetrating supernal arrangement cannot be overturned.

That [feeling] was initially impressed into the patriarchs’ elevated spirit. [Afterward,] their descendants were purified in the iron furnace of Egypt until they reached a measure [of that awareness] in an inner, hidden way.
That inner knowledge is an emotion-tinged knowledge. When it reaches its maturity, the conditions of life must proceed in accordance with it.
Had there not been a supernal Guide actualizing the revelation of life to act in accordance with that inner knowledge, the world would have tottered, and the distress of life would have been great.

But the illumination came. The light of Hashem was revealed on Mt. Sinai. Hashem showed Moses the treasury of His goodness and the secret of the splendor of His radiance so that Moses might teach the Torah, “the inheritance of the Congregation of Jacob” (Deuteronomy 33:4), in order to refine the entire world.
Accordingly, when the awareness of every pious person [of Israel], every person who seeks morality and justice, discovers a moral secret, the entire world demands to fulfill its revealed obligation.

But “He has not done so for any nation, nor has He informed them of the judgments” (Psalms 147:20). Therefore, [the other nations] are not commanded [to keep the entire Torah], and, in regard to the way that the Torah guides them, the course of nature is not directed through them. That is a mystery unique to Israel.

Getting Past Despair, and Getting Past Sin
Sometimes, a supernal righteous person necessarily falls into despair, since he doesn’t find any aspect of merit in himself. In order to maintain his spiritual stance, he is required to think that, in accordance with the measure of the ethereality of his soul, he stands above the physical dimension.

It does not at all occur to him to utilize that reasoning to be lenient, heaven forbid, even to the slightest degree, with any of the most minute laws of the Torah and most minute laws of the Scribes. Nevertheless, that idea in itself produces in the heart of this pure soul a thought of pride, as a result of which he receives the level of an eighth of an eighth of pride that a person requires (cf. Sotah 5a).
And in the world at large, this idea acts to help a person go beyond his sin, and it eases the repentance of all those who wish to truly repent with all their heart and with all their soul.

Comprehending the Divine
Just as comprehending the Divine is far from every person who otherwise has the ability to comprehend—even the most supernal of all such people—so too is it close to all.
Even an inanimate object possesses this power to comprehend Divinity, because there is no end and limit both to God’s infinite greatness and to His humility.

In comprehending the Divine, there aren’t divisions. Rather, when people comprehend, they comprehend the all. And that comprehending never has an end and conclusion. Rather, every point of the all prepares for a higher point of the all.

Every comprehension of the Divine, even the coarsest and smallest comprehension, is a full world and more precious than all wisdoms and sciences, and more precious than all the wealth and honor in all worlds.

Every person is able to enrich the world with his particular spiritual powers, if he is capable of revealing them. One need not be  of the wise or be a teacher, for even a simple person can do this, for there is no set limit to the richness of the natural inner depths of the soul, which is the light of God in this world.
That is because nothing is comparable to the wealth in the essence of the soul in its nature, which is a candle of Hashem in the world.

Joy, Service, Tranquility, Delight
Joy, service, tranquility, delight—that is the supernal bliss [in Hebrew, “bliss” is the acronym for these four words] that the righteous attain, each one in keeping with his activity.
When these lights bind together, Divine inspiration “chimes like a bell” (cf. Sotah 9b).

Free Choice and Its Effect on the World
Free choice lies in the point of a person’s will. It may freely lean to the good or to the bad.
Everything in the world possesses this hidden tendency.

If a person desires to turn to the good, everything in the world—in keeping with the connection of the power of its spiritual attraction—is drawn to the good. Thus, he raises everything and illuminates everything.
If he doesn’t desire that, he causes everything to lean to the side of evil and darkness, as he causes his will to lean to that.

Righteous people raise the entire world because their will is great and tremendous and there is no end to its spreading forth, since it clings to the light of Divinity, and it becomes a sort of model of the supernal.

Faith, Wisdom, Truth, and the Soul
The root of faith is in wisdom.

Wisdom is hidden in a person’s soul. Via that wisdom, his soul recognizes the greatness of Divine truth. However, he cannot actualize the details of that truth. Therefore, he connects himself strongly to a belief in those details, because he feels in the interior of his heart that they will reveal this great truth in all of the avenues through which it is revealed: in activity, speech and thought, in feeling, in imagination, in character, in personal dispositions, and in a soaring of life that is deeper and higher than every thought of his heart and than all finite attentiveness.

Preparing the World
Masters of supernal wisdom prepare the world to be connected to the holiness of faith.

They arouse in the world a thirst for the exalted and the eternal, and with that they build the foundation of the world, societal peace, and the might of goodness in order to perfect souls in eternal life.

Prayer Overturns the Inner and Outer Worlds for the Good
Prayer makes a literal revolution in the inner world for the good. Correspondingly, that causes an increased revolution in the entire external world for the good—in particular, along those lines where the two worlds are bound to each other.

The prayer of righteous people is compared to a pitchfork: “Just as a pitchfork turns over the grain, so too the prayers of the righteous cause a revolution in the mind of the Holy One, blessed be He, from the trait of anger to the trait of compassion” (Succah 14a).

The Overflowing Lights of Shavuot
The entire world gains first-fruit status on the holiday of Shavuot.
The entire world is unworthy of what righteous people feel in the interior of their heart on Shavuot.
[At that time,] the entire world is joyful. The entire world is immense, the entire earth belongs to Hashem with a supernal revelation.

The people of Israel rise to be “a treasured possession among all the nations” (Exodus 19:5). The souls of Israel appear in their burnished brightness, and a person’s overwhelming love and affection for every soul of Israel, for every individual in and of himself, grows without end, literally. Each person of Israel is revealed in his supernal beauty, in his holy majesty, like a precious stone that has no finite price, a treasured possession—a wondrous treasured possession.
It is impossible for the world to bear the light of the Song of Songs on Shavuot. The precious greatness must be hidden in Ruth, which is read on Shavuot.
Joy and delight unite in a balanced complex, united and consolidated with vast peace and supernal pleasantness.
Divine inspiration is revealed in every heart. The spiritual worlds are filled with radiance and brilliance.

Everything rejoices and everything trembles. “The earth fears and is calm” (Psalms 76:9). The Congregation of Israel rises. The Israelite spirituality of all the generations and of all worlds rises to its heights, draws forth light from its source. Its mouth is filled with pleasant songs. It breathes into itself all of the delights of the perfumes in the Edens.
The gardens of these Edens waft their good scent. How pleasant, how sweet! “Every soul will praise God!” (Psalms 150:6).

A person’s will rises. His mind expands, broadens, and is filled with lights, great lights. Good and pleasant, lovely and beloved: such is the day of the joy of our happiness, the day of the giving of our Torah, the day of the first fruits, the fiftieth day [since the bringing of the omer].

The “I” and the All
“The evening prayer is its own domain” (Tikkunei Zohar 5).

A person’s comprehension within his spirit of the world, a comprehension filled with all of its constituents, need not take into account contradictions from the aspect of what is above it and what is below it.

When a person knows that it is impossible for his inner “I” not to be suffused by the supernal all and by the Source of the all, he rises, from his spirit within him, and he is able to appreciate the entire spiritual breadth in the inner being of the light of his existence.
He will then know how to expand and rise, how to intensify the good light until he reaches the loftiness that transforms all darkness to great light, to the light of Hashem and to His goodness.

Everything Is in the Chambers of the Soul
A person must search in the chambers of his soul to find everything in it, to find the entire world and the entire Torah in it, in a single letter of the Torah, which no soul of Israel lacks. The entire Torah is included [in that letter]. [However, a person] must fill and again fill the light of that letter until he will create lights of letters without end and limit.

The Lights Within Us and Outside Us
The living light that comes from supernal holiness generates joy and might wherever it breaks through and bursts through to reveal its power.

The inner light that the soul pours forth from within itself must always encounter the encompassing and penetrating light coming from the Torah, from the overall supernal light that manifests itself in the world.
Every day, we must occupy ourselves with the quality of the strong bond between these two lights.
The entire world culture is an outcome of the outer aspect of this supernal bond.

Learning Kabbalah
A person who learns Kabbalah must remove the fear resting in his heart, due to his rationalistic assessment, that he might be damaging his faith in the Divine in that he might be corporealizing [Divinity]. These fears are nothing but deceitful chimeras.

Everyone knows that [a person’s] Divine inspiration strives to illuminate the world with the supernal Divine light. [That Divine inspiration] finds its ways by looking upon the Life of life, the great Divine Being, which is recognized through God’s spiritual actions much more than through His physical actions.

It is possible to err regarding God’s physical actions: it is possible to attribute them to a dynamic power that lacks light and life—and so when a person knows about such actions in themselves, they cannot enliven his soul. But spiritual activities unquestionably emerge from the hand of a full existence, a full, supernal wholeness.

It is precisely this supernal, whole knowledge with the wealth of its details that reveals the triumph of the supernal oneness. The supernal sources of this knowledge shine with such an exalted burnish that even the expression, “oneness,” is too meager and too small for it, and that knowledge states, “Prior to one, what do you count?” (Sefer Yetzirah 1:7).

The more that the light of life spreads out with a supernal breadth to visit the people whom the spirit of God created so that they will study the thoughts of supernal holy [Kabbalists]—the foundation of whose lives was the desire for the knowledge of Hashem—the more will the spirit [of God] intensify, and the more will an inner, vigorous form be renewed in them and in the depths of their heart (cf. Psalms 64:7).
Then those select few will pour supernal strength and might from their spirit onto the entire nation and onto the entire world, with compassion composed of kindness and might.

The Supernal Torah Enters the World of Deed
As a person learns simple matters in Torah, he will see how the supernal light descended in a marvelous manner to settle wonderfully in the world of deed.

His heart will be gladdened by this tremendous preciousness and by this strong vitality coming from the source of the holy of holies—[a vitality] that is whole because of the sanctified pathway of the light of Israel in the entire world.

He will clearly know that this light [of Israel in the world of deed]—which is constricted so much in words and in letters, in customs, in deeds, in laws, in Talmudic analyses and in Talmudic argumentation—encounters the supernal light that transcends all of these. [This light of Israel] cleanses itself in [the supernal light], and these two lights exult together.

Due to this continuous encounter, the light of the Life of worlds is filled with radiance and great delight. This encounter occurs as a result of the power of the person who is learning Torah for its own sake, who brings about “peace in the heavenly host above and in the earthly host below” (Sanhedrin 99b).

Tranquility Gives Way to Greater Light
When a person’s thought is elevated and he intends to perform elevated deeds, and he already feels an inner serenity in [his thought], he must know that this is not the ultimate tranquility and that these lights shining forcefully at present will yet be blurred so that mightier and more brilliant lights than they will appear in him and, through him, in the entire world.

Those Who Channel Abundance to the Entire World
People who have an upright heart and people who are supernally righteous know that they are conduits of abundance of life for the entire universe. They feel the waves of the abundance of the good that descends upon them and, through them, upon the world. This feeling of theirs clothes them in humility and awe, and causes them to continuously rise in the radiance of their minds and in the preciousness of their character traits.
Every fall prepares a double ascent.

The More a Person Knows His Value, the More His Value Truly Is
The discovery of the great value of a human being, of his great influence—in the flow of his life, in the greatness of his spirit, in his will and the effect of his mind on existence, on all being—the discovery of that constellation is unique to Israel.
The rest of the entire world is very far from that recognition.
They think that, in relation to the universe, the human being is merely passive: influenced but not influencing.
But in truth, that disparagement is entirely without merit.

It is a certainty that a spiritual illumination provided by the core spiritual quality of the essence of being is strongly connected with this knowledge itself: [that] the more a person knows his value, the greater his value truly is.
And the more a person recognizes the vivifying influence received by the various avenues of existence by his own central existence, the more will the force of that influence grow.
It is evident that such knowledge cannot be mere knowledge alone.
The character of a person’s life, his will, and the drawing forth of his soul must connect organically to this knowledge.
That connection must come into being after the character of a long history. And that is one of the ways in which the Congregation of Israel excels.
The intensification of the soul to the extent that it affects and galvanizes existence emerged uniquely among the people of Israel.
Jewish ethics is not only individual ethics, nor only familial and national ethics, nor even only overall human ethics—although everything is included in it. Rather, in its essence it is Godly.
It is the Torah of Hashem, of the Creator of the world: the Torah, which is the bringing into being of Creation—nothing less than that.
The greatness of this recognition has always been the inheritance of the people of Israel, and it is their pride and strength forever.

Finding the Depths of Revelation
In every artifact in the world, even a simple human artifact, a multitude of thoughts and feelings is revealed—much more than what is manifest.

One could fill a storehouse with the breadth of mind and feeling even in a simple statement, even in common conversations—just as there is no person in the world who does not possess, concealed within him, hidden abilities.
But all of that is considered as nothing compared with everything that can be revealed in every artifact that was revealed through Divine inspiration.

The means of revelation are ranked across the entire measure of holiness, each on its level: Torah, Prophets and the Writings [Tanach], and the other artifacts, those of the sages and scribes [e.g., the Talmud].
One may uncover many depths in the words of each and every Divinely-inspired artifact in accordance with how the flow of holiness has affected it, whether in a revealed way or in a hidden way.

But at any rate, it is understood that one cannot compare the ways of revelation in other artifacts—even in those in which the power of holiness pulses—with the ways of the revelation of the books that were spoken and written with literal Divine inspiration, which stand at the center of the world, at its primary spirituality.

And in an absolutely natural way, all of the ideas—all of the most expansive and most refined feelings, all of the perspectives that are stored in the depths of the heart—of the four ways of interpreting the Torah referred to as the “orchard” are connected with the letters of these Divinely inspired books. [The letters] too are taken from the treasury of the light that includes everything.
