And “words of Torah are each others’ friends and each others’ companions” (Shir Hashirim Rabbah 1:18).

With a greatness of spirit, we must approach the order of learning handed down in our nation, with the goal of interpreting the Torah in accordance with the “orchard” in order to expand its boundary, to cause its plants to blossom, to increase light and life.

Rays of Light Flowing without Pause
There is no material in the world that does not have rays of light that flow from it without pause. And how much more, there is no feeling and no spiritual thought in the world from which a multitude of thoughts do not flow without measure.
And the same applies to a person’s action and predilection, temperament and imagination.
Everything bears fruits and fruits of those fruits without measure. Everything wells from the Source of life. And everything lives, and everything rises and strives to proliferate and to disperse.

The Supernal Amalgam
A person’s attributes and perspectives, powers of life and deeds, proper behavior and civility, appreciation of reality and refined response to the beauty of Creation, together with a deep recognition of the splendor of holiness and the beauty of the Divine splendor, are connected to each other.

The immaculateness of upright people unites everything. And in the light of Torah, everything is clarified, and everything blends into a spiritual, vital, supernal amalgam that brings great and supernal happiness.

Time and the Flow of Wisdom
The world rises constantly, because the root of the world is constantly filled with the light of wisdom. And the more the root of time passes, the more wisdom increases. “In the elderly is wisdom, and length of days brings understanding” (Job 12:12).

As a result, all of the branches—which are all human beings with their structures and the inner contents of their spirits, and which are also all creatures, even inanimate matter, plants, and all animal life—are refined and rise. All heed the voice of supernal wisdom, and the pleasantness of understanding flows within them in a greatly concealed way.

The righteous people who look at the root of the world, and who possess the tendency of fear in their heart—which is the “beginning of wisdom” (Psalms 110:10)—of Hashem, Who is “the root and essence of all worlds” (Zohar 1:11b), add the light of wisdom in the world.
And when wisdom shines, the blessing of comfort and delight shines as well. The majesty of peace spreads in the world, and it is crowned in its entirety, and it rises.

The Present and the Future
The world stands ready to transcend the circumstance of an impoverished form of working the soil, one that has the form of a curse.

Sowing with all of its toil, winnowing, and the hoeing that precedes the reaping—all of these are consequences of the fall that resulted from Adam’s sin: “By the sweat of your brow shall you eat bread” (Genesis 3:19).

The spirit of the human being will rise, and the land will respond with supernal blessing. “Its fruit will rustle like the Lebanon” (Psalms 72:16), and “cakes and woolen garments will grow from the land” (Ketubot 111b).
And the labor of the human being, including that which is tangible, will acquire a more supernal form.

A facsimile of this ascent is the light that is revealed on the shemittah year, the “Sabbath of the land,” a year of rest from all work of the land, when the blessing produced by the soil, a blessing that Hashem has granted it, suffices for a person. Human competition ceases and the heart is refined, until it recognizes a comradeship with all living things. “All of the land’s produce will serve as food for your animal and for your beast in your land” (Leviticus 25:7).

Indeed, both the jubilee and the shemittah year are [present-day] impressions of a new, future world, the establishment of whose entire stamp the present world does not allow. These impressions proclaim a supernal goodness coming from the radiance of a higher spirituality.

But either way, [whether in the jubilee or shemittah year,] the human being in his technological character is obliged to elevate the labor of the soil from its low state. That is what the light of Hashem accomplishes via human technology: “In the future, all artisans will ‘stand upon’ [and work] the ground” (Yevamot 63a). The greater portion of the ground will emerge from its curse, because wisdom will redeem it.
However, all of that will only be the redemption of the human being. That is merely a precursor to the second stage: the redemption of the world.

The actual redemption of the world will transcend the need to “stand upon”—i.e., to work—the ground. Then the labor of the soil will not be a chore but an Edenic refinement that remains. The human being will stroll in the Garden of Eden. He will be there “to work it and to guard it” (Genesis 2:15).
But [a third stage will exist[: Eden itself—“no eye has seen it, God, but Yours—what He does for the one who waits for Him” (Isaiah 64:3). That is higher than all work and all guarding.

That future [of the third stage] are well impresses the radiance of its light upon the present. In [coming] brighter eras, its impression will be more recognizable, until there will be a supernal elevation as everything rises, as everything develops, as everything leaps and gallops upward—everything joyful, calling forth and singing with inner cheer, satiated with joys, comforted with delights.
The splendor of the all and the majesty of the source of the all will shine in the fraction that each individual constitutes.

The ethics of the present is connected to [that future state]. The light and salvation of the most exalted end-time are not disconnected from the ethical content of the present nor from the “booth made of the hide of the leviathan” (Bava Batra 75a) [at the time of the messiah]. What each individual has access to is all in accord with his deeds (ibid.).

This [knowledge] is the supernal awareness, the Israelite awareness, which knows how to appreciate ethical life in the beautiful eternity of that life’s splendor—something that no other nation and tongue knows, and that no eye of any uncircumcised sage will see.

And even if a person experiences all that now, the future is not dimmed for him even a bit. The joy of its majesty is not diminished. Rather, [that joy] rises more and is elevated because of its robust connection to the preciousness of an ethics, one that is not a human ethics limited within narrow confines and built upon foundations from which the spirit seeks to be liberated, but an eternal ethics, an Godly ethics.

That ethics is the light of life itself. It is not a tether upon the horns of a dangerous ox (Tikkunei Zohar, end of Zohar Chadash) but “a crown of harmonious beauty” (cf. Ezekiel 16:12) upon the head of every righteous person (Megillah 15b). “And those who are righteous will inherit the earth” (Psalms 37:29).
Ultimately, existence will be elevated until the most robust “I-ness” of all being will be fortified with truth and goodness, and with their themes.
“Therefore, [the people] will inherit double in their land; they will have eternal joy” (Isaiah 61:7).

We Utilize the Light of the Practical Sciences
We utilize the light of knowledge to address all of the needs of the human being. The practical sciences are constantly developing and accomplishing wonders at this time, and we must elevate this entire living treasury to the supernal goal of elevating the holy light within life. The entire treasury of knowledge must be developed and placed before those who sit before Hashem, so that “its merchandise and its hire will be holy for Hashem…, to eat to satiety and for stately clothing” (Isaiah 23:18).

The Transformation of Idolatry
From the standpoint of Joseph, who possessed “the strength of the ox” (Deuteronomy 33:17), there was no need [for the Men of the Great Assembly] to have nullified the evil inclination of idolatry (cf. Yoma 69b).

Nor did Joshua, [who was a descendant of Joseph,] nullify it (Arachin 32b). That is because he wished to elevate the world with the wholeness of all life so that the evil inclination of idolatry would be transformed into a holy light, helping increase the flame of holiness.

Joseph absorbed into himself all [of the holiness that had been] scattered amongst the seventy [nations, represented by their seventy] languages. [That accomplishment was] related to his being named “Jehoseph” (Psalms 81:6) with the letter hey added [to his name] (Sotah 36b), the letter from the name of the Holy One, blessed be He, with which this world was created (Bereishit Rabbah 12:10). The gathering together of these scattered [sparks of holiness] builds a complete life from its outset.
This may be compared to a fetus that the placenta encompasses, [referred to metaphorically with the phrase,] “the dark cloud is its wrapping” (Job 38:9).

[Jehoseph said,] “I heard a language that I did not know” (Psalms 81:6). [This indicates that he now understood the seventy languages that he had not previously known (Rashi).] The acronym [of these words] is shilya, “placenta,” which is transformed out of the darkness to light.

And the end letters of these words have the gematria (numerical value) of 480, which is that of the word “Talmud,” plus an alef. That means that everything is united to reach an exalted goal: the Commander—Aluf—of the world.

In truth, the Torah is solely delight, and not a burden. “You did not call out to Me, Jacob, because you grew weary of Me, Israel” (Isaiah 43:22). And so “I relieved his shoulder of the burden” (Psalms 81:7).

Then there will be no need for the evil inclination of idolatry to be hidden away in a lead container [as the Men of the Great Assembly hid it away[ (cf. Sanhedrin 64a). Then “his hands [will be[ removed from the container” (Psalms 81:7). In the depth of distress, supernal rescue will come, with “a strengthening of bones” (Yevamot 102b).

“You called in distress and I [will] rescue you; I will answer you from the concealed place of the thunder; I [will] test you at the waters of Meribah selah” (Psalms 81:8). The acronym [of the end of this sentence] is avra, “lead.”

The acronym of “at the waters of” (Psalms 81:8) [has the gematria of[ 110. [That is linked to the ox (and its strength),] because “the sound that a person makes to lead an ox is hen hen” (Pesachim 112b), [and hen hen too has the gematria of 110].

“Meribah selah” (Psalms 81:8). [The acronym of these words consists of the letters] mem samech. In the Tablets, [these letters] stood in their place miraculously (Shabbat 104a). [This acronym indicates] as well the elevation from the depths [of the destructive angel Samael, referred to by these letters] samech mem, and of the restoration of everything to God, Who is “powerful in holiness” (Exodus 15:11).
“He fed them with the fat of the wheat” (Psalms 81:17). The evil inclination is compared to a strain of wheat (Berachot 61a).

“From the rock I satiated you with honey” (Psalms 81:17). That is not honey that is found [unexpectedly,] coming when the mind is distracted (Sanhedrin 97a), for then [one would have reason to[ fear “lest you are satiated with it and vomit it” (Proverbs 25:16). The only concern here is that “there should be no foreign god in your midst” (Psalms 81:10).
And since “My nation did not heed My voice…, I sent them off in the stubbornness of their heart to follow their own counsels” (cf. Psalms 81:12-13).
These “counsels” are on a level that is lower than the foundation of the strictures that are ameliorated because of their vast pleasantness [that they receive from a level higher than themselves].

“If only My nation would heed Me, if Israel would go in My ways, [then] in a short while I would subjugate their enemies and repeatedly place My hand upon their adversaries” (Psalms 81:14-15), so that all of these foes would be their servants, carrying gifts, serving out of love.

“All gods will bow to Him” (Psalms 97:6), and “the enemies of Hashem will cringe before Him” (Psalms 81:16), presenting their testimony [as to the truth of God,] and then they will be deemed proper (cf. Isaiah 43:9).

And idolatry will come and testify about [the truth of[ the Holy One, blessed be He (cf. Avodah Zarah 2a), and idolatry will be erased from the world in the manner of the erasure of “the [idolatrous] crown of Malcam” (Samuel 2 12:30), which was [placed] upon the head of David (Avodah Zarah 44a), and which became “the crown and the testimony” (cf. Kings 2 11:12).

“And their time will be forever” (Psalms 81:16). Time itself is forever. “Today is like tomorrow” (Shabbat 87a). That [alludes to the] one [extra] day [of purification before the giving of the Torah] that Moses added of his own accord (Shabbat 87a).
“That is the day that Hashem made; let us be glad and rejoice in it” (Psalms 118:24).

Exalted Silence
In the depth of the soul, silence is demanded of every person in whom supernal thoughts—thoughts that in themselves transcend the domain of human expression—are established.

When a master of silent thought engages in his exalted silence, many worlds are built, exalted songs are elevated to their pinnacle of holiness, and supernal might with holy refinement rises higher than all of its spiritual spheres.
That silence, filled with life, stores the splendor of wisdom within itself.

All of the details, all of the most exact lines, of the spiritual and practical worlds are revealed—with an intense penetration—to the supernal sage, whose planted vineyards are bordered by the silence that suits wise people (cf. Pirkei Avot 3:13).
That is the supernal silence that in its splendor rises higher than the wind, the earthquake, and the fire. It is “a still, low voice,” and “behold, Hashem is passing” (Kings 1 19:12, 11).

Kabbalah and the Redemption
The supernal content of kabbalistic wisdom must necessarily attain wholeness as a result of the manifestation of Divine inspiration [in a person] and of [his] soul gaining a revelation in [the realm of] supernal understanding, [a realm that] transcends all of the senses of the flesh and the finite wisdoms that ensue from [these senses]. That [necessity] itself engenders the inner necessity that a person’s spirit will accustom itself to a supernal attentiveness of the spirit of God.

The students of prophecy would accustom themselves to [experience] the supernal content, whose image can be attained solely through an inner, eternal attentiveness that comes from the light of a life of holiness. [They accustomed themselves to that attentiveness] until these images themselves—which seek to fulfill their role of being understood, structured, and fruitful—helped raise the spiritual life of those people who were involved with them [so that they might attain] a measure of a Godly gaze.

At this present time, which is so close to the ultimate salvation—“the voice of the turtledove is heard in our land” (Song of Songs 2:12) and “the buds are seen in the land” (ibid.)—a demand continuously grows for us to seek the light of Hashem, to seek spiritual, supernal redemption, and to flow “to Hashem and to His goodness” (cf. Jeremiah 31:12). This present time obligates us to increase [our] acquisition of the inner Torah with holy visions that are not led up to our meditative attentiveness but [rather that come about] via the rising of the soul and the elevation of its might in the light of its purest and most supernal life.

Regarding people who are “the host whose heart Hashem has touched” (cf. Samuel 1 10:26) of this camp of God—that [host] will constitute our power that establishes the foundation of salvation, the power that grants grace, the light of life, and pride of greatness [characterizing] the entire springing up of life related to the revival of the nation in the land of Israel.

The book of the Zohar, which trailblazes new paths, which places a road in the wilderness, a highway in the lowland (cf. Isaiah 51:10; 40:3), is prepared—with all of its produce—to open the doors of redemption. And when the people of Israel will taste of that book, they will emerge from the exile (cf. Zohar 2:124b).

Our Smallness Before God Is Our Greatness
When we teach a person the ethos of subjugation before God but we do not teach him about Divine greatness, we damage his spirit, because we teach him to live a life of servitude and abasement.

It is requisite to first teach a person about the Divine greatness to such an extent that a faithful image will be born in his spirit showing that the relationship of subjugation engendered in his heart towards Divinity is in truth the trait of his own supernal greatness.

Indeed, if all of the worlds, with all of their quantitative and qualitative greatness, would be one great personage, their supernal greatness would inhere in their being able to envision a relationship between their smallness and the Divine greatness and that they are on a level of subjugation before the Divine greatness.

Blending Together the Torah
The foundations of the Torah are its straightforward meaning and its secret meaning.
As for its homiletical meaning and its allusions, they are the means to connect and interweave the apogee with the perigee. And the details are myriad.

In Joseph’s spiritual amalgam was included, in his striped coat, the fact that “Judah still rules with God” (Hosea 12:1). [Via wordplay, the striped coat corresponds to “straightforward meaning” and “secret meaning,” and “rules” corresponds to “homiletical meaning” and “allusions.”]
Since Joseph and Judah are one tree (cf. Ezekiel 37:19), the entire Tree of Life is whole, and from its fruit we plant multiple plantings in order to establish wholly the entire orchard.

Body and Soul, Angel and Human Being, and the Four Paths of the Torah
A person’s body, which is so material and lowly, corresponds to the tenet of straightforward meaning—in the Torah and in the world.
And his soul, which is so ethereal, spiritual, aspiring to wondrous great things, is from the secret counsel of God upon his tent” (cf. Job 29:4).
Supernal angels, seraphim and ophanim, are aligned in accord with allusions and homiletical meaning.
When [these angels] are incorporated into a person’s vital powers and the people of Israel become their companions, everything is whole.

But when separation prevails, we say, “Go descend, because your nation has acted corruptly” (Exodus 32:7), and the land “will cause thorns and thistle to grow” (Genesis 3:18). [Via wordplay, “descend” corresponds to “allusions, homiletical meaning,” and “thistle” corresponds to “homiletical meaning, allusions.”] [The land] lacks the vigorous power of reality and supernal etherealness, the light of the life of all existence.

When straightforward meaning aspires to its supernal foundation, which is the light of secret meaning, its arms spread out [with the character of] the contents of homiletical meaning and allusions, and these rise upward as the hands rise. “Raise your hands in the holy place” (Psalms 134:2).

Going Beyond the Superficial in Serving God
It is impossible to engage in the service of God without prior preparation.
Initially, thoughts pass through a person’s mind that grant his service a superficial character.

If we stand in prayer, for instance, while this superficial character wanders about within our contemplation, we strengthen these powers and their sources, all of which are “a degenerate wild vine” (Jeremiah 2:21).

Therefore, we must prepare our every service of God and our every prayer with a renewed character of inner contemplation that evinces from the Divine light a new internality—which, with its goodness, arouses a new flash of the supernal light.

The revelation of the will and radiance of the intellect that comes in the service of God that a person intends at that time appears in a form that strengthens absolute goodness and the manifestation of its light in the world via the light of the spirit of the span of time during which this service occurs.

Faith at Its Outset
All clarity comes from faith. And faith at its onset is composed of a mixture of fear and love.

In its inner being, the soul feels how faith, fear, and love from their very foundation turn only to the Divine, and that the entire fact that these traits exist in association with other matters is solely because some illumination of the Divine spark reaches there.

The Continuum from Affirmation to Negation
This world was created with the letter hey of God’s name (Menachot 29b). [In Hebrew, that is the acronym for] “required, prohibited.” These are two heads of the constituents of absolute affirmation and absolute negation.
Between them is the “substance” [in Hebrew, that is the acronym] for the three levels of [a continuum of] “obligation, precept, elective action.”

Creating a Vessel for the Light of Thought
Every allusion has its content and its root.
That is because the light of thought fills everything. And every vessel that we make in which to receive a mental flash of lightning receives some property.
At any rate, one must discern the content of the matter that the allusion communicates. [The Hebrew word for] “allusion” is itself is the acronym for “See what this is.”

On the Spectrum
Everything has its elevated aspect and its lowly aspect, and many lines between these two poles. And every person grasps every matter in the place that is appropriate for him.

The Science of Faith
Faith in the Divine is the ground from which all of the goodness of life flourishes.

Today, the science of agronomy enriches farmers, who were once universally considered to stand on the lowest rung of economic life. So too the science of faith will grant great and full-fledged happiness to the entire population that is connected to wholehearted faith as a result of being shown the great wealth that lies in its treasuries.

That which was prepared only for those wealthy in spirit in previous generations will now be prepared and presented clearly to each individual. This is because of the past eras that, with their spiritual acquisitions, facilitated the development of this science of faith, which will now come to light in its entire, splendid clarity.

Ethical Improvement and the Practical Sciences
Human ethics proceeds with goodness in its inner being. And correspondingly, scientific development proceeds and manifests itself in new forms that ease the yoke of life.

If these discoveries had come to the world when ethics was less than it is at present, the intensity of their richness and the diminishment of toil they would have caused would have damaged the order of life.

In truth, now as well ethics’ refinement exists only in its inner being, on a hidden level. Therefore, many are the impediments that prevent humanity overall from benefiting from its world. And so humanity does not gain an extensive and genuine benefit from the many inventions that its expanding practical spirit devises.

Welcome is the holy service of the spiritual sages, the teachers of the religion, of supernal truth and uprightness, those who illuminate the Divine light in the world, who prepare humanity for a type of life through which it will be able to receive all of the blessings from the great wealth of the practical sciences that are hidden away for it.

The greatness and wealth of the practical sciences will be properly appreciated only when they will bond with the essential wealth of the blessing of the spirit, whose source is the blessing of the Maker of all the worlds and the flow of His light.

Frustration and Delight in Every Field of Study
In every field of study in which a person engages, he will encounter frustration together with delight.

He will experience delight as a result of the expansion of his knowledge, the suffusion of the light of spiritual life in his soul. And he will experience frustration as a result of the way that every field of study constricts itself into its own specific horizons.
In particular, a person with a rich soul, with vast song and beauty, will suffer from the constriction of those fields of study involved with extraneous and fortuitous topics.

His pain will grow especially when specialists who have not experienced anything of the pain of an overflow of knowledge but who are satiated and joyful in their portion, great and elevated in their own eyes because of a vast wholeness that lacks nothing in their eyes, proffer to us dry kernels of matters that are in truth at their foundation filled with freshness, and that reflect all being.

They offer us, for instance, historical lectures that accord with external deeds and facts, as with a strong hand they rip away their specialty for which they are fit from the entire tapestry of great existence with its exalted splendor.
We must overcome the desolation of our spirit and learn from what these seekers raise in their net. But afterwards, we must renew the face of these matters in their living, inclusive source.

Whether we desire the improvement of the spirit of the overall community or whether we desire only our own improvement, in the end we cannot bear with equanimity the penury of mind, the lack of life and impoverishment of spiritual beauty that these specialists bring us despite their vast wealth, their multitudinous knowledge, and their industrious investigation arranged in a particular spirit—whether tending to the left or to the right.

When Clinging to God Is Disconnected from Everything Else
When clinging to the Divine comes to a person only as a lone thought or feeling—when all the pathways of his life, his entire outlook on the world, the entire richness of his Torah, his entire bodily well-being, his entire relationship to his environment, to the history of his nation and of the human race, to all the teachings of ethics and character, and to all the streams of song and poetry, including the sense of everything exalted and lovely, do not relate to clinging to the Divine with an organic connection—then that clinging turns into a sort of idle delusion that impoverishes the human—the individual and the populace—and that is not at all worthy of its great name.

But when clinging to the Divine emerges from great spiritual and practical richness, then it—and only it—is the crown of life. Only via it will the position of the nation be established. Via it, the glory of all the sciences and all of the finest and most magnificent rectifications in the world will be elevated. Via it, souls will be purified in their depth, and via it, life will be filled with gladness and sureness. Life will become rich, and the fear of illnesses, sufferings, poverty and death be unable to disturb its light, which bathes everything.

Everything is viewed through the lens of the Source of life. And everything is vanquished by the might of powerful men every thought of whose spirit and whose entire inter being are filled with the light of life.

The joy of eternity crowns them at all times and holy splendor beautifies the level they are on. From the radiance of their lives, a precious light manifests itself onto the entire world, onto their entire generation, onto all who hurry to benefit from their radiance.

And the Torah, whose goal is clinging to the Divine in the form of elevating all life to the Torah, in the form of the fulfillment of all practical and societal improvements and their preparation to reach their supernal goal, is a doctrine of life for the entire world, a doctrine that will in the future be the universal wellspring for the treasury of the human spirit.

The Living Wellspring and the Cracked Cisterns
The Divine light is continuously growing. It is fruitful, enlarging itself and strengthening itself, increasing the light and radiance of its life without interruption—as long as it is guarded from the ugliness of idolatry.
All of the pollution that idolatry causes comes because the interruption of growth and elevation is embedded in its character. “An idol is a eunuch, and cannot be fruitful” (Zohar 2:103b).
The living wellspring does not grow damaged. No decay arises in it. Its waters constantly gush forth. “They are new in the mornings; vast is Your faithfulness” (Lamentations 3:23).
But the quarried cisterns—besides the fact that their waters are fetid cave waters whose fetidness grows so manifest that it is soon suffocating—will be unable to store their waters.
Life makes cracks in these artificial containers. Falsehood is revealed, and the ugliness comes to the foreground. They are “broken cisterns that do not hold water” (Jeremiah 2:13).

Our Spiritual Distress
All names [of God] in the world are too narrow for us when we come to speak from the depths of our soul about the Divine exaltedness.

As we express these names, we know that we are perturbing their inner light [only in terms of their being] an ultimate cause of bodily and spiritual expression. This [causes us a] spiritual distress, as a result of which our soul expands. “From the narrows have I called to God; answer me in the breadth of God” (Psalms 118:5).

Ethics, Will and Knowing
It is possible to say that will is never known, just as knowing has no will.
But that does not prevent us from rising to a higher place where knowing and will are united.

And nothing forces us to deny that the form of the essence of life is arranged in such a way that the character of knowing and will together are a single entity in that form, rich and filled with worth. [When we reach that level,] the relationship of ethics to the essence of life will be solely of good ethics unifying knowing and the will in its branches, just as they are unified in their root trunk.

The Cosmic Persona
The universal, cosmic persona possesses ethics, will, and free choice.

Universal evil is a consequence of [the cosmic persona’s] ethical descent, just as personal evil is a consequence of an individual’s ethical descent, and societal evil is a consequence of a society’s ethical descent.

We have no permission to disconnect the image [of that persona as it is] revealed to us in the life of an individual and of the public [from the cosmic persona itself], saying that [life here on earth] does not have roots in the expanse of all life. It is impossible to envision a law of existence that does not extend to the most expansive universal horizons.

The universal descent is certainly more exalted and more filled with life than a constricted, individual descent is. The moon challenged [God, saying that it should be equal to the sun (Chullin 60b)]. The earth sinned [by producing fruit trees that were not in themselves edible as fruit (Rashi on Genesis 1:11)]. These factors preceded the sin of the human being. And the human being is a branch whose power is great enough to influence its root.

These matters turn around. Man will rectify his sin, and the earth will respond correspondingly, repairing its own sin as well. The moon will repudiate its challenge. Its flaw will be made whole, and it will not be at all diminished. All of the disturbances in the heavenly ranks will be set in order so that only the good will vanquish.

A person must possess a penetrating, inner gaze that accompanies a complete happiness related to the will that exists in the secret places of his soul. That gaze must unite with his ability to attain a supernal awareness that acknowledges the Divine good, the might of God’s ability, and the strength of His desire to do good, to illuminate, and to give life.

Then such a gaze provides us with its guarantee that things will be good. Prophecy and a flow of Divine inspiration will come to us, filling that which our intellect does not make whole, and the source of refined joy within us will be blessed with a blessing of peace and truth.

Pride and Humility
A person’s pridefulness damages the entire content of his holiness.

A person has some approximate image of the Divine greatness. Although he staunchly knows that [before God] all reflections are exhausted and all thoughts are considered as nothing, nevertheless, his spirit will necessarily connect with some image of God’s greatness and worthiness of veneration. And subsequent to that image, he inwardly accepts the impossibility of his comprehension and imaging. Rather, God’s Presence rests in his private sanctuary in a state of clouded comprehension.

But if he grows prideful and attributes exaltedness and wholeness to himself, his approximate image of his own greatness rises higher than the Divine image, and he remains standing in a state of terrible pridefulness beyond estimation.

Then God’s Presence wails over him and the light hovering upon God’s Presence in his private sanctuary turns away from him, so that he remains truly stunned and empty. He becomes such a total idolatrous object that it is a mitzvah to uproot him like an [idolatrous] Asherah tree.

A person should take to heart the entire contents of this thought and cling to humility, which constitutes the total truth that it is entirely impossible for a person to become prideful, and it is impossible for any created, emanated being to become prideful at the height of truth. Pride is fitting only for the One Who is proud over all the proud, and His pride is too great for the world to contain.
And that [pride of God] is itself absolute humility.
If this flash of holiness of supernal pride is not yet well-arranged in the world and human thought is not fit to encompass it, the great future will open gates for it.

“Hashem has reigned, He has clothed Himself in pride” (Psalms 93:1). And the phrase concludes, “Your testimonies regarding Your house, the holy dwelling, are very faithful, Hashem, for length of days” (ibid. 5). Length of days will satisfy the one who knows the name of Hashem, Whose true crown is humility.

The Holiness in Work
It is clear that a righteous person performs all of his deeds in a holy way, and that all of his physical actions ascend toward attaining the rectification of the world. The righteous person loves this work (cf. Pirkei Avot 1:10), which is on such an intrinsically high level and which “was given in a covenant, just as the Torah was given in a covenant” (Avot Derebbe Natan 11).

And so there is now no doubt that a complete rectification of the world and the expansion of the light of holiness truly exists in all work. There is something great and universal in every movement that rescues some part of existence from the dominion of chaos.

However, highest of all is the universal rescue brought about by the improvement of the inner life of being: the extrication of that life from its amorphous state and its rectification so that it becomes akin to unimpaired implements that perform their function well.

This viewpoint is the way of thought of great thinkers. But this way of thought unites as well with the tendency of the masses and, how much more, it unites with a tendency toward a love of actual work that expresses the tendency of an exalted spirit upon which the spirit of God hovers.

When righteous people are to be found in the generation upon which the light of Hashem continuously manifests itself, they unite their souls with the souls of all the people. Then the thought in the inner heart of the masses of human beings who engage in work unites with the thought of the heart of these righteous people.

The aspect of scourge that exists in work comes from the factor of “people’s envy of others” (Ecclesiastes 4:4) and from the factor of people’s hatred of others. That scourge derives significantly from the cursed form of the struggle of life in this degraded world. But that scourge will itself gain wisdom and emerge from the sum total of curse and come to the sum total of blessing.

Sometimes righteous people have the power to bestow the light of holiness upon the essence of work until that work possesses power commensurate with the power of the Torah: leading to the life of the world-to-come, to rectifying blemishes, and to causing those who engage in that work to repent. “Greater is a person who benefits from the toil of his hands than a person who fears heaven” (Berachot 8a).

And just as power exists to draw forth the holiness and inner Divine light within every type of work and to extricate holiness and inner Divine light from the sum total of curse, so too power exists to draw forth the holy light within all languages and within all wisdoms in the world. Great righteous people must pray that the light of the pleasantness of Hashem within all wisdoms and within all languages will be drawn forth in such a way that the honor of Hashem will appear everywhere and the rays of the light of Torah will burst forth everywhere. The prayer of these righteous people and the light of their will make an intense impression that has no end.

In particular, we must direct our prayers to this goal since we see that people today are strongly drawn to languages and sciences, and it is impossible to battle against all these people who turn to them. And when the time and its indications show the need for this, then profound righteous people arise to attain salvation, engaging in secret service.

With the greatness of their soul—their chayah and yechidah [soul levels]—they come and open the blocked conduits to situate the secret of Hashem in His objects of study. And Hashem’s objects of study are everything in the world—in particular, everything that has something in it of rectifying the world.

These righteous people arouse the holiness in every language with the might of Joseph, who incorporated everything into the letter hey [with which the physical world was created] (cf. Sotah 36b), and with the might of the [Divine] speech at Sinai that came to add much, much more light than that.

“The Lord will give speech; the women giving tidings are a vast host” (Psalms 58:12). “This means that each word … is divided into seventy languages” (Shabbat 88b). And so too “Moses explained the Torah well” (cf. Deuteronomy 27:8, Baal Haturim: [“in seventy languages”]). The word “well” means that he found the genuine goodness in every language, the power that pours holy splendor [onto that language]. And then the language is continuously clarified, and “a clear language transforms all the nations so that they will all call in the name of Hashem” (cf. Zephaniah 3:9).

Every type of work will shine with the light of life via the work of holiness. And the more that physical types of work and physical endeavors increase in the land of Israel, the more will work from its foundation emerge from its curse-associated lowliness via the people of Israel.

The more that the influence of the Holy Tongue will grow in the world, and the more the power of the Torah and pure prayer will rise—as they strive to broaden the light of Divine etherealness in the world, to clarify that etherealness and to communicate to human beings, via all ways of communication and via all paths of clarity and explanation, the majesty of its honor—so will the light be increasingly revealed in every language and tongue and in every wisdom and body of knowledge. And, how much more, the light of Hashem will shine upon all matters of aesthetics, beauty and song, the ways of proper this-worldly conduct and the pathways of civility. The light of Hashem will begin to pulse even in women’s adornments and the most modern ways of running a household.

And the thought that connects everything to the good and the upright, to the spirit’s Edenic nature and etherealness, to the love of endeavor and the majesty of trust in the Divine and the supernal love that pours light and life into every soul, will be revealed and visible in all these far branches.

Eternal life and temporal life will connect to each other with a vigorous association. They will receive from each other, and all details of all of the practical and intellectual phenomena in the world will shine with the light of the whole from the supernal light of the light of Torah that shone forth from Abraham, “the father of a multitude of nations” (Genesis 17:4), called Ethan the Ezrahite (Psalms 89:1)—“he who aroused from the east, the one whom righteousness accompanied” (Isaiah 41:2).

“And behold, the glory of the God of Israel comes from the eastern way, and its sound is like the sound of many waters, and the earth shines from His glory” (Ezekiel 43:2). And even the most fallen constituents will rise and be sanctified. “A wellspring from the house of Hashem will come forth and water the Valley of Shittim” (Joel 4:18).

Bind the Torah with Human Wisdom
The inner science and, most of all, its ultimate interiority—the holy science that vitalizes the light of life—does not depend on any other science, because it is a supernal river that emerges from Eden. “It is blessed with water from its own riverbed” (Shabbat 65b, gaonim).
People bind the Torah with ]human[ wisdom not to consummate some lack of strength in the Torah but in order to compose new associations and phenomena.

This creative process of binding the light of Divine spirit, the interiority of the Torah, with the wisdom of human awareness, at the full stature of both of them and with the full, fitting spirit of friendliness of both of them, will engender new souls in the world and will give a new, fresh, and healthy character to life.
From the far parts of Sheol this creative spirit will bring forth great lights to shine with new light, with the light of the righteous, upon all of the world’s residents.

We Must Train Ourselves to Love Others
We must train ourselves to love others—in particular, to love those of superior quality: wise people, strong people, singers and artists, those who work on behalf of the public.

We must recognize the light of goodness amidst the most outstanding people. The light of God spreads in the world through them—whether or not they themselves recognize the importance of their mission.

The Most Honorable Aspect of Every Matter
We must always find the most honorable aspect of every matter. Then the light of the entire world will be revealed in that light’s supernal glory. And the verse will begin to be realized: “He will remove the disgrace of His nation from the entire land” (Isaiah 25:8).

The Light of the Messiah
When the light of the messiah shines in a person’s heart, it teaches him to respect all created beings. “And it will be on that day, the root of Jesse will stand as a banner for nations. Nations will seek him, and his peace will be with honor” (Isaiah 11:10).

The Tongue of the Mute Will Sing
When we see an intensification of torrents of lights from below upward, we must draw forth [energy] from the Forty-Two Letter Name. And when we see streams descending from above downward, we approach the light of the Seventy-Two Letter Name.
The kidah—“cassia”—in the [Temple] incense includes these two phenomena in its letter hey.
That was the might of the High Priest: to exhibit kidah—“bowing on his face.”

But when “Levi demonstrated a kidah, he became lame,” because “he had spoken disrespectfully about God above” (Succah 53a). Still, Levi was “a great, tall (aricha) man” (Shabbat 59b) who drew forth the source of his thoughts from “length (orech) of days” and “length (orech) of face,” and bowing upon his face. He desired the splendor of Israel even in the exile, and so “he taught: [A woman] may go out with a diadem [in the public domain on the Sabbath]” (ibid.).

Those who love Hashem will shine “like the emergence of the sun in its might” (Judges 5:31). “The sun will shine upon such a person” (Genesis 32:31) so that his lameness will be healed. “Then the lame will skip like a hart, and the tongue of the mute will sing” (Isaiah 35:6).

Torah and the Gold of Sheba of the Imagination
As long as we engage in studying Torah and in learning wisdom, in performing deeds of lovingkindness and in civilizing the world with love of people and with propriety, we need not fear any outbreaks of delusions.

The most powerful manifestation of the wealth of the imagination will be transformed into a great light of the gold of Sheba. “[The poor person] will live and [the king] will give him of the gold of Sheba. And [the poor person] will pray on his behalf always; the entire day he will bless him” (Psalms 72:15).

The torrent of lights from below upward will bring forth the light of life without any travail and toil, like the traits of the Holy One, blessed be He, Who created everything with the breath of his mouth. “Just as I made heaven and earth with My word, so you as well” (Zohar I:5a). “I placed My word in your mouth and in the shadow of My hand I covered you, to plant heaven and to establish the earth and to say to Zion, you are My nation” (Isaiah 51:16).

“With Your Righteousness, They Are Exalted”
A person must fear lowliness more than exaltedness. “With Your righteousness, they are exalted” (Psalms 89:17).

The Experience of Supernal Righteous People
The sanctified spiritual sense in its supernal being is so developed in supernal righteous people that they only attain rest when their thought and all of their senses are connected to the Divine light and when their awareness—with its feelings—of the Divine is filled with delight and Edenic pleasures that are more full than every type of this world’s delight—more than the delight of every melody and song, more than the delight of every type of taste and fragrant scent of spices, of “spikenard and saffron, calamus and cinnamon, with all frankincense trees, myrrh and aloes, with all the chief spices” (Song of Songs 4:14).

All that they know, all of their good deeds and all of their good traits, all of their Torah and all of their wisdom, all of their industry and all of their uprightness and justice, all of their might and all of their light of life—in them, all of these are filled with an intellectual and emotional clinging to the Divine, which fills all of their being with the Edenic pleasure of all worlds.
They feel impoverished when a short interval passes during which the Divine Eden does not fill the entire fullness of their lives.

After such an interval, they are elevated with an elevation of modesty and a holy kiss to the light of the Living One of all worlds, with lowliness of spirit, with pure intellect, with purity of might, and with enduring faith.

Supernal rivers of Eden stream and flow through their soul and all blessings are stored in their soul: life and happiness, peace and friendship, wealth and freshness for the entire world, for all creations and for all creatures.
All Torah and ethics, all wisdom and proper behavior—all existence constitutes guidance on how to attain this supernal trait and the supernal aspect in it.

Intellectual and Emotional Edens
The Eden of intellectual awareness has one form, and the Eden of personal feeling has a different form.
The former is great in its quality but is not so deep in penetrating through life, and the latter does not have such a great quality, but it is deep and pervading.
When a person’s soul rises, these two Edens coalesce. There is no end and measure to their wealth and to their full surfeit, to the Eden of their ethereal being and to their clear and purified light.

The Three Stages in Performing a Mitzvah
As a person begins to perform a mitzvah, a great desire comes to him from the archetypal element of wisdom—which provides full awareness within the light of life—to experience the joy of the mitzvah.

Afterwards, this light aligns itself with his body’s limbs of action. Then comes the character of halachah, which possesses strength and life. But this matter must necessarily be encompassed in the boundaries of form expressed in action. Thus, the expansion of the soul is diminished, because the light of spirituality has passed through the conduits of measured characteristics.

But then, once a person has performed the mitzvah, and the Divine light in it has bonded with the life of his body and all of its powers, he is elevated, and supernal love gains strength within him without boundary.

“The blessing [recited] by those in the West, [the land of Israel,] when removing their tefillin—[‘Blessing are You, Hashem…, Who commanded us to guard His laws” (Berachot 44b)]—rises with an elevated height. And the preciousness of a person’s yearning for the light of this supernal love that follows after he has performed the deed of the mitzvah has no equal.

This is a double joy: “goodness of heart due to a profusion of all” (Deuteronomy 28:47). The mitzvah is truly “all,” and “the goodness of heart” that comes from the fulfillment of the person’s supernal spiritual longing refreshes all of life.

Keeping “Delight” from Turning into “Plague”
Service (Avodah), faithfulness (Ne’emanut), might (Gevurah): these are the foundations of “delight” (ONeG) that keep it from turning into “plague” (NeGA).

Representations of the Encompassing
When we speak of matters that encompass all being by making use of specific representations that come from spiritual or physical kernels that we comprehend, that is similar to land surveyors assessing large parcels of land with the aid of a small plumb bob.

The Light of the Torah in Distant Branches of Knowledge
We sometimes find the light of the Torah specifically in a distant place.
When people’s thoughts have shriveled and contracted, and that contraction grows so strong that many fundamental parts of the Torah are removed from the Torah, we must seek them in a distant place.
In general, the distinction between the Torah and non-Torah wisdom is not properly defined.
In order to properly elucidate the Torah, we must be familiar with almost all the sciences. However, we lack elucidation regarding when they were separated from the Torah.

The field of medicine is included in the Torah, as we see from the fact that the Sages inserted it in non-legal Talmudic passages. And the topic of maintaining good health was the essential factor that impelled Rav Huna to direct his son to become a student of Rav Chisda (Shabbat 82a), even more than the incisiveness of Rav Chisda’s halachic rulings.
In Proverbs, we find the praise of wisdom in general.
It may be that the moral corruptions of a few scholars led to the expansion of the idea of the distinction between the Torah and non-Torah wisdom.

In general, all of the sciences lead a person to recognize the Divine and to love God. That being the case, they are included in the command, “Hear O Israel…, you shall love Hashem your God” (Deuteronomy 6:4), regarding which the next verse states, “And these words that I command you today will be upon your heart, and you will teach them to your children” (ibid. 5).

Sometimes, a person must know how to act, but a particular branch of non-Torah wisdom does not suffice for that. The same distinction applies to various fields of knowledge in Torah that are not on a practical level.

And it is clear that one must begin by attaining practical wisdom. Indeed, familiarity with the spirit of the Torah, which comes as a result of learning Torah, elevates a person to be consummately practical.

To an extent, that property exists as well in every branch of knowledge, in certain respects. In fact, every branch of wisdom is the light of Hashem; and the clear parameter of what distinguishes the Torah from general wisdom is a great conundrum.

Practical and Contemplative Service of God
A person must accustom himself not to allow one domain to topple another, because each spiritual branch has its own function.
In particular, this caution must be kept in mind regarding practical ways of service and contemplative ways of service, and regarding their respective teachings.

At the time that a person engages in elevated spiritual teachings, he is not suited for tangible actions and their way of thought. But he must know that there is a practical domain in the world, which is very rich and has many branches, and he must strive so that his spirit will be prepared to absorb the practical side with all its details as well.

Conversely, when a person is connected to practical ways of service and their teachings, he must be aware that there is a supernal, spiritual world, and it is entirely impossible not to be refreshed by its scent.

In the midst of these different tendencies of the spiritual and the practical, a person should arrange a balanced psychological stance, a rich amalgam, so that he will be prepared to engage in Torah learning and in deed in their full senses.

The Ultimate Purpose of All Existence
The ultimate purpose of all existence is the revelation of the light of Hashem at the pinnacle of supernal delight, on such a supernal level of unity that the core being of every spark of life will rise beyond the entirety of that pinnacle.

Then the elevation of all existence will shine inherently in every detail. This is like a mirror: everything that stands before it is illuminated and appears in it. And there is no end to this great happiness.
To that end, existence must initially be separated into the smallest parts. And large ruptures must be made manifest in order to separate these points.
Then these points will be polished and refined. And once that occurs, each will include all being, and everything will be filled with the light of Hashem and His glory.

Seeing God in All Things
“Understanding” is the supernal ideal of how the world must be at the ultimate level of goodness, pleasantness and happiness—not as it is now with its boundaries, straits, and smallness, but with the concept of absolute freedom from every oppression in the world—a full world, a supernal world.
And higher than understanding is “wisdom,” a world prepared to recognize that which is higher than itself.
That [“wisdom”,] which is higher than every recognizable worldly ideal, and [“understanding,” which is] the full worldly ideal in the future—these two are always connected to each other.

And the life of all the worlds and their existence comes about by means of the hidden gaze of the supernal happiness of “wisdom” and “understanding” upon everything, which provides unceasingly the momentum of existence, from its vastest totality to its most precise particulars, and from the purest and brightest ethereal emanation to the most impure and dark materiality. Everything stands ready to rise, to shine, and to unite.

This unitary idea, which is encompassing and supernal, fills the heart of the righteous with greatness and joy. It strengthens and enlivens their spirit to engage in a whole, constant service, and it gives them spiritual strength of peace and honor to make peace with all the tendencies of life and to elevate them, to know how to honor all creatures and to see, from their standpoint, how everything does the will of its Maker.
And out of the supernality of this thought they know how to evince words of the living God from every utterance and from every movement, from every comprehension and from every occurrence.

The light of Torah and wisdom of God illuminates all of their existence from all sides, and within their inner being they honor the God of glory. The splendor of “His glory fills the world” (siddur) and surrounds the world. “From world to world You are God” (siddur), and “the kindness of God exists the entire day” (Psalms 52:3).

Just as [we] must elevate [our] fallen thoughts and traits (in which evil and ugliness may be discerned) to the source of their root in holiness, where we see that they are really exalted thoughts and good traits, so too must [a person] lift up [his] thoughts that are decent but that stand at the lowest level  – where evil and chaos are united with them, even though they face holiness. [He must lift them up] to the most elevated level of the ideal sublime – [a state of being that] is directed only toward total goodness and absolute straightness – until the uplifting [of these decent thoughts] grows and [reaches] the supernal world, over which pure holiness rules in its might.

The insolence (chutzpah) at the time preceding the messiah comes about because the world has progressed to such an extent that it demands an understanding of how every detail is connected to the whole. A detail that is not connected to the great whole cannot satisfy [a person’s] mind. If the world were engaged in [gaining access to] the light of Torah to such a degree that [a person’s] spiritual soul [would] grow to recognize the proper connection between details and spiritual wholeness, then the teshuvah and rectification of the world would be actualized. However, because [people’s] carelessness has led to [a state in which] the light of the inner Torah – which requires [that a person attain] an exalted state and an inherent holiness – has not appeared in the world correctly, the demand [of people for the structure of a life in which the details are understood within the [framework of the] whole has come at a time when the complete revelation of the light and the clearing of the path [leading] to understanding has not yet arrived. And this has caused terrible destruction. We must employ the supernal remedy, which is [the attainment of] increased strength in [our] spiritual ability. Then the common people will, [with their] feeling, directly understand and access a way of comprehending and appraising that which connects all of [their] Torah-[related] knowledge and deeds to the most supernal wholeness. At that point, the strength of spiritual life will again appear in the world, in deed and in thought, and a universal teshuvah will begin to bear its fruit.

The essence of learning Torah for its own sake can come only after [a person] is capable of [gaining] an understanding – accompanied by feeling – of how all of the details of the Torah are beloved and holy, and of how the universal light, which is filled with life and brings life to the world, courses through all of [these] details.

There are various causes of depression. [A person] must overcome all of them with the joy of [performing] a mitzvah. That is a constant joy that suits [the people of] Israel because of the spiritual light that always rests upon them. One cause [of depression] is a tendency,[expressed in] action, for coarse pleasure. A person’s soul is drawn by that to a place of darkness, and [there] it grieves over its descent.[A person] should transform this great woe to joy, for when [his] soul [will] rise from the yoke of exile that had burdened it, a great stream of joy [will] rise up from below, and the sublime, pure [level of reality will] grow ever richer in its spirituality.

(One needs to distinguish and differentiate two levels of Divine Providence governing the world.) God’s guidance [of the universe, as] connected to the moral dimension – whether [in relationship to] individuals or to nations and [other] groups – is all an extension of the nature of universal morality poured into the essence of being. This [guidance is alluded to] by the name Elokim (“God”). However, higher than this stands [God’s] concealed free will, which does not correspond to a revealed moral state. Instead, [it corresponds] to the supernal ideal, which is in consonance with the supernal gaze, transcending the conditions of present day existence. The illuminations that come from this state are the lights of the inner soul of all being. They include the past, present and future, transcending the structure and form of temporal periods. All of this is encompassed in the name “Hashem” as it is structured and in all of the pathways of its permutations.

The rectification of the political state as a whole and the rectification of [each individual’s] body in particular are part of the highest manifestation of holiness – [a manifestation] so holy that it cannot be illuminated in a revealed fashion by means of a characteristic light that has an obviously holy form. Rather, the light is wrapped within [this manifestation of holiness] and [clings] to it like a garment. The noble strands that emerge from these [rectifications are] practical details directed toward the rectification of the state and [of each individual’s physical] health, in the form of Godly commandments. These may be compared to tzitzit. And the culture as a whole may be compared to the tallit. The tzitzit bring forth a holy revelation of all of the light hidden in the entire tallit, with [the light’s] great revelation and manifestation. [Similarly, the] deeds of Godly commandments and holiness that make [their particular] mark in the totality of human action, [deeds] directed toward rectifying [man’s] life – communal and individual –actualize the light hidden in the depths of all the structures of human culture. They bring the revelations [of that light] to the place fit for [the light] and make visible the light of eternal life that gives life to everything, including temporary life.

The nefesh of the sinners of Israel in the era preceding the coming of the Messiah – of those who connect with love to matters concerning the entirety of the Jewish people, the land of Israel and the renaissance of the nation – is more perfected than the nefesh of those fully faithful Jews who lack this quality of an intrinsic sensitivity to the good of the whole and the building of the nation and the land. But the ruach is much more perfected in those who fear God and who keep the Torah and the commandments, even though an intrinsic sensitivity and impulse to act in matters concerning the whole of Israel are not yet as strong in them as they are in those in whom a spirit of transgression fouls their heart to such a degree that they connect themselves to foreign perspectives and to deeds that pollute their physicality and prevent the light of the ruach from being rectified [in them]. As a result, the nefesh [of these sinners] too suffers from their blemishes. The rectification – which will come about via the light of the Messiah [and] which will be greatly aided by the spreading forth of the teaching of the secrets of the Torah and the revelation of the lights of the wisdom of God in all of its forms that are worthy of being revealed – is that Israel will come together in one bond. And [then] the nefesh of those who are [God-]fearing, who keep the Torah, will be rectified by means of the perfected nefesh of the sinners, who are good in regard to matters of the entire [community] and [in regard to] the hopes, material and spiritual, that can be understood by human awareness and sensitivity. And the ruach of the sinners will be rectified by means of the influence of those who fear God, who keep the Torah and who are great in faith. And thus a great light will come to both [groups]. The manifestation of complete teshuvah will come to the world, and then the people of Israel will be prepared for redemption. The supernal tzadikim, the masters of the neshamah, will be the unifying conduits through which the abundant flow of the light of the nefesh will pass from left to right and the abundant flow of the light of the ruach from right to left. And the joy will be very great. “Your priests will don righteousness and Your pious ones will sing joyfully” (Psalms 132:9). And this will be accomplished through the power of the light of the Messiah, who is David himself, who “lifted up the yoke of teshuvah” (Moed Katan 16b). “For the sake of David Your servant, do not reject the face of your anointed one” (Psalms 132:10).

The more a person loves people, the more that one gazes with an approving eye at those who are immersed with all their might in matters of this world and its construction, the more one’s mind becomes settled. If one is capable of turning to the heights, to a supernal spirituality, to Godly perceptions, one will [then] find oneself more at home in his supernal world. The necessary affairs of the world that are incumbent upon humankind [and] that by their nature interfere with the supernal vision will not disturb that person so much, because he or she will know that these are being attended to on his behalf by all of those people who find satisfaction in this practical work of theirs. Ben Zoma said of this: “Blessed is He Who created all of these to serve Me” (Berakhot 58a).

There is no room to ask about the source of a person’s knowledge of supernal information. When we find within the soul a supernal spirit and a treasury of well-arranged knowledge – so that everything is aligned with everything else – [we may know that] this is the pinnacle of clarified [knowledge]. All knowledge that derives from analysis is merely a means of attaining this supernal knowledge, which the soul pours forth from its deepest depths. The most effective means of attaining this supernal trait is clinging to God with all of one’s might and studying the secrets of the Torah.

The light of Israel shows how it is precisely the yearnings that transcend the entire world that give the world life and happiness. Eternity is necessary not only for the sake of eternity but also for the sake of the moment. And the moment is important because it is one of the revelations of eternity. The world is important because it is one form of the infinite numbers of forms through which the light of the Divine Being is revealed.

Sometimes, when there is a need to violate the words of the Torah, and there is no one in the generation capable of showing the way, it occurs through breaching. Nevertheless, it is better for the world if it occurs by way of accidental violation. This is the basis of the principle, "Better they do it by way of accidental violation than by willful violation" (Beitzah 30a). It is only when prophecy dwells upon Israel that it is possible to reform it according to a "horaat shaah" (see Mishneh Torah, Rebels 2:4), and then it would be done in a permitted matter and even a revealed mitzvah. But with the concealing of the light of prophecy, this reform is done by way of a breach, which depresses the heart because of itself, but gladdens the heart because of its goal.

Holy people must truly be natural people, for whom all the qualities of the nature of body and spirit partake of the quality of life and health. And then in their ascent they are able to raise the world – and all will rise with them.
There are very precious things that cannot be revealed except through absence. And we respect those absences, for they inform regarding the very good causes which give rise to their very existence.

A person’s instinct is swifter and more exact than his or her intellectual recognition. A human being’s greatness [lies in the fact] that one can raise all of one’s recognitions to the heights of the most supernal aspect within instinct – from which comes exactitude and swiftness. In regard to a supernal, exalted [state of being], those people who truly possess divine faith have the mightiest instinct. [In this regard,] all culturally-focused people will ultimately return to them. [But] in terms of intermediary goals – such as yearning for morality, knowledge, the building up and honor of the [Jewish] nation, and so forth – culturally focused people have the strongest instinct. Everyone who has a strong instinct [in some matter] is weak in those [other] matters that require [him to engage in] calculation and deliberation. Therefore the [various] strata of the [Jewish] nation must be bound together so that they will receive illumination of knowledge and strength of instinct from each other, in accordance with the level of the particulars of how these portions are divided among them.
In my youth, I would sense a stench of excrement from the prayer houses of the nations, even though they were seemingly very clean and stood in the midst of a garden of planted trees.

Just as supernal holy people have no connection to mundane and trivial concerns, and [their] trait of holiness is beyond any [this-worldly] purpose, so that it goes without saying that [a holy person] eats in order to learn [Torah], pray, perform mitsvoth and the like-this being an intermediate trait –  [furthermore,] the essence of [the holy person’s] eating and similarly [that person’s] speech and all of the movements and emotions of life are filled with holiness and light. And how much more is it the case that for these people all wisdoms in the world – whether deep or superficial, pure or impure – have an intrinsic [upward] direction, and everything that enters into the circle of their awareness rises as they rise. It is true that, in practical terms, no one reaches this level, for the Torah has set eternal boundaries [barring certain behaviors] for everyone. But in regard to that which pertains to [the realm of] thought, “boundaries are no higher than ten [handbreadths]” (Shabbat 43a), “there is no Satan and no evil occurrence” (I Kings 5:18), and “even the Angel of Death teaches [such a person]” (Shabbat 89a).

In the days preceding the coming of the Messiah, whoever connects in the inclination of one’s heart to the salvation of Israel possesses the soul of a supernal holy person, which cannot be gauged with the measure [meant] for an intermediary [person].

Torah sages are perfected by means of the unlearned masses – for even though the light of the Torah constitutes the life of all [people], nevertheless it is also “a drug of death for those who turn leftward with it” (cf. Shabbat 88b), and it reduces the strength [of sages] much more than if they had been lacking Torah and [only] simple nature had acted upon them in the pathways of their lives. And since all people have a component of ugliness, however small, the Torah indeed becomes harmful to them corresponding to this component. And in this area – the harm is incomparably stronger than the reward. And the counter-remedy to the drug of death blended into the Torah sages is activated by the general connection that they have with the unlearned masses of the entire [Jewish] nation, for in this way the latter pour forth the influence of [their] natural straightness, which has not been at all degraded by means of any sophistry. [Then] the small drop of the drug of death turns back again into a drug of life. And in this way it also gives life to the entire people, including among them the unlearned masses.

[Regarding] the impurities in [people’s] understanding of divinity, awe, faith, and everything dependent upon these – as long as the nation as a whole has no need to rectify the ways of its practical life, the damage [that these impurities cause] is imperceptible. But since the time has come that the national revival must arrive, and the blossoming of the “horn of salvation” in actuality must be revealed, [these] impurities immediately create an obstacle. The nation can only bond together, and, in the depths of its life, understand the secret of its might and the images of its structures by means of purified perceptions and actions that emerge with the highest clarity from [people’s] pure, true knowledge of God. This is why a great negative force is aroused [at the time] preceding the coming of the Messiah, [a force characterized by] great insolence. That negativity will burn away all that is weak and ugly in Godly concepts and [all] that depends upon [those concepts], in the whole of the nation. Even though this is terrible to see – because a number of matters of truth, good traits, commandments, and laws seem to be swept away by the stream of negativity –  nevertheless, everything will ultimately blossom in purity and might with exalted holiness from the seed that is powerful, pure, and exalted, which no negativity will [be able to] reach. Its light will shine as a new light on Zion, with a wondrous greatness beyond any image that the impoverished powers of weary souls – [suffering from] material and spiritual weakness resulting from the long and debilitating exile – can visualize.

When the light of divine inspiration begins to manifest, even if only in the imagination, one hears [in it] the joyful voice of all of Torah and ethics; one senses in it the refinement of all beauty and the clarity and certainty of all wisdom. [From its] general, latent form, its vision then expands into letters and words, sentences and principles, then into teachings and ideas, according to the extent of one's skill, effort, and toil in Torah.

It is not a far-fetched concept that everything connected to a person in any way—his food and drink, his belongings and movements, all of his possessions—bears an essential relationship to his inner essence. The past, present, and future do not differ in this regard. In all things, there is a revelation of being, and every being is, in some way, alive and contains some aspect of consciousness. We are surrounded by life on all sides. In our elevation, everything is elevated, and in our degradation, all things are degraded. When our essential self is elevated, all the manifestations of our life are elevated as well. The more authentic this elevation is, the more broadly it extends, reaching even the most distantly connected sensations. And the elevation toward Godliness, according to the degree of its revelation, elevates everything that is connected to us, in the most expansive sense possible.

The core of our knowledge of the Divine is this: One, Creator, Commander. The entire treasury of spirituality comes only to provide explanations and clear descriptions of how to understand this knowledge, to clarify it, and to elevate it in a form that is at once most ideal, noble, intelligent, practical, simple, and sublime.

I love all. I cannot but love all people, all nations. From the very depths of [my] heart, I want the glory of all, the perfection of all. My love for Israel burns more greatly and is deeper, but [this] inner desire spreads out in the force of its love to all, literally. I have no need whatsoever to force this feeling of love – it wells directly from the holy depth of wisdom of the Godly soul.

No accident is it, but rather the very nature of my soul, that I feel pleasure and peace of mind when I involve myself in Divine mystical matters expansively and freely. It is my main purpose. All other purposes of my various other aptitudes, whether they be practical or intellectual, are but secondary to my essence. I have to find my happiness within me, not in the approval of other people, nor in any career whatsoever. The more I know myself, and the more I allow myself to be original and stand on my own two feet, from my self-awareness, merged with knowledge, consciousness, feeling and poetry, the more the light of God will shine on me, and the more my ability to be a blessing to me and the world will develop.

By its fundamental nature, [a person’s] consciousness of God flees a blemished, splintered and incomplete life for a life that is whole, outstanding, and full, even in this world. One spark of the light of God that lives in a person’s heart suffices to expel infinite instances of darkness. Those who say that the knowledge of God diminishes the character of life are fools without understanding who are standing on the outside. And a nation that knows its God must appear in the world with the knowledge of the on-going perfection of life in light of the living God.

A great soul finds it difficult at times to constrain itself to do any one particular form of [divine] service, or any kind of finite intellection or study, for it is constantly occupied with [supernal] images whose endless streams cease not, even for an instant.  These include various different matters, and exalted, yet hidden longings, about which even a person who thinks deeply will be unable to grasp them by nature of their depth and brilliance

Personal understanding of divinity can be encapsulated in zeir anpin (reduced size) [which concentrates one’s views of] God as unique, the Creator of all, [Who has made] the world and all beings with the work of His hands. But this understanding is small, and there exists arikh anpin (a broader state) [of comprehension that is] much greater than this, and that incorporates everything into a supernal and wondrous unity, exceedingly higher than the above mentioned personal thought.

When a person sins, that person is in the world of separation. At that point, every element stands alone. Evil is evil in itself, with an evil and harmful quality. [But] when a person does teshuvah out of love, the light of the existence of the world of unification – where everything is organized into a single unit – immediately shines upon that person. And in [that] universal connectedness there is no evil at all, for the evil combines with the good in order to season it and elevate its precious worth even more. And with this, “willful sins are transformed into merits” (Yoma 86b) – literally.

If the new science [of our day] boasts of having freed itself from theology, it must be known that on the other hand, theology has now been freed from the sciences, which are bound in human cables. And as a matter of course, the term "new" must apply to supernal matters, not to things which humans create, but rather "the term 'new' is that which God Himself bestows (Isaiah 62:2)". The theology newly freed from being bound to the sciences is Prophecy, the unique [inheritance] of Israel, which shall soon be revealed to us.

The insolence (chutzpah) at the time preceding the Messiah is [the expression of] a diminution of light, which has the purpose of rectifying the vessels. It is not at all similar to other, [previous] instances of criminality, which were entirely empty, [acting] in a destructive manner. However, within this camp of the insolent there are also sparks that must be entirely extinguished. And that extinguishing will come about as a result of a great illumination of the light of the Torah from supernal might, by means of the appearance of very great tzadikim. “The light of the righteous will rejoice, and the candle of the wicked will be extinguished” (Proverbs 13:9).

Without the insolence preceding the Messiah, it would be impossible to explain secrets of the Torah with an absolute revelation. Only due to the coarsening of feelings that results from this insolence (chutzpah) is it possible to receive very exalted intellectual lights. And in the end, everything will return to [a state of] complete rectification.

The feeling of love must develop in all of its details so that it will display all of its treasures of intellectual, emotional, and imaginative vitality. Then the treasury of God will rise to the heavenly love that is associated with the name of HashemGod. Similarly, the aesthetic sense must overall be so well developed that the soul can gird itself with the image of heavenly beauty, such that it will be able to stand at its highest levels. The literature of the [present] generation and the desire for the expansion of beauty that has taken hold of [the generation] – even though these tend toward mundane matters and are at times extremely polluted – are nothing else than preparatory levels for the supernal purity of the exalted glory that will appear in the world.

To provide a contrast to those studious people who are scrupulous about constant perseverance [in Torah learning], it is necessary that a faculty be found that shows how the free, inner light may be revealed through [a person’s] perambulations and tranquility, [which provide] a breadth of mind through which [one’s] soul rises, soaring in “a vehicle that flies through the air” (Sanhedrin 106b), where it looks for all of its desires, seeks its refined concepts – seeks and finds them.
